title: Private household
context: Evaluate the following statements on private household:
statements: A person living alone in an apartment counts as a private household.
Only families with children are considered private households.
Several students living together in a shared apartment form a private household.
Every private household has a variety of needs every day.
If you live alone, you are not part of the economy because a household needs at least two people.
tactical_explanations:
Living alone does not change the status. This includes a person living alone in an apartment or in a house, explicitly as a private household, just like a family or a shared apartment. The economic unit in which daily needs occur is not the number of housemates.

Even those who eat breakfast alone, heat and drive to work, thus remain part of the economy.

The statement is true.

Children are not a ticket to the household concept. A family of four is considered a private household, but also a single person and student in a shared apartment. The common parent is the daily bundle of needs, not a certain relationship. The restriction to families with children is therefore too narrow and wrong.

The statement is false.

Several students under one roof are no exception to the household concept. If they live together in a shared apartment, they are considered a private household, analogous to the family in the house and to the single person. Shared rent, kitchen and everyday life make them a unit with common and individual needs for food, warmth, education and mobility.

This is exactly what private households mean.

The statement is true.

Food, housing, warmth, security, sleep, personal care, education and mobility are only examples. It is noted that every private household, regardless of its composition, has a variety of such needs every day. Some of them can be breast-feeded without buying, many can be satisfied with products and services.

The daily diversity of needs is therefore the common starting point for all households, not a special case for large families.

The statement is true.

Economy does not begin with a couple relationship or when a company is founded. Every person is part of a private household, whether alone, in partnership, family or community. The person living alone has the same basic needs as other households: food, housing, warmth, security, personal care, education, mobility.

Many of these needs are met by products and services that he does not create himself but asks for in companies. Thus, the minimum size of two people is not in theory; it would artificially define single people out of the economy, even though they need or want goods daily.

The statement is false.

title: Goods as products and services
context: Evaluate the following statements on goods:
statements: Products such as bread or a bicycle and services such as a haircut are called common goods.
Goods are only physical products; services do not include them.
Treatment by a doctor and advice from a bank employee are services that can meet needs.
Every need needs a product or service, otherwise it will remain unfulfilled.
Goods are produced and offered, as well as in demand and purchased so that people's needs can be met.
tactical_explanations:
Bread, pastries, soap, toothbrush, car, fuel and energy are called products; haircut, medical treatment, banking advice or a coaching session as services. Both groups are explicitly called goods. The collective term covers not only tangible things, but also services that someone provides for others.

If you see only the goods, half of what households ask every day is undercut.

The statement is true.

To only carry physical things as goods is contrary to the definition. Products and services are collectively called goods because both needs can be met: the bicycle as well as the repair, the bread as well as the doctor's visit.

To remove services from the concept of goods would make the demand for treatment, advice, cutting and training invisible. Precisely these services, however, create the economy in addition to the products.

The statement is false.

Banking advice and medical treatment are theoretically necessary or at least helpful for meeting health or financial orientation needs. They are not physical products such as bread, soap or a bicycle, but are among the goods because households ask them and practices or banks offer them.

The benefits arise in the execution of the performance, not only by the possession of an object. Whoever only lets tangible goods be considered goods, exactly these everyday services are removed from the economy, although they are combined with products in one term.

The statement is true.

Sleep, proximity or conversation can satisfy needs without someone buying a product or booking a service. Of course: not every need needs a product or service to meet, even if that is true for many needs. Food, care, mobility or medical assistance often run over goods, but other needs do not.

The absolute claim that every need can only be fulfilled through the market overshadows the book statement.

The statement is false.

Supply and demand are combined. Goods are produced and offered on the one hand, and demand and purchase on the other, so that numerous needs can be met. Without creation there would be nothing to buy; without demand from households and other companies there would be no reason to provide bicycles, repairs or pastries in the known form.

This interplay is a first essential feature of the economy.

The statement is true.

title: Households and non-residential production
context: Evaluate the following statements Who is responsible for the production of goods:
statements: Private owners can produce all the goods they need and want, even in the necessary quality and time.
In most cases, people lack the skills and skills they need, as well as the necessary production conditions and means of production.
Therefore, many products and services are produced by companies.
Only companies have needs; private householders never ask for goods.
A first essential feature of the economy is that there are products such as bicycles and services such as repairs.
tactical_explanations:
Self-bread on Sunday does not refute the basic line. People could not produce the goods they need and wish for, even in the necessary quality and in the time available. This would be too difficult or impossible because skills, skills, production conditions and means of production are in most cases lacking.

The absolute claim that households covered all the needs themselves, ignores precisely this limit and the role of companies.

The statement is false.

Skills rarely suffice for anything in everyday life. Anyone who wants to have a car, electricity, toothbrush or bank advice in a usable form needs machines, knowledge, rooms and intermediate services that typically do not bundle a single household.

The lack of skills and skills, as well as the lack of production conditions and means of production are mentioned as the reason why self-sufficiency in quality and time is failing. Therefore, it is too difficult or impossible to create all goods by itself.

It follows that companies take on these tasks very often, not the claim that each household can meet all needs alone.

The statement is true.

Companies are jumping into this gap. Construction companies, carpentry, bakeries, boutiques or broadcasting companies produce for others and create services that households and other businesses need or want. Because self-production is often impossible or too difficult, these tasks are often taken over by companies.

The household remains a demander, the company a provider; both belong to the economy.

The statement is true.

The image is distorted by the demand side. Every private household has daily needs for food, housing, heat, education or mobility and often asks for goods. Companies recognize these needs and offer what households or other companies need.

So needs are on both sides: in the household as a starting point, in the company as an opportunity to obtain intermediate consumption and to create value for customers.

The statement is false.

Bicycles and repairs are a pair. It is a first essential feature of the economy that there are products such as bicycles and services such as repairs. Both hot goods, both are produced and produced and offered, both are requested and purchased to meet needs.

Anyone who only accepts the goods or only the service fails to fulfil this feature.

The statement is true.

title: Business and customer needs
context: Evaluate the following statements on the role of enterprises:
statements: Companies such as a bakery, a carpentry shop or a construction company produce for others and create services.
Companies only recognise the needs of households and never of other companies.
By offering what customers need or want, companies create value and benefits.
Private owners do not buy goods because only companies are allowed to trade with each other.
A boutique or a broadcasting company is also one of the companies that produce for others.
tactical_explanations:
Bakery, joinery and construction companies are the theory of companies that do not primarily produce for their own refrigerators, but for others. They produce products and services that ask for private households or other companies. This is precisely the difference between household and household that does not produce many goods themselves.

For others-producing is the short answer to the question of what companies are.

The statement is true.

To name households as addressees only, the sentence is not allowed. Companies recognize the needs of private households and/or other companies and offer what they need or want. Flour for the bakery, components for the joinery or broadcasts for a broadcasting company are such operational needs.

Those who strike the second group of addressees understand customer orientation only half.

The statement is false.

Value does not arise from production for its own sake. When a company recognizes needs and responds to them with an offer, it creates value and benefits for customers. This can solve a problem, close a gap, facilitate work or make life more pleasant.

Without this reference to the needs of the other party, the performance remains an effort without the added value described in theory.

The statement is true.

Households are on the demand side. Goods are in demand and bought so that needs can be met; bread, energy, a doctor's visit or a trainer's lesson are everyday examples. A ban on only companies acting with each other does not occur.

It would remove the private household from the economy, although every person is part of such a household and has daily needs, which are often met by products and services. Buying and demand of households belong to the first characteristic of the economy, not to a special right of companies among themselves.

The statement is false.

The list of examples is open. Besides construction, carpentry and bakery are explicitly mentioned a boutique and a broadcasting company as well as many, many more. All produce for others and create services. The legal form or the industry does not change anything in this basic role: anyone who recognizes needs and offers goods acts as a company within the meaning of the section.

The statement is true.

title: Bakery in the morning
context: A Viennese bakery sells pastries to households and obtains flour from a mill. Rate the following statements:
statements: The pastry is a product, a later haircut at the hairdresser a service; both are goods.
The need for sleep can only be met if the household buys a sleeping product.
The bakery as a company can have needs for itself, for example, according to flour of another company.
The purchase of bread meets a need for food by asking for and buying the good.
Because the bakery is a company, it has no own needs.
tactical_explanations:
Pastry is on the product side, the haircut on the service side. As an example, bread and pastries as well as the haircut are typical examples and include both among goods. In the morning, the household buys one, and later perhaps the other; economically, both belong in the same process of supply and demand.

The distinction between product and service remains meaningful, the generic term goods applies to both.

The statement is true.

Sleep does not need a ticket from the market. This includes sleep as a daily requirement, while stressing that not every need for a product or service is needed. A pillow can help, but it is not mandatory to buy. The claim that sleep exists only via a sleep product, makes a possible help a false necessity.

The statement is false.

Flour connects two companies. The bakery not only recognizes the need for food in private households, it needs inputs itself: flour, energy, rooms, appliances. It is explicitly true that companies recognize the needs of private households and/or other companies and offer what they need or want.

The mill thus creates a good for the bakery, the bakery creates pastries for households. Value and benefits arise on both levels, not only at the shop counter. Anyone who agrees with the bakery's own needs because it is a company cuts precisely this chain.

The statement is true.

Food is one of the aforementioned household needs, bread and pastries one of the mentioned products. The way to fulfilment here is through production and supply of the bakery as well as demand and purchase of the household. This pattern is exactly as a characteristic of the economy: goods are created so that numerous needs can be met.

The bread-shop in the morning is the simple everyday case.

The statement is true.

The status of a bakery without flour, energy or working ovens cannot offer anything. The needs of other companies are explicitly stated in theory; the bakery is on both sides, as a supplier to households and as a demander to the mill.

The formula, only households would have needs, but companies would not, does not stand up to the description.

The statement is false.

title: Bicycles suitable for children
context: Parents are looking for a child-friendly bike; a company develops wheels that fit the anatomy of children. Rate the following statements:
statements: Parents may need to buy suitable bicycles for their children and companies can respond with an offer.
A successful company does not need a thoughtful idea for product or service as long as anything is manufactured.
A well thought-out idea meets a need, solves a problem or closes a gap, thus creating added value and benefits.
Only public limited companies may orient themselves to customer needs; a limited company may not.
The idea of a company can arise from a need in the own private household of the founders.
tactical_explanations:
Parents who like to ride a bike can have the need to buy well-suited bikes for their children. This is precisely the need for a child-friendly bike that companies can recognize and answer with their offer, for example by adapting components to the anatomy of children.

This is typical of the normal case of customer orientation: the private household has a need that produces and offers companies for it. Child-friendly geometry is not an extra to the product, but the answer to the perceived needs. This creates the described benefit for customers, here for children and parents at the same time.

The statement is true.

Making something is not enough. A successful company is based on a well thought-out idea for a product or service that meets a need and thus has added value and benefits for the customers. Production without this reference remains employment; it does not create the value described in theory.

The thoughtful idea is the bridge between household needs and supply, not a decorative side work.

The statement is false.

The idea is to meet a need and solve a problem, close a gap, make work easier or make life more pleasant. This results in benefits for customers. The children-friendly wheels that take anatomy and safety seriously are just as close to the wheels that would be only smaller adult models.

The statement is true.

Customer orientation is not dependent on the share. As an example, a GmbH that offers bicycles suitable for children is explicitly named and also counts bakery, boutique or broadcasting company, without making a legal form a condition. Anyone who recognizes needs and offers goods acts as a company.

The claim that only public limited companies are likely to be customer-oriented does not stand and is wrong.

The statement is false.

Searching for a home can be the start. The foundation in the example is based on the search for the right bike for your own children: a need in the private household of the founders becomes a business and product idea. This does not change the fact that many other households can have the same need later on.

The origin of the day-to-day life explains why the idea starts at the demand, instead of a commodity without addressees.

The statement is true.

Energy, toothbrush, mobility, medical treatment or a haircut remain typical requests, even if baked on Sunday.

statements: The families who shop at Novak are private households; the bakery is a company that produces for others.
Bread is a product and delivery is a service; both are among the goods.
Because Novak runs a company, he does not own a private household.

In the bakery two rolls stand side by side. The buying families live together and have daily needs for food; are called exactly such living communities private households. Novak's plant recognizes this need and bakes for customers, not only for their own needs.

A bakery is thus the example of a company that produces for others and produces services.

Products such as bread and pastries are to be separated from services such as a delivery, a haircut or a trainer's lesson, but both groups are to be considered goods. Novak creates the physical pastries and additionally the performance to bring it to the door.

Anyone who only leaves bread as good and excludes delivery narrows the concept that the chapter explicitly covers. The separation of product against service remains meaningful, the common bracket Good as well.

Novak bakes for others during the day, but in the evenings he needs food, home, warmth and personal care and then stands on the same side as his customers.

The statement is false.

The needs of the people in the household arise, not only because of the origin of the goods. Food remains a daily need, regardless of whether the bread is produced in the own kitchen or in a bakery. Just because many households do not bake bread themselves, they buy it as a good from companies. The origin of the goods does not eliminate the need.

The statement is false.

People could not produce the goods they need and wish for themselves in the necessary quality and time. Often skills, skills, production conditions and means of production are lacking. Therefore, companies such as bakeries often take on these tasks.

The sentence is precisely this frequent takeover by companies without claiming that households would never bake themselves.

The statement is true.

Fabian does not produce the table for his own use, but for Petra's family and thus creates benefits. The distribution of roles on behalf is thus the basic distinction of the section, not a special legal form.

Repairs are only the clear example of service in the chapter, alongside bicycles as a product, not the only permissible form. In addition, the treatment by a doctor, the advice by a bank employee, a haircut and a trainer's lesson are available.

Fabian also provides a service for others, separately from the product table, with the delivery to the apartment. The word only makes an example of an exclusivity that does not bear the representation. Anyone who cuts deliveries from the services confuses illustration and definition.

The statement is false.

Companies recognize the needs of private households and offer what they need or want. Petra's family wants a suitable table; Fabian responds with manufacturing and delivery. This is exactly the core business action: an idea for a product or service that solves a problem and provides benefits.

The statement is true.

Every private household has many needs every day, such as food, warmth, safety, sleep, personal care, education and mobility. A purchased table covers one of them, but leaves the rest. The chapter emphasizes the variety, not the unique saturation, of a single good.

The absolute claim that payment would cover all needs does not hold the scene. In the evening the family needs more food, sleep and warmth.

The statement is false.

The chapter includes food, housing, warmth and security, sleep, personal care, education and mobility. Sleep and safety are the everyday needs of every private household, not special cases. They do not always have to trigger a good, but belong to the daily variety. The sentence correctly reflects the examples.

Only living groups with at least four persons are considered private households.
Households could always produce all the goods they need and want themselves in the necessary quality and time.
The boutique is a company that produces or creates services for others and is oriented towards customer needs.
All three types of housing are common that they have a variety of needs every day.
tactical_explanations:
A person living alone in an apartment or in a house is considered as a private householder as a family or a flat. The family status as a pensioner does not change the definition. It has the same everyday needs for food, housing, warmth and security. Living alone does not take anyone out of the economy, it only makes the household smaller.

The statement is true.

The four-person family is an example, not a lower limit. The family, the WG and the single person are explicitly the same. A minimum head count of four would push the pensioner and many couples out of the term, although the representation includes them. Only plus number turns an illustration into a wrong rule.

In the apartment house two of the three types of housing would not be households, which contradicts the chapter.

The statement is false.

People could not produce the goods they need and wish for themselves because it would be too difficult or impossible. In most cases, the necessary skills and skills as well as the production conditions and means of production are lacking. Therefore, companies often take on these tasks.

Always making the same sentence covers the opposite of what the chapter describes as the first characteristic of the economy: goods are produced by businesses and demanded by households. The boutique on the ground floor exists precisely for this reason.

The statement is false.

The boutique is in theory in a series of construction companies, joinery, bakery and broadcasting companies. All these companies produce for others, recognize needs and offer what customers need or want. On the ground floor of the house, the boutique fulfils this role in relation to the households above.

The sentence follows the definition and does not require delivery to other companies, although this would be permissible.

The statement is true.

What is common to all private households is the daily variety of needs. Family, flat and single persons differ in size, not in this quality. Food, apartment, warmth, security and the other points of the list arise independently of the family type. The common parent of the chapter is precisely this diversity of needs.

The statement is true.

title: Supply, demand and the term good
context: In a small town there is a bakery, bicycle workshop and doctor's office. Evaluate the following statements on the topic of goods, needs and the role of companies:
statements: Goods are only in demand and bought; production and offering are not part of the economy.
Bicycles are products, repairs services; both are called goods.
Companies are responsible for the production of many goods, because households often have no skills or means of production for them.
A company that only supplies to other companies does not recognise needs because needs arise exclusively in households.
Not every need needs a product or service to fulfill it.
tactical_explanations:
A first essential feature of the economy is that products and services exist and bear the same name goods. They are produced and offered on the one hand and are in demand and bought to meet needs. The bakery, workshop and practice are on the supply side; households ask for it.

Only demand without creation cuts half of the mechanism. Without offering, the mentioned enterprises in the small town would not be at all as economic actors in the sense of this chapter.

The statement is false.

The chapter is currently choosing bicycles as a product example and repairs as a service example. It is then said that products and services are also called goods. The workshop, which repairs a wheel, thus creates a good in the wider sense, even if nothing new rolls out of the factory hall. The double designation is intentional, not negligence.

The statement is true.

Households could not produce the goods needed themselves in the necessary quality or time, which would be too difficult or impossible because in most cases skills, skills, production conditions and means of production are lacking. Therefore, these tasks are often taken over by companies.

Baker, mechanic and doctor are exactly such takeovers, not exceptions to the teaching set. Often, this does not always mean, but the basic mechanism remains.

The statement is true.

Households and/or other companies are the responsibility of the company. The needs of other companies are therefore planned, for example according to the input, tools or minutes of broadcasting of a broadcasting company. Those who supply exclusively to companies nevertheless recognize the needs, only operational.

The workshop can repair wheels from households and repair the company car at the same time as a bakery.

The statement is false.

The presentation clearly separates: Not every need needs a product or service to be fulfilled, but for many it is true. Sleep, a conversation or security in the near environment can succeed without purchase; bread, toothbrush or a doctor's treatment often does not. The small town illustrates the second group, the first does not refute.

The sentence indicates the limitation of the definition.

The statement is true.

title: Zwei Rollen in einer Person
context: Mrs. Berger runs a small construction company and lives alone in an apartment. In the evening she sleeps without buying a service. Rate the following statements on the subject of belonging to the economy:
statements: Each person is part of a private household, whether he lives alone, in a partnership or in a family.
Students in a shared apartment are not considered private households because they are still in education.
As a single person, Mrs Berger belongs to a private household and at the same time runs a company that produces for others.
Sleep is a need that must always be fulfilled by buying a service.
A construction company creates value and benefits for customers as soon as it recognizes their needs and offers suitable services.
tactical_explanations:
The first sentence of the section is clear: every person is part of a private household, whether he lives alone or in a partnership or family. The way of life changes, the belonging does not. Mrs. Berger alone in the apartment falls under the same rule as a couple or a family with children.

The economy does not begin with the company, but with this household.

The statement is true.

A few students living together in a shared apartment are expressly considered private household. The educational status is not an exclusion criterion. They have the same daily needs for housing, food, education and mobility. The claim that training keeps them outside contradicts the example in theory.

Mrs Berger's single-parenting does not change this WG rule, both forms count.

The statement is false.

The construction company is responsible for the second role in creating services for others. The chapter mentions construction companies, especially among the companies that produce for customers. The same person can be household and during the day companies, without any role canceling the other.

The scene around Frau Berger is exactly this double that applies to a baker or a boutique owner.

The statement is true.

Sleep is in the list of needs, and at the same time it is true that not every need needs a product or service. Mrs. Berger fills sleep by resting in her own apartment without buying a coaching lesson, an overnight stay at the hotel or another paid service.

Always plus purchase act makes a possible tool a duty that denies the presentation. A mattress can help, but does not have to be bought so that sleep is a need at all. The need remains, the market pressure does not. This distinction separates 1.1 from a pure purchase list.

The statement is false.

Companies recognize the needs of households and/or other companies and offer what they need or want. They create value and benefits. A construction company that provides housing or renovation follows this pattern. Success depends on the thoughtful idea that solves a problem, not just on the sign above the door.

The statement is true.

title: Budget tasks
context: Evaluate the following statements on the division of labour within households:
statements: Within households, many different tasks are shared between several people, who can then concentrate on specific tasks.
The division of labour is exclusively found in factories and never in private households.
In the household, one person can mainly take over the food preparation, while another is responsible for cleaning the bathroom.
Those who take on a role in the budget must also do all other budgetary work to the same extent.
Persons in the household may be responsible for certain tasks.
tactical_explanations:
Cooking, cleaning, shopping and care are not a single package. The theory describes the division of labour within households so that the many different tasks are divided between several people. Whoever is responsible for a task can focus on it instead of doing everything at the same time.

This very internal division is a level where division of labour and specialisation take place in a modern economy, alongside the later level in enterprises. Without such roles, everyday life would remain an undifferentiated bundle; with them, a discernible division of competence becomes out of living together.

The statement is true.

Factory halls are not the only place. Households and companies are considered side by side: tasks are shared in homes and houses. One person cooks, another one cleans the bathroom. The claim that division of labor only begins on the assembly line, scrapes the household side, which the section explicitly mentions.

The statement is false.

Food preparation and bathroom cleaning are an everyday example. It is not true that every family has to split exactly as it is, but shows how responsibility for individual tasks can look. One person mainly takes care of cooking, the other is responsible for the bathroom.

Thus, the general rule of internal division of labour becomes tangible without the household being declared a factory.

The statement is true.

Responsibility for a task is concentration, not the duty to manage the entire household at the same time. Whoever cooks mainly is not automatically responsible for any other work to the same extent.

The absolute requirement to do all tasks in parallel to the same extent, cancels the division described above and contradicts the point that individuals can concentrate on certain tasks.

The statement is false.

Responsibility and concentration are common. Once tasks are shared among several persons, individuals can be responsible for certain tasks and engage in them. This is formulated in parallel for households and companies. Without such responsibility, the division would remain a mere mess without clear roles.

The statement is true.

title: Divisions in the company
context: Evaluate the following statements on the division of labour within enterprises:
statements: In enterprises there are usually departments dedicated to specific operational areas and functions.
Purchasing, production, sales (distribution), marketing and accounting are examples of such departments.
Within an enterprise, tasks must never be divided between several persons.
Employees can be responsible for certain tasks and concentrate on them.
The department is exclusively sales; purchasing and accounting are not part of it.
tactical_explanations:
Operational organization does not mean chaos at a desk. It is noted that in companies there are usually departments that devote themselves to specific areas and functions. Purchasing is something other than accounting, production something other than marketing.

This internal structure is the operational form of division of labour, parallel to the division of tasks in the household. Typically, not every micro-enterprise necessarily carries each sign; the pattern remains the functional separation.

The statement is true.

The series of examples is deliberately broad. Purchasing, production, sales and sales, marketing, accounting and other functions are typical departments. None of these are mere accessories: each grouping tasks on which people can concentrate. Anyone who knows only one of these jobs has only half seen the division of work in the company.

The "usw.-" at the end of the list shows that other functions can have the same meaning without repressing the examples mentioned.

The statement is true.

Never allow internal division, turns the section around. Especially within the companies, the many different tasks are distributed among several persons. Divisions exist because not every person is supposed to do everything at the same time. A ban on in-house division would make the described organization impossible.

The statement is false.

The responsibility lies with the core of internal specialisation. Employees are responsible for certain tasks and can concentrate on them instead of representing the entire company in one person. That is exactly how the division of labour within the companies is.

Concentration does not replace quality assurance with other bodies, it makes depth possible in one function.

Without such roles, purchasing, production and distribution remained the same undifferentiated activity. The department is the organizational framework for the responsibility to be tied to persons.

The statement is true.

Sales is an example, not the only department that is permitted. Purchasing, production, marketing and accounting are expressly in addition. The restriction on sales cancels functions without which an enterprise could neither obtain any input nor produce figures.

The list in theory is open and ends with "usw.

The statement is false.

title: Many goods in certain quality
context: Evaluate the following statements What specialization means for the supply of enterprises:
statements: Specialization prevents a baker from offering a wide variety of bread and pastries in a suitable quality.
Specialization and the corresponding organization of enterprises can offer a large number of goods in certain quality.
A car manufacturer produces many cars, a hairdresser takes many different haircuts and treatments daily.
It only depends on the quantity; a certain quality does not matter in this context.
The wide variety of occupations shows the high degree of division of labour and specialization in our economy.
tactical_explanations:
The baker is the counter-example. Precisely because the company and employees specialize in bread and pastries and organize the process, the well-known variety in certain quality is created, not despite the specialization, but through them.

Those who read specialization as a ban on variety are confused with the obligation to bake only one piece.

The statement is false.

Two levers work together: the specialisation of employees in certain products or services and the appropriate organization of the company. This does not follow poverty in the assortment, but the ability to offer a large number of goods in certain quality. Quantity without any quality concept would be a different argument; the theory links both.

Organization means that processes, responsibilities and skills are bundled in such a way that the company can deliver in a repeatable manner. Without this internal order, specialization would remain a label without a supply power. With it, the focus on a field becomes the observable breadth of bread, cars or treatments.

The statement is true.

Three pictures, the same logic. The baker with many breads and pastries, the car manufacturer with many cars, the hairdresser with many cuts and treatments: each one a specialized company that does not provide a single piece, but a large number or variety in certain quality. Services are included, not only physical products.

The statement is true.

"In certain quality" is the same sentence as the large number of goods. The volume alone is not enough to give the book. A bunch of failed loaves or incorrectly painted cars would not be what specialization and organization should do here. To remove quality from the context shortens the sentence inadmissible.

The statement is false.

Not only companies, but also professional profiles are specialized. The wide variety of occupations that can be taken up is considered as a sign of the high degree of division of labour and specialization. Anyone who sees only machines and no professions, overlooks this social side of the same development.

The diversity of occupations arises because people and businesses do not do everything at the same time, but train fields. This is the same logic as in the company, only at the level of employment overall. The section presents this indication directly next to bakers, autoworks and hairdressers.

The statement is true.

title: Internal division of labour in the enterprise
context: A company separates purchase, production and sale to different persons. Rate the following statements:
statements: Within the company, work is divided by several people.
The persons concerned are then responsible for certain tasks and can concentrate on them.
In a modern economy, division of labour and specialisation take place only between countries, never within businesses or households.
Divisions such as purchasing, production and sales (distribution) correspond to the operational form of this division.
As soon as departments exist, no personal responsibility for individual tasks is removed.
tactical_explanations:
To leave purchasing, manufacturing and selling in one person would be the opposite of the organization described. The level within the company is explicitly mentioned: many different tasks are divided between several persons. The described operation follows exactly this pattern, not a special way.

The statement is true.

The person who takes over the purchase can concentrate on it; he who produces or sells, as well. Responsibility for certain tasks is the formulation of the textbook, not just a loose recommendation. Concentration here means depth in one function, not disinterest in the rest of the operation.

Without this attachment to persons, there would be departments only on paper. The internal division of labor lives on the fact that someone is responsible and can exercise the respective area, instead of serving all functions simultaneously with half attention.

The statement is true.

These include several levels: within households and businesses, between businesses and also among countries. Those who only apply the country level, even though they are first mentioned, will break the first levels. "Only between countries and "never internally" are therefore wrong, regardless of the fact that there will be international specialisation later on.

The internal and external division of labour do not exclude each other. A company with departments can simultaneously obtain or export intermediates; this does not cancel the internal division. Absolutism "only countries" is the trap, not the multi-levelness itself.

The statement is false.

Purchasing, production and sales or sales are in the sample series of departments. They are dedicated to operational areas and functions. The case with separate persons for these fields is the everyday implementation, not an invention outside the text.

The statement is true.

Divisions do not replace people with anonymous nothing. On the contrary, tasks are assigned to persons who are responsible. Existence of departments increases responsibility, it does not delete it. The claim that responsibility evades the department turns organization into irresponsibility.

The statement is false.

title: Agrana and Rosenbauer
context: Evaluate the following statements on Austrian examples of specialised companies:
statements: Agrana is a food and industrial group; the Viennese sugar is only one of many products.
Rosenbauer International AG is based in Leonding and produces fire trucks and equipment.
Agrana produces exclusively Viennese sugar and no other goods.
The companies mentioned only show a small section of the great variety of companies.
A specialised company must never have its headquarters in Austria.
tactical_explanations:
Viennese sugar is the well-known label, not the entire range. Agrana also produces fruit preparations and fruit juice concentrates, starch and bioethanol. Specialization means: the Group and its employees concentrate on certain fields of food and industrial goods production, not on a single brand product.

Headquarters in Vienna does not change this classification.

The statement is true.

Fire vehicles and equipment mark the field. Rosenbauer, based in Leonding, Upper Austria, is an example of a company specialising in certain products. The section lists such companies to show their diversity and specialisation, not to ask for internet addresses.

Specialization excludes the same operation from producing any kind of goods. It does not exclude that several related products are produced within the field, here vehicles and equipment for fire brigades. This concentration illustrates the case.

The statement is true.

The only thing that contradicts the product list is sugar. Fruit preparations, concentrates, starch and bioethanol are among them; sugar is explicitly one of many products. The case lies in the word "exclusively" which makes a well-known article the whole company.

The statement is false.

Four names do not replace the whole economy. Of course, the following examples showed only a small section of the great variety of companies. Agrana and Rosenbauer are illustrations, not a complete map and no obligation to know each corporate website.

Anyone who memorizes the list as completeness misses the purpose: to make it visible that companies with employees specialize in certain products and services. The detail character belongs to the statement, not as footnote afterwards.

The statement is true.

All the examples mentioned are Austrian companies. Based in Vienna, Leonding or Linz, the company is compatible with specialization. A ban on Austria does not occur and would make the illustrations that are at stake invisible.

The statement is false.

title: Voest and Do&Co
context: Evaluate the following statements to Voest and Do&Co as specialized company:
statements: Voest is a steel and technology group headquartered in Linz, Germany.
Do&Co is an Austrian company with business areas such as catering, restaurants, airport lounges and hotels.
Specialization means that a company can only have one business segment.
Companies specialize in the production of certain products and/or services with their employees.
Do&Co is not allowed to provide services as a specialized company, but only physical industrial products such as steel.
tactical_explanations:
Steel and technology, not any industry. The Voest is one of the well-known Austrian companies, the headquarters is in Linz, the field is steel and metals. Thus, the section Specialization illustrates: Focus on certain products, not the entire world of goods. Linz is a location for illustration, no examination question for a website.

The statement is true.

Catering for events and flights, restaurants, lounges and hotels form the bundle. Do&Co is headquartered in Vienna and stands for specialization in the field of gastronomy and related services. Several business areas within this field do not contradict the specialisation, they describe it.

If you only consider factories to be specialized, this is exactly the service example. Do&Co is considered as a section of the company's diversity alongside Agrana, Rosenbauer and Voest.

The statement is true.

Agrana combines sugar, fruit, starch and bioethanol, Do&Co catering, restaurants, lounges and hotels. Specialization means focusing on certain products and/or services, not the rule "always only one". The word "always" makes a wrong narrowing of one direction.

The statement is false.

Employees and companies belong together. Specialization is not an abstract industry brand, but rather the focus with the employees on certain products and/or services. Therefore, companies can then offer a large number of such goods in certain quality.

The formula "and/or" allows industry and service alike.

Without the people who concentrate on tasks, specialization would remain an empty company sign. Internal division of labor into departments and the orientation of the whole company into a field interlock. This is exactly the approach chosen by the section before it mentions the Austrian examples.

The statement is true.

Steel is the field of the Voest, not the mandatory format for any specialized company. Do&Co creates services: catering, restaurant, lounges, hotels. Products and services are in the introductory phrase side by side. Anyone who forbids services because specialization should sound "industrially" ignores the explicit example.

The statement is false.

title: Services and departments
context: A clinic is responsible for diagnostics, care and administration, analogous to operational functions. Rate the following statements:
statements: In a service establishment, tasks can also be divided into several persons and areas, which focus on specific functions.
Specialization does not occur in service occupations, because only industrial enterprises may share tasks.
In companies there are usually departments for operational areas such as purchasing, production, sales, marketing or accounting.
A hairdresser, who makes many cuts and treatments daily, illustrates specialization in services.
Each department must fulfil all operational functions simultaneously, otherwise there is no organization.
tactical_explanations:
Diagnostics, care and administration are different tasks. The theory does not limit internal division of labour to factories: within the companies, tasks are distributed to several persons who are responsible and can concentrate.

A service company with a divisional area follows the same logic as purchasing, production and distribution in an industrial enterprise.

Organization means that not every person exercises every function at the same time. Focus on diagnostics or administration is specialization inside, not a violation of the concept of the company. The clinic is a scene for exactly this internal level.

The statement is true.

The hairdresser in the introductory section is itself a service example: many different haircuts and treatments daily, made possible by specialization and organization. Do&Co later stands for catering and gastronomy. The claim that only industry may share, cancels these cases. Specialization applies to products and/or services.

The statement is false.

The departmental series is the standard business image. Purchasing, production, sales or sales, marketing, accounting, etc. are dedicated to areas and functions. A clinic can be arranged in an analogous way without the names having to be identical; the pattern remains internal division of labor according to functions.

Typically, it means that every micro-company is not necessarily putting all these signs on the door. The point is functional separation, not a rigid list of five logos. In the clinic, administration, care and diagnostics correspond to this separation according to tasks.

The statement is true.

Haircuts and treatments are services, not physical products such as bread or cars. Nevertheless, the section leads as proof that specialization allows a large number of services in certain quality. The hairdresser is thus the service donor to the baker and the car manufacturer.

The statement is true.

Organization means separation by function, not the duty to do everything at the same time in each department. If each job were to perform purchasing, production, sales, marketing and accounting in parallel, the meaning of the department would fall. Concentration on certain tasks would be impossible. The absolute "all functions simultaneously" tilts the definition to the opposite.

The statement is false.

title: Ebenen innerer Spezialisierung
context: Evaluate the following statements on division of labour into households and companies and on the Austrian business examples:
statements: In private households, there is no division of tasks between persons.
Agrana, Rosenbauer, Voest and Do&Co serve as illustrations of specialised Austrian companies and only as a small section of the diversity.
Specialization and organization of companies can offer a large number of goods in certain quality, such as bakeries or autoworks.
Within companies, departments focus on operational areas, such as marketing or accounting.
Those who specialise as companies can only produce a single product without quality standards and never a service.
tactical_explanations:
No distinction in the household is contrary to the first level. Tasks are distributed among several persons; cooking and bath cleaning are the school example. Household and business stand side by side as internal division of labor. The absolute "nothing erases this level.

The statement is false.

Four companies, one purpose: to make it visible that companies with employees specialize in certain products and/or services. Agrana in the food and industrial goods field, Rosenbauer in fire fighting technology, Voest in steel and technology, Do&Co in catering and catering.

They are explicitly called as small sections, not as completeness and not as querying Internet addresses.

Illustration means: recognize the pattern, not memorize the company chronicles. Seat details and fields help to see specialization in concrete terms. Anyone who misunderstands the names as a mandatory catalog misses the section; anyone who reads them as examples of concentration on a field meets him.

The statement is true.

Bakers and car manufacturers are the guiding principles for quantity and quality. Specialization of employees plus organization of the company do not result in poverty in the offer, but many goods in certain quality. Cars in series, bread and pastries in variety: the same principle, other goods.

Without the internal order, i.e. responsibilities and processes, the focus on a field would remain poor. With it, precisely the ability to deliver becomes out of concentration. The sentence in theory links both conditions; whoever sees the company label "bäckerei" and no organization does not explain the visible variety.

The statement is true.

Marketing and accounting are in the departmental series alongside purchasing, production and sales. They are operational functions, not just labels. Internal specialisation means that such units are dedicated to an area instead of using all functions at the same time. This applies regardless of which Austrian example is placed next to it.

The statement is true.

Three errors in one set. Specialization allows a large number of goods, not just a single piece. Quality is thought of, not deleted. Services are included: hairdresser, Do&Co, and the introductory set says products and/or services.

The combination of the obligation to be united, the waiver of quality and the prohibition on services does not stand up to any of these statements.

A single piece of quality-based products would be the opposite of what bakers, automakers and hairdressers show. Agrana with several food products and Do&Co with several service fields also refute the narrowness of "only one product, never one performance". Specialization is focus on a field with depth, not a production ban.

The statement is false.

title: Tables or only bathroom furniture
context: Company Althuber manufactures in the furniture industry exclusively tables and chairs, company Leitner exclusively bathroom equipment. Evaluate the following statements about the specialization between companies:
statements: Spezialisierung zwischen Unternehmen liegt vor, wenn Betriebe einer Branche nur bestimmte Produkte erzeugen.
Inter-company specialisation requires that Althuber and Leitner have merged into one single company.
The division of only tables and chairs versus only bathroom facilities is a case of specialisation between companies.
Within one sector, no company may limit itself to a narrow range, because specialization occurs exclusively between countries.
The division of labour and specialisation also take place between companies in a modern economy, not only within one company.
tactical_explanations:
In the furniture industry, one company can only produce tables and chairs, another only bathroom equipment. This restriction on certain products within an industry is called specialisation between companies. It is not about departments in a house, but about separate companies with a narrow assortment.

Althuber and Leitner illustrate this level without having to cover the entire furniture range.

The statement is true.

Two legally separate furniture companies can specialise without merging. The theory speaks of specialization between companies, i.e. several companies whose products complement each other or narrow within an industry.

A merger into a single legal entity would be the opposite of this separation: then there would be rather internal division of labour into departments, not the inter-company level. Althuber remains a table and chair manufacturer, Leitner remains a bathroom furniture specialist, and precisely this separation is the point.

Group membership, joint owners or a joint company sign are not a prerequisite. Specialization is based on the fact that there are several companies.

The statement is false.

Only tables and chairs on one side, only bathroom facilities on the other: this is the furniture example of the section, almost literally. Specialization means that not every furniture company produces everything, but focuses on certain products.

The scene around Althuber and Leitner thus falls under the inter-company level, not a mere question of taste in the assortment.

The statement is true.

The levels of specialisation are parallel: within households and companies, between companies and between countries. Those who strike the inter-company level and only allow countries to apply shorten the list. A furniture industry with narrow assortments is expressly permitted and even the example of teaching.

Althuber may stay at tables without the only permissible form of international specialisation.

The statement is false.

Modern economy knows the division of labour on several levels at the same time. Within one company there are departments, between companies there are narrow assortments and supply chains, between countries there are focus areas. The statement states that the inter-company level belongs to it and does not arise in the in-house.

Althuber and Leitner are two companies, not two departments of the same company.

The statement is true.

title: Fruit, frozen food and carton
context: An agricultural establishment supplies fruit to a frozen food company and to a fruit preparation manufacturer. Both are supplied by a packaging specialist. Rate the following statements on the specialization in the supply chain:
statements: Specialization is also available where the products of one company are the prerequisite for the production of another.
Agricultural holdings can supply fruit and vegetables to several processing companies.
The packaging manufacturer is outside of any specialization because he does not produce food himself.
A frozen food company must always produce fruit and packaging in its own factory, otherwise there is no modern economy.
The same agricultural supply can supply several customers, such as frozen food and fruit preparation.
tactical_explanations:
Intermediate consumptions combine businesses to a chain. Fruit from the farm is the material prerequisite for the production of frozen food or fruit preparation. This is precisely the case called specialization: the products of one are the condition for the production of the other. It is not enough to think only of narrow assortments in the same industry.

The Hof chain, processing, cartonboard is the second pattern of inter-company specialisation.

The statement is true.

Fruit and vegetables do not leave the farm in one direction only. In the text, agricultural companies supply several customers, such as frozen food and fruit preparation. A farm does not have to bind to a single processor in order to be considered specialized. Several customers are expressly provided for.

The scene meets this multiple pattern, not a one-way street to a corporation.

The statement is true.

Packaging is itself a specialized product. The processors are supplied with cartons and similar covers from another company that specializes in the production of packaging. Food production is therefore not a ticket to the category of specialization.

Those who exclude the carton business because they do not stir yoghurt, do not recognize the chain: fruit from the farm, processing to frozen food or fruit preparation, then the shell without which the goods are not traded. The third stage is part of this, precisely because their products are the prerequisite for the sale of the second stage. Specialization does not end with edible goods.

The statement is false.

The production of all pre-products is not exactly a description of the modern division of labour. Anyone who produces bicycles or fruit yoghurt does not necessarily produce every item and every fruit itself. Freezer food can buy fruit and buy cartons. The claim that only the complete self-production counts as a modern economy turns the chapter around.

Dependence on suppliers is the downside, not a formal error.

The statement is false.

The same harvest can be used by several customers. The frozen food and fruit preparations are called together as recipients of agricultural deliveries. A farm does not have to reserve the quantity exclusively for a plant to be specialized. Parallel customers show how a specialized pre-product enters into various further processing processes.

That's exactly what the scene is.

The statement is true.

title: Climate, mineral resources and know-how
context: Countries focus on sectors for which they have favourable conditions. Evaluate the following statements on international specialisation:
statements: Countries specialize in specific sectors of the economy, and in particular in those areas for which they have favourable conditions.
These conditions include the theory of climate, mineral resources, labour and know-how.
International specialisation is impossible because the climate is the same everywhere and locations are not different.
Knowhow does not play a role in the choice of location of countries, only natural resources are crucial.
A country with a suitable climate can promote agricultural production without any country having to set the same priorities.
tactical_explanations:
Countries choose priorities rather than being equally strong in each economic sector. International specialisation is described as activity in certain areas and as promoting those fields for which favourable conditions exist. Climate, raw materials, labour and knowledge are such levers, not a random generator.

The statement reflects this logic without claiming that a country can only know one sector.

The statement is true.

Four conditions are side by side: climate, mineral resources, workers and know-how. None of the four is mere a word of jewellery. A wine-growing region uses climate, an ore site mineral resources, an industrial site often labor and accumulated knowledge. The list is the definition of favourable conditions in this section, not an open formula of wish.

If you strike one of the four, you shorten the theory.

The statement is true.

Climate differences are just one reason why countries set different priorities. If the climate were identical everywhere, one of the mentioned location characteristics would be omitted, but the rest remained.

The claim that international specialisation is impossible because the climate is nowhere different is double wrong: the climate is different between wine-growing areas, grain belts and colder zones, and specialization is not solely dependent on the weather. Natural resources, workers and know-how remain independent reasons.

An industrial location can be distinguished by knowledge and labour, even if the climate is inconspicuous. Thus, it is impossible to follow either factually or conceptually from the equality of the climate.

The statement is false.

Knowhow is in the same brackets as climate, mineral resources and labour. It is therefore explicitly a location factor, not a residual item. Taiwanese bicycle specialists in the woom example are later called precisely because of decades of know-how. To apply only mineral resources covers three of the four requirements and contradicts the enumeration.

Raw materials can help, they do not replace knowledge.

The statement is false.

Appropriate climate can be an agricultural focus, while another country promotes metals, industry or services. International specialisation does not mean that all choose the same areas. Each country starts where the conditions are favourable.

The statement captures this diversity and remains within the book list of location factors.

The statement is true.

title: Woom and global bike parts
context: Woom GmbH does not completely create children's bicycles in its own factory, but works with highly specialized companies in different countries. Rate the following statements about the international division of work on bicycles:
statements: Those who produce bicycles do not necessarily produce all the items that are necessary for an entire bicycle.
On the bicycle one can recognize inter-company and international specialization at the same time.
woom relies on highly specialized companies in different countries, from Poland to Cambodia.
Most of the Woom production is done by Taiwanese bicycle specialists with decades of know-how, which manufacture in Southeast Asia.
International division of labor on bicycles means that all individual parts must necessarily be created in Austria.
tactical_explanations:
Bicycle factories often buy rims, gears, saddles or frames instead of pressing each part themselves. The following applies: whoever produces bicycles does not necessarily produce all the parts necessary for an entire bicycle. In-company specialization means here that highly specialized companies supply intermediate services.

The final assembly or the brand does not replace the entire parts production. woom is the clear counter image for complete self-production: global brand, worldwide production, partner from Poland to Cambodia. A finished wheel in the trade does not prove that a single plant has produced each screw itself.

The statement is true.

The bicycle is a cross-company level and country level. Parts come from specialized companies, and these companies are located in different countries. The chapter therefore presents the bicycle as an example, in which both forms are recognized at the same time. Anyone who sees only departments in an Austrian plant, undermines the international chain.

woom makes both visible: foreign businesses and foreign locations.

The statement is true.

Poland to Cambodia is the geographical bracket in the quotation of the Woom website, as of March 2021. Highly specialized companies in different countries secure the quality standards, not a single parent plant. The statement repeats this proof without memorizing export statistics. Cooperation across country borders is the core here, not an advertising phrase without content.

The statement is true.

Taiwanese bicycle specialists, for example, carry the majority of production and manufacture in Southeast Asia, based on decades of know-how in bicycle production. This is international specialization in know-how, not in Austrian mineral resources. The brand woom remains global, manufacturing follows the sites with accumulated knowledge.

The statement is based on this sentence of definition.

The statement is true.

All parts in Austria would be the opposite of the chain described. International division of labour means that leading exporters of bicycle parts are sitting in different countries and working with partners from Poland to Cambodia. A compulsion to produce all components domestically is the example.

Quality standards are served here by specialized foreign companies, not by autarky.

The statement is false.

title: Competence and larger number of units
context: A company focuses on a few steps and buys other components. Evaluate the following statements about the production advantages of specialization:
statements: Specialization is the advantage for production to concentrate on fewer work steps and to develop competence in this area.
If you do not have to create all components yourself and do not have to perform all work steps yourself, you can achieve a larger quantity overall.
Specialization brings only disadvantages to production and never benefits in terms of competence or quantity.
Competence grows in the narrower field on which the company focuses, not by creating each part in its own plant.
A larger number of units is only possible if each company carries out all the work itself.
tactical_explanations:
Less work steps in the company create space for practice, organization and quality in this particular section. This is called a great advantage of specialization: one focuses on fewer work steps and can expand the competence in this area.

A frame builder who does not develop every circuit at the same time can become deeper in frame production because time, machines and personnel do not split up on all components. The statement comes to this mechanism without denying the dependencies that were later dealt with.

The chapter has a successive advantage and disadvantage; here only the advantage is meant competence, not the assertion of a riskless world.

The statement is true.

The theory explicitly links the larger number of pieces to the fact that you do not have to create all the components yourself and not all the steps yourself. If you do not produce each part yourself, you can focus your own line on what you can do and create more finished pieces.

The amount is not increasing despite specialization, but because specialization shifts work outwards. That is the second production advantage in addition to competence.

The statement is true.

The chapter does not claim any disadvantages, except for one. It has great advantages: concentration, competence, larger number of pieces, often lower costs per piece. Dependence and ecological burdens follow. Anyone who cuts the advantage side reads only the downside. Competence and quantity are precisely the positive effects.

The absolute wording never holds out the advantages of the structure.

The statement is false.

Competence is in the selected section. Focus on fewer steps is the way there, it is not a full range of products in your own work. A company that does everything itself, splits up practice and organization. The theory binds the gain of competence to the narrower area. Purchase of the other components is compatible with this profit, and often only makes it possible.

The statement follows this bond of focus and skill.

The statement is true.

All steps are the brake, not the condition for quantity. Larger quantities are just justified by the fact that you do not have to produce everything yourself. The claim turns the causality around. Self-production of all components binds hall, staff and time to many partial works and limits the finished quantities. Specialization loosens this bond.

The statement is false.

title: Hall and unit costs
context: A production hall is built. Whether it runs full or only half the capacity does not change the construction effort. Evaluate the following statements about costs and specialization:
statements: Not all production costs increase with the number of pieces produced.
A production hall costs the same amount in the construction, regardless of whether it produces the full or only half capacity.
With higher production, the total production costs can be divided into a larger number of units, so that the costs per unit are reduced.
The costs of the hall always rise in a ratio of 1 to 1 with the number of pieces, the quantity doubles, the hall expenditure doubles.
The lower production costs per unit can subsequently reduce the price at which a piece can be sold.
tactical_explanations:
Number of pieces and cost block do not always run parallel. Some expenses, such as the construction of a hall, arise regardless of whether many or few pieces later leave the line. It is important to note: not all production costs increase with the number of pieces produced.

This independence opens the way to decreasing costs per piece as soon as the amount grows. Variable inputs can grow along, the hall construction does not do it in the construction.

The statement is true.

The building costs of the hall do not depend on whether there is full capacity or half capacity later. The chapter says this explicitly: the hall costs equal amount in the construction, full or half use does not change this amount. Specialization and larger quantities use this block by sending more products through the same hall.

The statement is the rule of the text, not a special business theory outside the definition.

The statement is true.

The total cost divided by the number of pieces is the cost per piece. If the denominator rises, while a large part of the counter, such as the hall, stops, the quotient falls. This is precisely described as a division into a larger number of pieces. Lower unit costs are therefore in many cases the result of higher production under specialization, not a coincidence.

The identity cost per unit equals total cost by quantity bears the claim.

The statement is true.

The construction of a production hall is a cost block that does not grow at all. Whether the full capacity or only half the capacity is running later, the one-time construction costs do not change. If the amount generated doubles, this amount of the hall does not double in step.

Suppose the hall costs 400000 euros in the construction: for 2000 pieces, the cost of the hall is 200 euros on each piece, for 4000 pieces only 100 euros. The total production costs are distributed over more units, the costs per piece are reduced.

A rigid ratio of 1 to 1 of hall effort and number of pieces contradicts exactly this mechanism which the theory demonstrates at the hall.

The statement is false.

Lower unit costs do not remain in the accounting. The chapter results in the following: the price at which a piece can be sold can fall. Specialization thus acts over quantity and cost sharing up to the market price. The statement does not claim a forced price reduction, but the mentioned possibility.

Hall, quantity and price are related in this order.

The statement is true.

title: Risk of supply and medicines
context: A pharmaceutical company obtains active ingredients from specialized suppliers. A batch comes late and in fluctuating quality. Evaluate the following statements on the disadvantages of specialization:
statements: Specialization also means dependence on the other companies that are to supply.
This dependence concerns the quality of the delivery and a sufficient quantity to arrive at the right time.
Delayed or poor delivery can affect your own production and lead to loss of image and order.
This dependency is particularly problematic when it comes to products that the population urgently needs, such as medicines.
As soon as a company is competent in one step, any dependence on suppliers is eliminated, because it can completely eliminate delivery risk.
tactical_explanations:
Suppliers carry parts of the chain that the specialized company no longer manages itself. Dependence is therefore the downside of concentration, not an operating accident. This disadvantage applies immediately after the cost advantages. The pharmaceutical manufacturer who buys active ingredients is attached to foreign plants, even if the own tableting is excellently organized.

Spezialisierung beseitigt diese Bindung nicht, sie erzeugt sie.

The statement is true.

Quality and time quantity are the two axes of dependence. Poor batch and delayed batch are both mentioned: quality of delivery on the one hand, sufficient quantity at the right time on the other. Price alone is not the criterion of this section. The pharmaceutical case hits both axes: fluctuating quality and delay.

Those who only look at the purchase price underestimate the disadvantage described in the chapter.

The statement is true.

Production is still or becomes defective as soon as the precursor is missing or unfit. This can lead to loss of image and loss of orders, according to the theory. The chain is causal, not just annoying: supply errors, impaired own production, damaged external effect, broken orders.

The late drug charge illustrates the same path. A finer division of labor increases this vulnerability when a specialized input is lost.

The statement is true.

Drugs are an example of goods that the population urgently needs. Subcontracting dependence is particularly problematic there, because not only a company image, but the supply is at stake. A late drug is not a mere question of margins.

The statement takes over this qualitative judgment of the chapter without inventing a certain amount of mismatch. Urgency makes a social risk out of operational dependence.

The statement is true.

Competence in one's own step does not replace the foreign batch. The chapter clearly separates the advantages of concentration, skill, quantity and unit costs from the dependence on quality and date. Anyone who explains the advantage side to remove the risk, merges both paragraphs into a single desired image.

The pharmaceutical company can master tableting and still cannot deliver without a timely, usable active ingredient; image and orders remain vulnerable. Can't completely eliminate the delivery risk, it makes its own cutout strong and the rest of the chain foreign.

Especially in the case of drugs that the population urgently needs, this foreignness remains dangerous.

The statement is false.

title: Long distances as an environmental load
context: Bicycle parts travel across continents before a ready-made bike is available at the dealer's. Evaluate the following statements about supply chains and the environment:
statements: Long delivery routes and supply chains are also an ecological problem.
Transporting individual parts for a product from different countries and continents many thousand kilometers usually means a high environmental burden.
This load is mainly caused by transport by trucks, container ships or aircraft.
International specialisation completely eliminates the ecological burden of transport, because unit costs and environmental pollution exclude each other.
The theory does not mention ecological problems of long chains, it deals exclusively with hall costs and competence.
tactical_explanations:
Long distances are in the chapter as a separate disadvantage next to the dependence on supply. Specialization over country borders creates gains in quantity and competence, but attracts transport routes to itself. Delivery routes and supply chains are explicitly named an ecological problem.

The bicycle parts that cross continents are precisely this case, not a marginal issue outside the division of labor. Ecology is part of the evaluation of specialisation, not only the unit costs.

The statement is true.

Many thousand kilometres for individual parts from different countries and continents: this is how the representation formulates the rule of a high environmental impact. It is not about a unique short distance between two neighboring plants, but about the global chain that prepares the bicycle example.

As a rule, it means: typically high load, not an invariably natural law without means of transport. The statement remains with this qualitative rule.

The statement is true.

Three carriers of the load are named: trucks, container ships and aircraft. Especially this freight transport is burdening the environment when parts are moved over long distances. The list is the concreteization of the ecological problem, not any traffic list. A bicycle frame that travels by ship and truck falls under it.

Other modes of transport do not exclude the phrase philosophically, it designates the central ones.

The statement is true.

Unit costs and environmental load are running in a row in the chapter, not as mutually extinguishing sizes. Lower costs per piece are an advantage of specialization because hall and similar blocks are distributed over more units. Long distances are an ecological problem of the same specialization as parts travel across countries and continents.

The full elimination of the transport load by international division of labour does not claim the representation. On the contrary: exactly the international chain generates the kilometers with trucks, container ship and aircraft. Whoever declares advantage and disadvantage to a game, in the environment disappears as soon as the unit price falls, contradicts the structure.

The statement is false.

Hall costs and competence fill the advantage sales, dependence and long distances fill the disadvantage sales. Ecology is explicitly mentioned there: high load especially by trucks, container ship and aircraft. The claim that the theory is silent about the environment and knows only hall and skill, cuts the final part.

The bicycle with global parts is incompletely read without this page. Specialization is presented as a double face, not as a mere cost history.

The statement is false.

title: Family budget of Hubers
context: Evaluate the following statements on scarcity in private household:
statements: Hubers' family budget is limited, so they have to decide how much they spend on housing, mobility, daily shopping, saving and holidays.
Once the family receives a regular income, their money is unlimited and scarcity is eliminated.
If the Hubers put aside more for the holiday, less remains for other uses of the same budget.
With scarce resources, only companies, not private households, need to manage.
