The Commission is proposing to the Council that the Council should adopt a directive on the approximation of the laws of the Member States relating to the labelling of dangerous substances.
tactical_explanations:
The Hubers have a certain family budget, not an infinite cash register. Living, car or bicycle, shopping, saving and holiday access to the same pot. This is precisely the distribution of budget for scarcity: limited resources, several possible uses, a decision.

In the text of the teaching, the family explicitly decides: how much for living, how much for mobility (car, bicycles), how much for daily purchases, how much to save, how much for vacation. This is not a free wish list, but the division of a limited budget on rival uses.

The statement is true.

A salary finally arrives and remains. The family continues to distribute limited income on competing needs. Shortage does not disappear on payday, and unlimited money is not available. The claim that regular income keeps all borders, does not stand up to the definition.

No private household has unlimited money or other means of exchange. A salary is itself a scarce resource that has to be used planned. Whoever links unlimitedness to the payday confuses inflow with infinity. After the transfer, the Hubers remain in the same scarcity as before, only with a concrete amount on the account.

The statement is false.

More for holidays means that the same euro cannot be spent at the same time on housing, mobility or weekly shopping. The budget is a scarce resource with alternative uses. The shift of a item changes the remaining allocation.

The statement is true.

The resources on both sides are scarce: for households and companies. No private household has unlimited money or other means of exchange. Therefore, the Hubers must also manage, not just a factory. The restriction on companies alone is wrong.

The statement is false.

Because resources are scarce, their use must be planned: raw materials, labour and financial resources are not unlimited. In the household, this means that the family budget is deliberately distributed between housing, mobility, consumption, saving and holidays. That is economy in the sense of scarcity.

Raw materials, machines, labor, financial resources and much more are not available indefinitely. Therefore, they must be managed with them, that is, their use must be planned precisely. For Hubers, the family budget is this financial limit. Planning here is not a virtue exercise, but the result of scarcity.

The statement is true.

title: Unlimited goods and money
context: Evaluate the following statements on scarcity as the starting point for economic activity:
statements: The exchange of goods for money would be relatively easy if both were available indefinitely.
Every company can produce unlimited quantities of goods as long as demand exists.
No private household has unlimited money or other means of exchange available.
Shortage is only a matter of financial resources, but not of raw materials, machinery or labour.
All economic operators must decide what they are using limited resources for which alternative uses exist.
tactical_explanations:
If there were goods and money without a limit, there would be no compulsion to choose. The exchange would then be a mere liquidation without planning the use. Precisely for this reason the starting point emphasizes: it would be so simple only under Infinity, which does not apply in reality.

The statement is true.

No company can produce unlimited quantities of goods. The means of production, raw materials, machines, labour force and financial resources are scarce. Demand alone does not remove these limits. The claim of unlimited production capacity contradicts scarcity.

Demand can increase the desire for more goods, but it does not create endless machine hours, endless raw materials and infinite equity. Resources are scarce on both sides, household and companies. That is why the exchange would only be easy if goods and money were unlimited, which they are not.

The production limit remains, even if customers are standing in line.

The statement is false.

Private householders have limited money and limited other means of exchange. Therefore, they have to choose what is bought or exchanged. The statement directly affects the household side of scarcity.

The second basic question of economics is therefore next to production: what should be bought or exchanged. Limited means of exchange force selection. A household without limits in money would not have to ask this question. The reality of scarcity makes it inevitable.

The statement is true.

The balances are not just scarce. Raw materials, machines, labor, financial resources and much more are not available indefinitely. Those who narrow shortages on money leave out the other resources with which households and companies actually have to manage.

The list is deliberately broad: raw materials, machines, labor, financial resources and much more. Time, natural resources and sinks are added later in the same logic. Money shortage is a case, not the definition. Anyone who only sees the account overlooks the rest of the limited resources that households and businesses have.

The statement is false.

The following is a characteristic: all economic operators decide what limited resources are used for, although there are alternatives. We all therefore need to manage. The ongoing choice between possible applications is the core, not a special problem for individual companies.

The characteristic is not only for a particular size of the company, but for all economic operators because alternative uses exist. The current decision on what limited resources are used for is the common pattern of family, business and other actors in this section.

The statement is true.

title: Production means at Voest and Woom
context: Evaluate the following statements on scarcity in the company:
statements: A company like Voest or Woom must clarify what it can produce and what means of production are available in what quantity and quality.
Decisions on the use of limited resources are at the heart of the economy.
Financial resources of an enterprise may be invested completely without considering current payments, because investing is not an alternative to liquidity.
The means of production a company can afford is part of the scarcity decision.
If a company does not recognise scarcity, the use of resources remains automatically efficient.
tactical_explanations:
Companies like AGRANA, Rosenbauer, Voest, Do&Co or where are the same limits as a household, only on the production side. What should and can be produced? Which machines, intermediate consumption and labour force are available in what quality and quantity? This is the company example of scarcity.

What means of production do I need, which I can afford. Quantity and quality of the means are part of the same question. A company cannot pretend that there are unlimited inputs available. Voest, Woom and the other companies mentioned, manage by recognizing these limits and planning the deployment.

The statement is true.

It is not the mere possession of machines that makes up economies, but the current choice of what limited resources are used for. Samuelson and Nordhaus grasp the essence of economics as recognition of scarcity and as organization of the most efficient use of resources.

This resource use is constantly associated with many decisions and actions. Buying, selling, acting, investing and convincing are the everyday form of this choice, not a unique plan. The focus remains on the decision about limited means, not the mere existence of a machine park.

The statement is true.

The question is: how much can be invested, how much should be available for current payments? Investment and liquidity are alternative uses of the same financial resources. Anyone who invests everything and ignores payments misses this scarcity.

Financial resources have alternative uses: investment in investments or availability for current payments. Both at the same time, the amount is not sufficient. The claim that investing is not an alternative to liquidity, removes precisely this rivalry and thus the scarcity in the company.

The statement is false.

Besides the desire to produce something, the question of which means of production can be afforded is also important. Price, quality and available quantity of means limit the feasible. This is not a technical marginal note, but part of the central allocation decision.

The statement is true.

Efficiency does not arise by itself. The essence of economics is to recognize scarcity as a reality and to organize the use as efficiently as possible. Anyone who denies the border does not plan to use it, and then efficiency is not automatically guaranteed.

Samuelson and Nordhaus: the essence of economics consists in the recognition of scarcity as a reality and in a social organization that allows the most efficient use of resources. Without recognition of reality, there is no such organization in the company. Automatic efficiency is then an empty hope, not a mechanism.

The statement is false.

title: Basic questions of economic activity
context: Evaluate the following statements on the basic questions that derive from scarcity:
statements: The current decision on limited resources raises the question of how and for whom to produce in what quantity and quality.
The only basic question of economics is which price is formed on the market.
The basic questions include what is to be bought or exchanged.
Quality of production does not matter in the basic questions, the only decisive factor is the quantity produced.
Economics consists of many human activities such as buying, selling, trading, investing and persuading.
tactical_explanations:
The basic questions are derived from this, including: What should be produced in what quantity and in what quality, how and for whom? The statement correctly reflects this production question.

The statement is true.

The choice of resource use is different: production (what, how, for whom, quantity, quality) and the question of what is bought or exchanged. A single market price question as the only basic question does not replace this list.

This section does not deal with market equilibrium and not the economic cycle. The basic questions are production questions (which, like, for whom, quantity, quality) and the purchase or exchange question. Whoever makes the market price the only basic question, shifts the material into a later chapter and drops the scarcity questions of this section.

The statement is false.

In addition to the production side, the use side of households and other consumers is: What should be bought or exchanged? This also follows directly from the fact that funds are limited and alternatives exist.

Private households do not have unlimited money. Therefore, the exchange question is not a question of taste, but part of the economy. What is bought or exchanged competes with other uses of the same limited budget. The basic question is necessarily a matter of scarcity, not only of the production hall.

The statement is true.

The basic question is that quantity and quality are common. Anyone who only lets the number of pieces apply, will remove the quality dimension that is explicitly asked for. Shortness also affects the quality in which it is produced, not only how many units are produced.

In what quantity and in what quality: both parts are in the same list. To remove quality would mean to plan scarce resources only by number of pieces. A company like Do&Co or Woom also decides on the quality of the performance, not only about the number of units. The absolute formulation "no role" is therefore wrong.

The statement is false.

The use of resources is linked to many decisions and actions. The economy is described as a complex entity of human activities, such as buying, selling, trading, investing and convincing.

The economy is an enormously complex entity of various human activities. The quoted list Buying, selling, trading, investing and convincing makes it visible that resource use is not a single booking, but many actions. The statement follows this description.

The statement is true.

title: Day of learning or sports training
context: Evaluate the following statements on opportunity costs of time:
statements: If Lea uses the same afternoon to learn for the exam, she cannot use it for sports training at the same time.
Because learning costs nothing, there are no opportunity costs if Lea does not do the training.
opportunity costs are lost returns or the benefits of alternative actions that have been waived in favour of another.
Recreation and recreation have no economic value, because they are not always easy to express in money.
Leas limited time is a scarce resource with alternative uses.
tactical_explanations:
Time cannot be doubled. The afternoon that goes into learning is not available in parallel for sport or hobby. This example shows: one use excludes the other. This is the temporal side of opportunity costs.

If you spend your time studying for school or study, you cannot spend the same time with sports training or a hobby. Lea sits in this very example. opportunity costs are the unaccompanied benefits of training here, not a course fee for learning. The impossibility of living twice the same afternoon is the scarcity of time.

The statement is true.

opportunity costs are not dependent on whether a learning allowance is met. The unachieved benefit of training, fitness, joy, recovery, is the waiver that Lea wears when she learns. A price of zero on the chosen path does not erase this lost benefit.

A price of zero on the chosen option is a common mistake of thinking. opportunity costs are lost returns or not achieved benefit of the abandoned alternative action. Training, hobby, recreation: this falls away as soon as the afternoon is part of learning. Costless learning does not change this definition.

The statement is false.

The definition is: opportunity costs are lost returns or not the benefits of an alternative action that has been dispensed with in favour of another. Not the cash output of the chosen option, but the lost benefits of the abandoned alternative.

Option Learning vs Option Training: the benefit of B, which you do not use because you choose A. The definition clearly separates between the chosen action and the abandoned action. Cash receipts of the chosen action do not replace this missed benefit. That's exactly the way the term is built.

The statement is true.

In the example of the woom founder, it is expressly true that a leisure activity with joy and relaxation is also a value, even if it cannot be expressed in money value so easily. Thus, worthlessness does not follow from the fact that no invoice is in euro.

The statement is false.

Resources include time, money, means of production, natural resources and sinks. Leas hours are limited and have alternative uses. Therefore, it must manage: it decides what the scarce time is spent.

The statement is true.

title: Vegetable or flower meadow
context: Evaluate the following statements on opportunity costs of scarce area:
statements: The garden area is scarce: the family plant vegetable beds, can no longer grow flower meadow in the same place.
If she chooses the flower meadow, the opportunity costs are the lost use of vegetable harvest.
If it chooses vegetables, the unused use of the flower meadow is one of the opportunity costs, even without any sales proceeds.
opportunity costs only arise when the area is sold later, not already by the use itself.
The same area to be used twice full, once as a bed and once as a meadow, is possible in parallel and eliminates scarcity.
tactical_explanations:
The garden example in theory is scarce: vegetable beds at the same place exclude a flower meadow. The area is the scarce resource that only one use currently carries. The statement describes precisely this exclusion.

The area here is the scarce resource with alternative use, analogous to time and money in the other examples. At the same place to lead beet and meadow fully parallel would mean that the area is unlimited. The representation constructs the case as exclusion: planting vegetable beds means no more flower meadow at the same place.

The statement is true.

Those who choose the meadow do not use the abandoned alternative, here typically harvest, saving when purchasing or enjoying vegetables. opportunity costs are this lost yield or benefit, not the gardener's bill of the meadow alone.

opportunity costs are the yield of option B, which you do not have to do, because you have chosen option A. A is the meadow, B the vegetables. The lost benefit of the harvest is B, regardless of whether the family gives the flowers away or considers them. The gardening costs of the meadow are not this size.

The statement is true.

The flower meadow creates beauty and recreation; if the family abandons it in favour of the beds, this benefit is the abandoned alternative. The definition explicitly covers such non-monetary benefits.

Beauty and recreation of the meadow are benefits, even without sale. This fits the remark that joy and recreation represent a value, even if it can not be expressed as money value. opportunity costs must contain this not achieved benefit. A missing market price does not render the meadow worthless in terms of definition.

The statement is true.

opportunity costs are created by the decision for option A and against option B, i.e. even when using it. A later sale of land is not a prerequisite. The waiver of the other use of the area is the choice itself.

The decision against alternative use is made at the moment when the area is bound. A sale would be another, later choice over the same scarce resource, not the condition that opportunity costs exist at all. Whoever makes the sale a prerequisite, shifts the term to the land register.

The statement is false.

At the same place, there can be no full vegetable beds and a full flower meadow. Parallelity would deny the scarcity of the area. The alternative use remains an either-or-question, not a double use of the same parcel.

Shortness means: not unlimited, alternative uses, decision necessary. Double full use of the same parcel would fake Infinity. The family must manage, i.e. plan the use of the area. Parallelity as a lifting of scarcity contradicts the example.

The statement is false.

title: Elif: Re-training or unpaid internship
context: Evaluate the following statements on opportunity costs of an unpaid alternative:
statements: If Elif takes the internship, the opportunity costs include the 400 euros lost monthly tutoring.
Because the internship does not pay anything, no opportunity costs arise when choosing the internship.
If Elif stays with the tutoring, the opportunity costs include the unaccompanied benefits of experience in the internship and career prospects.
opportunity costs may be stated in euros only, other dimensions do not count.
As a student, Elif still has to manage with a short time and choose between the two uses.
tactical_explanations:
Option Internship means renunciation of option allowance. The lost earnings of the abandoned alternative are the 400 euros per month. This is the financial side of opportunity costs, analogous to the renunciation of another professional activity in the company's construction.

The statement is true.

Zero pay on the chosen way is not zero waiver. The tutor who can no longer give Elif falls away. opportunity costs are the lost benefits of the alternative, not the payout of the chosen employment. Unpaid does not delete this amount. Note: The next best use given is decisive, not the cash flow of the selected option.

Unpaid is the internship on the account, not without alternative. Elif could give tutoring in the same time and earn 400 euros. This lost income is option B. The definition does not ask whether Option A pays a salary, but what is dispensed with in favour of A. Zero pay on A does not delete B.

The statement is false.

If she stays with the tutoring, she excludes the internship. Experience, contacts and career prospects are benefits that she does not achieve. Also, not easily count in money-capable sizes, as in the leisure value in the founder example.

The benefits of the alternative given up are the professional prospects and experience comparable to the other professional activities that the woom founders could have chosen. Not all benefits bear a price tag. The statement remains in the definition because it indicates the benefits of the excluded option not achieved.

The statement is true.

Time, recovery, experience and other benefits may be included in the opportunity costs. It is expressly true that joy and recovery are a value, even if it is not so easy to express itself in money value. The rule "only euro" is too narrow.

The presentation allows leisure value, recreation and similar sizes. Experience from the internship is in the same open category of benefits. A rule that only allows for euro is narrower than the definition of opportunity costs.

The statement is false.

Being a student does not stop scarcity. Your hours are limited, tutoring and internship overlap, alternative possibilities of use of time remain. All economic operators, including them, must decide what the scarce resource time is used for.

Student, household, company: resources are scarce on both sides and with all economic operators. Time is explicitly part of the resource list. Overlapping uses of the same hours force the choice. Status as a student does not abolish scarcity or the obligation to plan the use.

The statement is true.

title: Next best alternative, not the sum of all options
context: Evaluate the following statements defining opportunity costs:
statements: If Sara chooses to use the laptop between washing machine and laptop, the opportunity costs are the lost use of the washing machine, not the sum of all the purchases that were eventually discarded.
opportunity costs are the sum of the prices of all the alternatives rejected.
There is no shortage of only two options, because scarcity requires many choices.
If Sara buys the washing machine, the opportunity costs are 1200 euros, so the addition of both prices.
opportunity costs refer to the abandoned alternative, not to the purchase price of the actually chosen item.
tactical_explanations:
The design is option A vs option B: the yield or benefit of B, which you do not use because you choose A. For laptop vs washing machine B is the machine. A list of all goods that have never been purchased does not belong in this size.

Sara has two concrete, mutually exclusive purchases, not a catalogue of all consumer requests. opportunity costs measure the lost benefits of the next best abandoned alternative. Summing up all goods ever discarded would blow the size and solve them from Option A versus Option B.

The statement is true.

The definition calls the alternative action, which one has renounced in favour of another, the abandoned alternative, not an addition of all rejected prices. Whoever sums up the fridge, travel, concert and machine, measures something different than opportunity costs.

Note: The lost benefit is the next best use, not a basket of all cancellations.

Adding all the prices you have rejected is exactly the mistake that the definition does not give up. The alternative to action you have dispensed with is an alternative, not the amount of cancellations. Refrigerator plus travel plus concert plus machine would be a shopping cart, no opportunity costs.

The statement is false.

Two rival uses of the same means create scarcity. The family budget, the garden area, learning or sports: everywhere an either or is sufficient. Many options are not a prerequisite. The absolute threshold "only starting from many alternatives" is wrong.

The statement is false.

If Sara chooses the machine, the relevant waiver of the use of the laptop (in the example 700 Euro purchase plus its use), is not machine plus laptop. opportunity costs do not add both cash registers.

Washing machine 500 plus laptop 700 only gives 1200 as the sum of two prices that Sara does not pay both and not both as a waiver. If she chooses the machine, she gives up the benefit of the laptop. The addition treats both goods as if they were the same abandoned alternative. This contradicts Option A against Option B.

The statement is false.

The price of A is the expenditure for the actual purchase, not the definition of opportunity costs. The lost income or the unrealized benefit of B remain decisive.

The purchase price of the selected item is the issue for A. opportunity costs are lost income or not achieved benefit of B. Both figures can appear in euros and remain different terms. Anyone who makes the A cash slip for definition misses the waiver.

The statement is true.

title: Start-up capital, securities or world tour
context: Evaluate the following statements on alternative use of money:
statements: If Jonas invests available money in the establishment of a company, he can no longer put the same amount into certain securities.
He can no longer spend the same amount on training or a world trip after the foundation.
Because a foundation is future-oriented, the opportunity costs of unselected investments are zero.
The opportunity costs of the establishment may include the loss of potential profits from securities.
Money, which is once meant for the company, has no alternative use and therefore does not have to be managed.
tactical_explanations:
It is precisely this chain that is called: putting money into a foundation means not investing the same amount in certain securities that might make profits, and one use excludes the other.

If you invest money that you have available in setting up a company, you can no longer invest this amount in certain securities. Jonas is in this textbook set. Alternative use and exclusion are fully described. The statement is the direct application.

The statement is true.

Likewise, the money can no longer be spent on an education or a world trip. Training and travel are other alternative uses of the same scarce financial means. The sentence repeats this point correctly.

Education and world travel are in the same paragraph as further uses of the same amount. After the bond to the foundation they are excluded. This is scarcity of financial means, not a moral warning of travel. The same sum cannot be financed in parallel company, study and world travel fully.

The statement is true.

Future orientation does not change the definition. opportunity costs are the lost return on the abandoned alternative, such as possible securities gains, benefits of travel or training. They do not become zero just because the foundation looks forward.

Zero opportunity costs would only exist without alternative use. Securities, training and travel are just such alternatives. The fact that a foundation aims at the future does not change the scarcity of the amount nor the lost earnings of the unelected investment. Future does not redeem the waiver.

The statement is false.

"Maybe profits" is explicitly part of the securities example. This unearned income is opportunity costs of the foundation, provided the securities are the abandoned alternative. Uncertainty does not take their character as lost income.

With securities, you might be able to make profits. This possible, then not achieved return is the lost return of the abandoned alternative. Uncertainty (maybe) belongs for example and does not take the amount as opportunity costs. It remains decisive that this path has been excluded.

The statement is true.

A mental commitment to purpose does not stop scarcity. As long as the amount could be spent on securities, training or travel, there are alternative uses. Therefore, money must be used to manage, so that it must be planned and decided.

An etiquette "for the company" is not a lifting of the scarcity. As long as other uses are conceivable, it must be decided what the amount is used for. Businesses are precisely the same as planning. Ending in the head does not replace the reality of limited funds.

The statement is false.

title: Time of Woom Founders
context: Evaluate the following statements to the opportunity costs in the company at the example Woom:
statements: The time and energy that Bezdeka and Ihlenfeld put into the construction of Woom GmbH could have been devoted to another occupation.
opportunity costs of the foundation are always only a lost salary in euros, never the value of leisure.
A given-up leisure activity with joy and relaxation can represent opportunity costs, even if the value cannot be expressed simply in money.
Depending on what the founders have given up, these abandoned possibilities represent their opportunity costs.
Because woom is later a company, during the construction all opportunity costs of the time used were accounted for.
tactical_explanations:
The example of opportunity costs is precisely this structure: a lot of time and energy in which, while the same time of another job or leisure could have been applied. Alternative employment is the core of the example.

Whether it is another professional activity to earn money, it is a leisure activity: both paths were open during the construction and were not chosen. Time and energy of the founders are scarce resources. The company example of opportunity costs is this waiver, not only a later profit and loss account of the GmbH.

The statement is true.

The two are mutually exclusive: other professional activities for money and leisure with joy and recreation. The leisure value counts, even if it is not so easy to express in money value. "Always only salary, never leisure" contradicts the text.

"Always" and "never" make the sentence a trap. The representation calls salary and leisure side by side and emphasizes the value of recovery, even without simple money valuation. opportunity costs of the foundation can therefore be lost income or not achieved leisure benefits, depending on what was actually abandoned.

The statement is false.

Recreation and joy are explicitly mentioned as value. Whoever gives up to build the company will bear opportunity costs in the form of not achieved benefit. Lack of euro valuation does not invalidate this benefit.

Not so easy to express in monetary value does not mean worthless. The definition explicitly allows not achieved benefits, not only lost earnings in euros. Joy and recovery of abandoned leisure are these benefits. The statement follows the founder example without additional acceptance.

The statement is true.

The wording is literally defined: depending on what the two have given up to build, these abandoned possibilities represent their opportunity costs. It depends on the actually displaced alternative.

Depending on what the two have given up on it: the formulation makes the opportunity costs dependent on people and situation. Not every conceivable use counts, but the abandoned possibility. That's exactly how the term is bound to woom.

The statement is true.

opportunity costs arise in the decision to use time for the construction and exclude other options. Later corporate success does not retroactively change that during the construction of alternative uses of time. Success does not delete the then abandoned.

During the construction the time was bound. Later existence of woom GmbH is the result of the election, not the proof that at that time no alternative existed. opportunity costs lie in the excluded employment of those years. Success afterwards does not count it to zero.

The statement is false.

title: Eine Filiale, zwei Standorte
context: Evaluate the following statements on the short capital input of a trading company:
statements: This year's capital is only enough for one branch, so the company must choose between location A and location B.
If it opens in A, the opportunity costs are the lost yield that location B would have provided.
If opened in B, the opportunity costs are the sum of the expected revenues of A and B together.
Large chains do not need to operate because their resources are virtually unlimited.
Like a household, the company decides what limited financial resources are used for, although alternative locations would be possible.
tactical_explanations:
Financial resources are not available indefinitely. If the capital is only available for one branch, the location is a decision on the use of scarce funds with a clear alternative. This corresponds to the company shortage: what can be afforded, what is the money used for.

What is to be and can be produced, what resources are available, how much to invest, how much to make current payments. A second branch would be a second use of the same scarce capital. If it is only enough for one, the location choice is the decision on the use. The company must operate, not just build.

The statement is true.

Option A excludes option B. opportunity costs are the yield of B, which is dispensed with because you choose A. The lost branch income in B is exactly this size, not the construction costs of A alone.

opportunity costs are the return on option B, which is waived because you have chosen option A. A is location A, B is location B. The lost branch income in B is B, not the bill of the construction manager in A. The statement complies with the definition.

The statement is true.

Adding A plus B would treat both returns as if they were attainable at the same time. However, capital is only enough for one branch. opportunity costs measure the lost return of the abandoned alternative, not the sum of both projects.

Sum A plus B assumes that both revenues are the waiver. However, waiver is only the non-chosen branch. To open two locations at the same time fully prohibits the scarce capital. The addition repeats the same error as with the sum of all rejected purchase prices: it does not measure the next best alternative.

The statement is false.

AGRANA, Voest or a trading chain cannot produce unlimited goods or open up locations. Size does not change the recognition of scarcity into Infinity. All economic operators must plan to use limited resources.

No company can produce unlimited quantities of goods. Size does not change raw materials, machinery, labor power and financial resources into infinity. Large chains must nevertheless plan the use. The claim that they do not have to operate contradicts the characteristic that all economic operators must decide.

The statement is false.

Household and companies are scarce on both sides. Alternative uses of capital (A or B) force economies: plan, decide, exclude other options. The analogy to the household is factually true here.

Resources are scarce on both sides. The household shares the family budget, the company shares the capital for locations. Alternative uses force the same logic. The analogy is laid out, not as an exception for trade.

The statement is true.

title: Overtime: Orders or maintenance
context: Evaluate the following statements on the use of scarce working hours in production:
statements: The limited overtime is a scarce resource and must be divided between the order backlog and preventive maintenance.
If time goes into the gap, opportunity costs include the unachieved benefits of failure to maintain, such as lower risk of failure.
If time goes into maintenance, opportunity costs include lost returns from faster processing of the residue.
If the employees agree, overtime is unlimited and there is no allocation decision.
A well-considered economic decision involves the opportunity costs as a consequence of the choice.
tactical_explanations:
The same overtime cannot fully serve the residue and full maintenance. Alternative possibilities of use of the production time force a decision on what the scarce resource is used for.

Working power is mentioned in the resource list and is not available indefinitely. Overtime is a limited block of this working power. Late or maintenance are alternative applications. The division is economy in production: decide what the short time is used for.

The statement is true.

Option residue means decision against option maintenance. The unreached benefit of maintenance, less risk of disruption, more stable production, is the waiver. opportunity costs may include such benefits, not just an immediate cash receipt.

Unachieved benefit of failed maintenance is option B if A is the residue. Lower risk of failure, quieter line, less consequential damage: these are benefits, even without an immediate invoice. The definition covers such benefits. opportunity costs are not only a lost piece wage here.

The statement is true.

Conversely, time in maintenance is missing from the backlog. Lost returns or unrealized deliveries are the return of the abandoned alternative. Opportunity costs are defined exactly as such.

Lost returns from faster processing are the return of the abandoned alternative as soon as the hours are stuck in maintenance. Deliveries that come later or fail are this return. Option maintenance against option residue remains an A-against-B. The statement takes the definition in the other direction.

The statement is true.

The consent of the workforce does not make people available indefinitely. Night hours, rest and machine time remain scarce. "Unlimited as soon as someone says yes" denies the reality of scarcity, which must be recognized in order to plan resources.

Unlimited overtime would only exist if labor was not a scarce resource. Consent does not change health, calendar and machine running into infinity. Without limit, the decision was made for what hours are used for. This is precisely the decision that is at the heart of the economy. Allocation remains.

The statement is false.

An economic decision is only well thought out and reflected upon when one is aware of the consequences. These consequences include the opportunity costs: the given up because other options were excluded. The statement makes this criterion.

Being aware of consequences means seeing the waiver, not only the advantage of the chosen layer. opportunity costs are among these consequences because other options are excluded. A decision that sees the lag and forgets the failed maintenance, or vice versa, would not be the reflected economy of the section.

The statement is true.

title: Oak wood: tables or shelves
context: Evaluate the following statements to the scarce use of materials in production:
statements: If the joinery chooses the less profitable line, the opportunity costs are zero because a better option would have existed.
Personal pleasure in a product line erases all opportunity costs of this choice.
Economics means treating scarce raw materials as if they were unlimitedly prepared to set priorities.
Because the same wood is "processed as well", no opportunity costs arise between tables and shelves.
Limited oak forcing to decide between alternative product lines and plan the use.
tactical_explanations:
Especially if a more profitable alternative exists and is not chosen, the lost yield of this alternative is the opportunity costs. Zero would be them only if no alternative use existed. The better option to know does not reduce the cost to zero, it makes it visible.

If there is a better alternative and if it is not chosen, its lost yield is just large, not zero. Zero would be the claim that there is no alternative use of wood. Tables against shelves are however two uses of the same scarce quantity. The better option to know makes the opportunity costs visible, it does not brush them.

The statement is false.

Joy at work is a benefit of the chosen line, it does not count away the lost yield of the other line. As with the Woom example, joy and renunciation can stand side by side. Personal satisfaction is not an eraser for opportunity costs.

Personal joy is the benefit of the chosen line and can explain the choice. It does not calculate the lost yield of the other line against zero. When building which counts leisure value besides lost content, without one of the sizes extinguishing the other. Joy and opportunity costs consist side by side.

The statement is false.

Economic activity is the opposite: recognising scarcity and carefully planning the use, organizing it as efficiently as possible. Imputing infinity and removing priorities means not managing. The formula distorts the definition.

The use of scarce raw materials must be managed, that is, its use must be planned precisely. Infinity is the refusal to plan. Unpriority means ignoring alternative uses. That is the opposite of recognition of scarcity as a reality.

The statement is false.

The fact that wood is processed does not change the fact that tables and shelves are rival uses of the same scarce quantity. Option A remains against option B. "Converted as it is" describes the material consumption, not the abandoned product line.

"Consisting of any kind" only describes that wood enters into any product. opportunity costs ask which product does not arise. Tables exclude shelves from the same batch. Material consumption alone does not cancel the rivalry of the lines. Option A against option B remains.

The statement is false.

Raw materials are not available indefinitely. Alternative applications (tables or shelves) force the decision on what the wood is used for. This is scarcity in the company and the reason to plan the use.

Limited oak is the raw material that is not available indefinitely. Carpentry must decide what it is using, although there is the other line. This is scarcity in the company and the reason for planning. Without this decision, there would be no economy on wood, only consumption.

The statement is true.

title: Air, water, soil and sinks
context: Evaluate the following statements dealing with scarce natural resources:
statements: Time, money, means of production, natural resources and sinks are resources whose use includes decisions against alternative uses.
The importance of scarce resources is not apparent, especially in the case of air, water and soil, because these goods grow indefinitely.
Short-term decisions can cause long-term environmental damage and environmental problems and economic challenges.
Sustainable economic activity means maximising only one's own benefits and eliminating effects on other people and the environment.
Companies can only succeed in the long term if they sustainably manage and involve the effects of their decisions on others responsibly.
tactical_explanations:
The list of resources to be used specifically includes time, money, means of production, natural resources and sinks. Any use for Option A is also the decision against Option B and generates opportunity costs. Natural resources are in the same logic.

Taking down, for example, the absorption capacity of air, water and soil, is part of the resource list in addition to time and money. Any load or use for Option A excludes different uses or less load than Option B. opportunity costs arise here as a lost benefit of abandoned use.

The statement holds the list and the A-against-B logic together.

The statement is true.

Especially in the case of air, water and soil, the importance of scarce resources becomes clear. Unlimited regrowth is not the statement of the text. The focus is on the burden and use of these media, because they are scarce and vulnerable.

Especially in the use and the exposure of air, water and soil, the importance of scarce resources becomes clear, not the opposite. Unlimited regrowth would deny scarcity, especially where the presentation sharpens it. Short-term decisions can damage these media. The justification "unlimited regrowth" does not bear.

The statement is false.

Climate science analyses show that short-term decisions can not only cause long-term environmental damage, but often already present environmental problems and economic challenges. The doubling of later and now is essential.

Not only long-term ecological damage, but often already today environmental problems and economic challenges: the sentence has two time horizons. Whoever sees the distant future undermines the present side. The statement mentions both and thus remains at the climate science point of the section.

The statement is true.

Sustainable economic management therefore means not only thinking about one's own benefits, but also including impacts on other people and the environment, today and for future generations. "Only one's own benefits, leaving the environment out" is the opposite of the text.

Not only to think about your own benefits, but to include impacts on other people and the environment, today and for future generations: this is the definition of sustainable economic activity in this text. Maximizing only your own benefits with the omission of the effects is the rejected attitude, not the demanded.

The statement is false.

All economic operators, including companies, can only be successful in the long term if they sustainably manage and take into account the effects responsibly. Examples are environmentally friendly ingredients and equipment, energy-efficient processes or sustainable logistics.

Long-term success is linked to sustainable business, including for companies. Responsible inclusion of effects can be achieved through ingredients, equipment, energy-efficient processes or logistics. The statement repeats the success condition of the section without trying to cycle or market prices.

The statement is true.

title: Three dimensions of sustainability
context: Evaluate the following statements on sustainable thinking and business:
statements: Sustainable thinking involves ecological, social and economic considerations.
In this understanding, sustainability only includes the ecological dimension, economy and social issues.
Economic and social objectives must also be achieved for social cohesion and for the acceptance and success of environmental measures.
Sustainable action aims to play out ecology against economics and to put social goals into action.
Environmentally friendly ingredients, energy-efficient production processes or sustainable logistics are examples of how to include effects on others.
tactical_explanations:
The presentation explicitly links the three sides: in addition to ecological and social and economic considerations. Sustainability is not a pure environmental label here, but a composite understanding. The statement reflects this breadth.

Ecology alone would not bear social cohesion and the acceptance of ecological measures if economic and social goals were not to be met. Therefore, sustainable thinking involves the three considerations. The statement is the first half of this link and remains.

The statement is true.

Sustainability encompasses and links the three dimensions of ecology, economy and social affairs. Those who leave out economy and social affairs, remove two of the three pillars. This contradicts the textbook understanding.

Three dimensions: ecology, economy and social affairs. Outside of leaving two dimensions destroys the understanding in which sustainability includes and links. The section builds sustainability precisely not as a pure environmental issue. The limitation to ecology is wrong.

The statement is false.

Social cohesion and the acceptance of ecological measures are dependent on the achievement of economic and social goals. Ecology alone, without these goals, does not support the text's argumentation. The statement makes the reason.

Acceptance and success of ecological measures depend on economic and social goals. Cohesion is the social reason, not an addition. Anyone who isolates ecological goals underestimates this condition. The statement gives the reason for the textbook.

The statement is true.

Sustainable action aims to reconcile the three dimensions, not to play out ecology against economics and to put social issues back. Stinting would be imbalance, the goal is to achieve harmony.

To reconcile the goal of sustainable action is to play out and to put things in balance. Setting ecology against economy and putting social issues back is contrary to the three dimensions. The direction of the sentence is reversed to the text.

The statement is false.

The inclusion of effects on others is made more concrete: environmentally friendly ingredients and equipment, energy-efficient production processes, sustainable logistics solutions. The examples mentioned are the paths of responsible business.

Ingredients, resources, energy-efficient production, sustainable logistics: these are the concrete ways to take effect on others. They show that sustainable business management is not just a headline. The examples are from the section and support the statement.

The statement is true.

title: Reflektierte Entscheidung unter Knappheit
context: Evaluate the following statements on the link between scarcity, opportunity costs and sustainable economic development:
statements: opportunity costs include what you have given up or what you have given up on, because you have chosen an option and excluded others.
An economic decision is only well thought out when one is aware of these consequences, including the opportunity costs.
Short-term own benefits without looking at future generations already fully fulfils the requirement of sustainable business.
Efficient use of resources requires recognition of scarcity as a reality.
Once a company produces energy efficient, social and economic goals can be ignored, because one dimension of sustainability is sufficient.
tactical_explanations:
The consequence of the choice is thus expressed: opportunity costs include the given, because a certain option excludes others. It is the waiver that arises with the decision itself, not only a later invoice. The statement follows this provision.

The options not selected are excluded. opportunity costs are precisely this exclusion in income or benefits. The provision is based on the consequences of the decision, not on a later tax return. Whoever chooses A bears the waiver of B, and this waiver has a name.

The statement is true.

The decision is well thought out and reflected only with awareness of the consequences. These consequences include the opportunity costs. Anyone who sees only the immediate advantage of the chosen option and hides the waiver does not fulfil this criterion.

Without this consciousness, the choice remains unreflected: one sees the advantage of A and hides B. The section demands both. The economic decision is well thought out only when the opportunity costs are thought as a consequence. The statement sets this threshold right.

The statement is true.

Sustainable economic activity involves other people and the environment, both today and for future generations. Only the short-term own benefit is exactly what the presentation describes as insufficient, because short-term decisions can create ecological and economic problems.

The next generations are next to those affected today. Short-term own benefit without this view is the pattern that can generate ecological damage and today's environmental problems. Sustainable economic activity would only be fully fulfilled with the inclusion of other people and the environment in both time horizons.

The statement declares the requirement met, although the core is missing.

The statement is false.

The essence of economic activity is the recognition of scarcity as a reality and of a social organization that allows the most efficient use of resources. Without this recognition, planning of the operation remains empty. Efficiency is at the recognised limit.

Recognition of scarcity as a reality comes before the organization efficient use. Whoever denies borders does not plan the use and does not allow efficiency. Samuelson and Nordhaus bind both together. The prerequisite in the statement is this order.

The statement is true.

Sustainability links ecology, economics and social affairs; sustainable action aims to reconcile them. Energy efficiency primarily serves the ecological (and partly economic) side, but does not replace social and economic goals that are necessary for cohesion and acceptance. One dimension is not enough.

One dimension is not enough because sustainability links the three dimensions. Energy efficiency can help ecologically and economically while leaving social goals open. Economic and social goals must be achieved for cohesion and acceptance. Ignoring after a technical measure contradicts the agreement.

The statement is false.

title: What, how and for whom
context: Evaluate the following statements on the basic questions of economics:
statements: The current decision on limited resources raises the question of how and for whom to produce in what quantity and quality.
Once something is produced, the question of who is produced for is eliminated, because then everyone is supplied.
The basic questions include what is to be bought or exchanged.
How is produced is not one of the basic questions; the only decisive factor is what is.
The quantity and quality of production are the same basic question, not just the quantity.
tactical_explanations:
The main questions are: what should be produced in what quantity and in what quality? The sentence completely reproduces this list without replacing the market price. The list is based on the basic questions of production, including the question of production: what should be produced in what quantity and in what quality?

The statement is true.

The basic question explicitly mentions what is needed in addition to what and how. Production without the addressee would not be a complete allocation: the same machine hours can result from children's bicycles, steel carriers or catering depending on who is planned for.

Supplying all does not automatically follow from any output. The claim that the question will fail as soon as anything arises will remove some of the basic questions.

Those who take any good off the belt have not yet decided which needs are met and in what quantity and quality. Shortness forces precisely to choose between possible recipients and uses. All would be supplied only if resources were unlimited. That is not the case. The question for whom therefore remains part of the economy.

The statement is false.

Next to the production side is the use side: What should be bought or exchanged? Private households do not have unlimited money or other means of exchange. Therefore, the question of buying and exchanging is a fundamental question of economics, not just a taste note after production.

The statement is true.

The way in which production is made is in the same list as what and for-us. Machines, labor force and processes are scarce means; their choice is the "how" question. Whoever only lets what apply, cuts the way in which it is used. A company such as Rosenbauer or Do&Co not only decides on the product, but also on the processes, quality of the means and organization.

The limitation to what alone is wrong.

The question of how is not a technical game outside the economy. Alternative methods use the same scarce resources differently. Therefore, as in the basic questions, as soon as it has to be planned, what limited resources are used for. Just asking what would mean to consider the route of use unlimited.

The statement is false.

In what quantity and in what quality: both parts are on a fundamental question. Leaving out quality would mean planning scarce means only by quantity. Good performance is part of the same decision, not a later piece of jewellery. The sentence holds the double.

The statement is true.

title: Family budget of the Meiers
context: Evaluate the following statements on scarcity in private household:
statements: The Meiers have to decide with a certain family budget how much they spend on housing, mobility, daily shopping, saving and holidays.
If they have paid the rent, the remaining budget items are available indefinitely.
More for the car means less room for the same pot, for example for saving or for holiday.
With scarce financial resources, only businesses have to consume; households only consume.
The economic situation here means planning the use of the limited budget.
tactical_explanations:
A family has a certain budget, not an infinite cash register. Living, car or bicycle, shopping, saving and holiday access the same limited amount. This budget example shows scarcity: several possible uses, a decision on the use.

The statement is true.

Rent is a use, not the end of scarcity. What remains after the transfer is still finite and must be distributed to mobility, purchases, savings and holidays. Unlimited would be the remaining items only if money were no longer a scarce resource. Paid housing does not lift the limit of the family budget.

The Meiers continue to operate after the rent, only with a smaller remainder.

No private household has unlimited money or other means of exchange. The division of housing, mobility, purchases, saving, holidays remains a division of the same pot. Whoever treats a post as done and declares the rest infinite confuses a booking with Infinity. Shortage is in the budget overall, not only before the first transfer.

The statement is false.

The same Euro cannot be extra into the car and extra into the savings account at the same time. Alternative uses of the same budget generate the waiver. More mobility reduces savings or vacations because the funds are scarce.

The statement is true.

The resources on both sides are scarce: for households and companies. That's why the Meiers must also operate, not just a factory. Consumption does not replace planning; consumption in particular competes for limited resources. The restriction on companies alone is wrong.

All economic operators must decide what they are using limited resources for, which would be alternative to use, and we must all manage. A household that is only consuming and not planning would deny scarcity. The distribution of roles between producers and consumers is cutting off the budget side of the scarcity that the theory explicitly calls.

The statement is false.

Because funds are scarce, their use must be planned precisely. In the household, the family budget is this financial limit. Living, mobility, purchases, saving and holidays are the rival uses that are decided upon. That is economics in the sense of scarcity.

The statement is true.

title: Means of production at AGRANA and Do&Co
context: Evaluate the following statements on scarcity in the company:
statements: A company such as AGRANA or Do&Co must clarify what it can produce and what means of production are available in what quantity and quality.
The means of production that the company can afford is part of the scarcity decision.
Financial resources may be invested entirely without considering current payments, because investing is not an alternative to liquidity.
Decisions on the use of limited resources are at the heart of the economy.
Known brands can produce unlimited quantities of goods as soon as customers wait.
tactical_explanations:
Companies like AGRANA, Rosenbauer, Voest, Do&Co or woom are similar to a household, only on the production side. What is and can be produced? What means are available in what quality and quantity? This is the company example of scarcity.

The statement is true.

Besides the desire to produce counts which means of production can be afforded. Price, available quantity and quality of machines, intermediate consumption and labour force limit the feasible. This is part of the central decision on the use of resources, not marginal note of accounting.

The statement is true.

The theory asks explicitly: How much can be invested, how much should remain available for current payments? Investment and liquidity are alternative uses of the same financial means. Anyone who invests everything and ignores payments misses this rivalry.

The claim that investing is not an alternative to liquidity is exactly the scarcity of the company.

Financial resources are not available indefinitely. The same amount cannot be fully available in investments and fully as means of payment. Current payments are one use, investing another. Without this alternative there would be no decision on the use of funds. The sentence denies the alternative and thus the center of the economy.

The statement is false.

It is not just the possession of sugar factories or kitchens that makes up economies, but the current choice of what limited resources are used for. There, the focus lies on: planning, deciding, excluding other options.

The statement is true.

No company can produce unlimited quantities of goods. Raw materials, machines, labour force and financial resources remain scarce, even with a well-known brand. Demand or queues do not create infinite means of production. Infinity would only be given if goods were available indefinitely, which the starting point expressly denies.

Customers can increase their desire for more output, but they do not extend machine hours, raw materials or equity into infinity. AGRANA and Do&Co must continue to clarify what they can afford. Size and awareness do not change the recognition of scarcity into infinity. The production limit remains the reality at which the economy is managed.

The statement is false.

title: Samuelson: Knappheit anerkennen
context: Evaluate the following statements the essence of economic activity after Samuelson and Nordhaus:
statements: The essence of economic activity is the recognition of scarcity as a reality and a social organization that allows the most efficient use of resources.
Those who deny scarcity still automatically manage as efficiently as possible.
This resource use is constantly linked to many decisions and actions of economic operators.
Efficient deployment is created by itself as soon as any resources are available without anyone deciding.
Economics means using limited resources planned because alternative uses exist.
tactical_explanations:
Samuelson and Nordhaus grasp the essence of this: Recognize scarcity as reality and a social organization that allows the most efficient use of resources. Without this recognition, planning remains empty. The sentence gives the quotation factually.

The statement is true.

Efficiency does not arise by itself from denial. Anyone who does not recognise the border does not plan the deployment and does not allow an organization to use efficiently. Automatic efficiency would then be an empty hope, not a mechanism. The essence of economics begins with recognition, not with its refusal.

Without recognition of scarcity as a reality, there is no planning of the use and no social organization that allows efficiency. Denial means pretending to be unlimitedly prepared for raw materials, labor power and money. Then the decision on what means are not taken. This is precisely the decision that is at the heart of the decision.

Anyone who cuts them does not manage efficiently, but not in the spirit of the text.

The statement is false.

The use of resources does not remain a unique formula, but depends on many actions. Buying, selling, trading, investing and convincing are the everyday form of this choice. Participants are constantly deciding, not only once in the year of foundation.

The statement is true.

The availability of resources does not replace the decision. Without choice between alternatives, there is no planned use. Efficiency requires someone to recognise and organize the scarce stock. Resources that no one has yet been allocated are not yet an economy.

Samuelson binds efficiency to organization and recognition, not to mere presence. Machines in the hall that no one plans to solve the basic questions do not. What, how, for whom, quantity and quality remain unanswered as long as no one decides. The sentence implies automatic where the representation requires actions of economic operators.

The statement is false.

Because funds are scarce and alternative applications exist, all economic operators must decide and plan. This is the definition of business in this section, not a special case of large corporations.

The statement is true.

title: Kaufen, Verkaufen, Handeln, Investieren
context: Evaluate the following statements to the economy as a network of human activities:
statements: The economy is an enormously complex entity of various human activities such as buying, selling, trading, investing and persuading.
Economics consists exclusively of production in factories; buying and convincing do not count.
Households and businesses are scarce on both sides and must plan to use their funds.
Convincing is not part of the economy because the economy consists only of machine hours.
The exchange of goods for money would be relatively easy if both were available indefinitely.
tactical_explanations:
Samuelson and Nordhaus describe the economy as a complex entity of human activities and call it buying, selling, trading, investing and convincing. The use of resources appears in exactly these actions, not just in a piece list.

The statement is true.

The list quoted is deliberately broad. Anyone who only lets the factory apply, cuts off buying, selling, trading, investing and convincing. Households decide what is bought or exchanged; companies invest and convince customers. Production is a part, not the only activity.

Only factory narrows the structure, which considers the representation as enormously complex.

Economic operators are acting continuously, not only on the assembly line. The exchange of goods for money, the investment of financial means and the persuasion of others are mentioned in the same sentence. A definition that only knows production halls would hide the household side and large parts of the company side.

This contradicts the enumeration and the focus: decisions on scarce resources in many forms.

The statement is false.

The resources that households and companies have are scarce on both sides. Therefore, they need to be managed, so their deployment is planned precisely. The two-sidedness is the characteristic, not a one-way from the factory to the customer.

The statement is true.

The list of activities also includes investment and action. Machine hours are a scarce resource, not the definition of the economy. Anyone who convinces, because only technology counts, confuses a means of production with the entire structure of human activities.

Convincing is explicitly mentioned in the textbook quotation. It is one of the actions with which resource use is organized, for example when a company gains customers or employees for a use of scarce funds. Machine hours do not explain why buy, sell and trade. The narrowing on technology drops the complexity that Samuelson emphasizes.

The statement is false.

If there were goods and money without a limit, there would be no compulsion to choose. The exchange would then be a mere liquidation. The starting point of the section is precisely this: relatively simple it would be only under Infinity, which does not apply in reality.

The statement is true.

title: Mila: bookstore or swimming academy
context: Evaluate the following statements on opportunity costs scarce Saturday hours:
statements: Milas Saturday morning is short: she cannot spend the same time in the bookstore and full in the swimming academy.
If it chooses the Academy, opportunity costs include lost income of overlapping shift.
If she chooses the shift, she is part of the opportunity costs training and a possible sporting opportunity, even if this chance is uncertain.
Because a scholarship or a sporting opportunity may only occur, this benefit must never count as opportunity costs.
Mila does not have to be a private person; scarcity of time applies only to companies.
tactical_explanations:
Time is mentioned in the resource list and is not available indefinitely. Bookstore and academy are alternative uses of the same morning. Full parallel use would pretend infinity. Mila must decide what the short time is spent on.

The statement is true.

Option Academy means abandoning option layer. The lost yield of the abandoned alternative is the income that would have been generated in the bookstore. This is the definition: yield of B, which is dispensed with because one chooses A.

The statement is true.

Conversely, the academy lacks what the shift is pushing: training time and a possible sporting perspective. Unachieved benefits must be uncertain. The theory explicitly allows for securities to be made that you might be able to achieve profits; this potential, then not achieved, return remains opportunity costs.

Uncertainty does not take the character as a benefit of the abandoned alternative.

The statement is true.

Perhaps in the founding example of the securities, part of the argument is not an exclusion. An uncertain, unaccompanied benefit remains the benefit of the abandoned alternative. Never counting would be an absolute rule that does not set out the presentation.

Those who make uncertainty a ban could also no longer read the potential security gains as opportunity costs of the foundation.

Note: Uncertainty does not change the definition to zero; it describes the lost yield that might have occurred.

The Academy can offer an opportunity that cannot be safely expressed in euros. Nevertheless, it is option B as soon as Mila chooses the shift. The definition does not mention the benefits achieved, not only safe cash inputs. A ban on uncertain sizes would be narrower than the theory and would eliminate leisure value and perhaps profits.

The statement is false.

All economic operators must decide what they are using limited resources for. We must therefore all manage. Private person, household, youth: the status does not cancel out scarcity of time. To name only companies, the household and person side, where the chapter Time and Learning explicitly explains.

Student, apprentice, household, company: resources are scarce on both sides and with all economic operators. Surprising uses of the same morning force the choice. An exception for private individuals would reverse the feature we all need to manage. Mila plans to use her hours as well as a company's use of labor force.

The statement is false.

title: Halbe Beete, Nachbars Wiese
context: Evaluate the following statements to the allocation of scarce garden area:
statements: If the family divides the scarce area into beds and meadows, it still manages: the use of the limited area is planned.
If a flower meadow grows with the neighbour, the own area becomes unlimited and the family no longer has to decide.
Compost instead of purchased earth does not change that at the same place there are not full beds and a full meadow.
The opportunity costs of the beds are the gardening hours of the beds themselves, not the lost use of the meadow.
Beauty of the unchosen meadow may be included in the opportunity costs, even without selling the flowers.
tactical_explanations:
The area remains limited; a larger proportion of meadows displaces the bed area and vice versa. Economics means to plan the use precisely. The family decides for which sections are used, although alternative divisions exist.

The statement is true.

Shortage is not in the neighbourhood landscape of the household itself. The own parcel is not infinite, just because flowers are standing elsewhere. Alternative uses of the own area remain. The family must continue to decide, otherwise it denies the reality of scarcity on its side.

No private household has unlimited area, money or other means. The neighboring property is not their resource and does not replace the choice between bed and meadow. Unlimitedness through foreign gardens would be a category error: economic activity affects one's own limited stock. The obligation to decide does not cease by looking over the fence.

The statement is false.

Costless of an intermediate supply, here compost, does not extinguish the rivalry of the surface. At the same place, full beds and full meadow continue to exclude. opportunity costs are dependent on the abandoned use of the scarce area, not on whether earth was bought.

The garden example in theory argues about the same location, not the price of the substrate.

The statement is true.

The beet is chosen; the meadow is omitted. The price or effort of A is not the definition of opportunity costs. The lost yields or the ungained benefits of B, here beauty and recovery of the meadow, remain decisive. Gardening hours of the beet are effort of the chosen option, not the waiver.

The purchase price or work of the chosen object is the expenditure for A. opportunity costs are the benefit of B. Both can contain effort or Euro and still remain different terms. Whoever makes the bed work a definition, fails to give up the meadow at the same place. Exactly this is how the theory separates Option A from Option B.

The statement is false.

No benefit has to be a market price. The meadow creates beauty; if the family dispenses with it in favour of the beds, this benefit is the abandoned alternative. Joy and recreation are a value, even if it cannot be expressed in money value.

The statement is true.

title: Foundation instead of securities and world tour
context: Evaluate the following statements on alternative use of money:
statements: If Mira invests available money in the creation of a company, it can no longer put the same amount into certain securities.
Similarly, it cannot spend the same amount on training or a world trip after the establishment of the company.
Because a foundation is future-oriented, the opportunity costs of the unselected plants are automatically zero.
The opportunity costs of the establishment may include the loss of potential profits from securities.
A mental purpose commitment for the company cancels all alternative uses of money.
tactical_explanations:
It is precisely this chain that is called: putting money into a foundation means not investing the same amount in certain securities that might make profits, and one use excludes the other.

The statement is true.

Likewise, the money can no longer be spent on an education or a world trip. Training and travel are other alternative uses of the same scarce financial means. After the commitment to the foundation they are excluded.

The statement is true.

Future orientation does not change the definition. opportunity costs are the lost return on the abandoned alternative, for example possible securities gains or the benefits of travel and training. They do not become zero just because the foundation looks forward. Zero would only exist without alternative use.

Securities, training and travel are just such alternatives. Mira's goal in the future of her company does not change the scarcity of the amount nor the lost earnings of the unselected investment. Future does not redeem the waiver. Automatically zero would be only a world without option B, which explicitly mentions the presentation.

The statement is false.

Perhaps earning profits is explicitly part of the securities example. This unearned income is opportunity costs of the foundation, provided the securities are the abandoned alternative. Uncertainty does not take their character as lost income.

The statement is true.

An etiquette for the company is not a lifting of the scarcity. As long as the amount could be stuck in securities, training or travel, there are alternative uses. Therefore, money must be managed, so planning and deciding. Ending in the head does not replace the reality of limited funds.

As long as other uses are conceivable, it must be decided what the amount is used for. Economics means exactly this planning. A mental dedication does not change that the same euro does not finance in parallel company, study and world trip fully. Alternative uses remain until the decision excludes them, not even by a label.

The statement is false.

title: Bezdeka, Ihlenfeld and the next alternative
context: Evaluate the following statements to the opportunity costs in the company at the example of the Woom founders:
statements: The time and energy of the founders are scarce resources; other professional activities or leisure were alternative uses during the construction.
If both founders have enjoyed building, their opportunity costs are automatically zero because satisfaction erases any waiver.
The opportunity costs are dependent on people: depending on what everyone has given up, not the sum of all possible life paths.
Because a GmbH later exists, leisure benefits of the founding years do not count, because companies only know Euro.
The decision to start up would be well thought out only if the abandoned possibilities were thought of as consequences.
tactical_explanations:
Christian Bezdeka and Marcus Ihlenfeld put a lot of time and energy into the building. Of course, they could have pursued another occupation during this time, whether it was another professional activity to earn money, be it a leisure activity. Time and energy are scarce resources with alternatives.

The statement is true.

Personal joy is the benefit of the chosen line and can explain the choice. It does not calculate the lost yield of the other line against zero. When building which counts leisure value besides lost content, without one of the sizes extinguishing the other. Joy and opportunity costs consist side by side. Automatically zero would be only one world without option B.

Satisfaction at the chosen path is not the eraser for the excluded occupation. The definition measures the not achieved benefit of B, not the mood at A. Whoever declares joy to zero setting, could consider any pleasant foundation to be opportunity free.

The representation does the opposite: he just calls the abandoned possibilities as opportunity costs, regardless of the enthusiasm for Woom.

The statement is false.

Depending on what the two have given up to build, these abandoned possibilities represent their opportunity costs. The formulation is dependent on people and situation. Not every conceivable use counts, but the actually displaced next best alternative, not a catalogue of all life paths.

The statement is true.

It is important that joy and recreation are a value, even if it cannot be expressed in money value. The later legal form GmbH does not change this evaluation of the founding years retrospectively into only euros. Companies as an organization do not replace the time decision of the people who build.

During the construction the time of the founders was bound, not that of an already finished balance sheet. Leisure benefits count in the definition as not achieved benefit. Euro-only would be the narrow rule, which the representation at this point just expands. Existence of the GmbH afterwards is the result of the choice, not the proof that only salaries were allowed to count.

The statement is false.

Economic decisions are only taken carefully and reflected upon when one is aware of the consequences. Opportunity costs include: what one has given up because other options have been excluded. For the founders, this means thinking about salary or recovery as abandoned possibilities, not just seeing the product idea.

The statement is true.

title: Voluntary or paid shift
context: Evaluate the following statements on opportunity costs of an unpaid alternative:
statements: If Simon takes honorary office on the same Saturday, opportunity costs include the lost income of the overlapping paid shift.
Because volunteering does not pay anything, this election does not result in opportunity costs.
