If Simon stays in the shift, the opportunity costs are the unsuccessful benefits from volunteering.
opportunity costs may be stated in euro only; other benefits do not count.
As a young person, Simon still has to manage with a short time and choose between uses.
tactical_explanations:
Option Voluntary means waiver of option shift, provided both claim the same Saturday. The lost earnings of the abandoned alternative are the earnings of the shift. This is the financial side of opportunity costs, analogous to the abandonment of another professional activity in the company's construction.

The statement is true.

Zero pay on the chosen way is not zero waiver. The shift that Simon can no longer afford falls away. opportunity costs are the lost benefits of the alternative, not the payout of the chosen employment. Unpaid does not erase this yield. Note: The next best use given is decisive, not the cash flow of the selected option.

Unpaid is the volunteer's account, not without an alternative. Simon could work the shift at the same time. This lost income is option B. The definition does not ask whether Option A pays a salary, but what is dispensed with in favour of A. Zero pay on A does not extinguish B. Costless of the chosen act is no free letter against scarcity of time.

The statement is false.

If he stays in the shift, he excludes honorary service. The sense, joy or recovery of volunteering are benefits he does not achieve. Also, not simply in money-capable sizes count, as in the leisure value in the founder example.

The statement is true.

Time, recovery, experience and other benefits can be included in the opportunity costs. It is true that joy and recovery are a value, even if it is not so easy to express itself in monetary value. The rule only Euro is too narrow. Always only Euro, never other dimensions would be the absolute trap.

The definition does not explicitly allow for the benefits achieved. Voluntary sense belongs to the same open category of benefits as recreation. A rule that only allows euro is narrower than the determination of opportunity costs. Anyone who cuts other dimensions can no longer read the word example with leisure value.

The statement is false.

Being young does not stop scarcity. His hours are limited, shift and volunteering overlap, alternative possibilities of time remain. All economic operators, including him, must decide what the scarce resource time is used for.

The statement is true.

title: Household and holding in front of the same border
context: Evaluate the following statements to compare budget and operational resources:
statements: The same logic is faced with households and businesses: limited resources, alternative uses, decision on use.
Once a household consumes and produces a farm, scarcity is eliminated on one side.
The basic questions combine what is produced with the question of what is bought or exchanged.
Raw materials, machinery, labour force and financial resources are not available indefinitely and must be used in planning.
Only the state must operate; private households and businesses are excluded from scarcity.
tactical_explanations:
On both sides, resources are scarce. The household divides the family budget into housing, mobility, purchases, savings and holidays. The company clarifies what it can produce and what means of production it can afford. Alternative applications force the same decision-making logic.

The statement is true.

Consumption and production are two locations of the same scarcity, not its abolition. No household has unlimited means of exchange, no enterprise unlimited output. Whoever declares a side to be infinite, because it consumes or produces, misses the characteristic: resources are scarce on both sides. Role change does not erase the border.

Exchange would be simple only if goods and money were unlimited. That is not the case. Consumption means distributing limited money on purchases. Production means using limited means of production. Both actions are economies. The claim that one of the sides is free of scarcity by their role contradicts the two-sided nature of the section.

The statement is false.

From the current decision on limited resources, both basic questions follow: the production question (what, how, for whom, quantity, quality) and the question of what should be bought or exchanged. Household and operation are connected in this pair, not separated into two sciences.

The statement is true.

The list is deliberately broad: raw materials, machines, labor force, financial resources and much more. They must be used to manage, that is, to plan their deployment precisely. Planning is the result of the lack of infinity.

The statement is true.

We all have to operate. The characteristic is that all economic operators have alternative uses, and there is no exception to the state and to the exemption of households and businesses. Private households and companies are just the two sides where scarcity is explained.

The state as its own player in the cycle belongs in a later chapter. Here, households and companies bear the examples. They would exclude the chapter. All economic operators decide what limited resources are used for. The absolute exception is wrong.

The statement is false.

title: Irrigation: field A or field B
context: Evaluate the following statements on the scarce use of natural resources in production:
statements: Limited irrigation water is a scarce resource and must be split between two fields or assigned to a field.
Because water occurs in nature, there are no opportunity costs between the fields.
If the holding chooses field A, the opportunity costs are the sum of the yields of both fields as if both were fully irrigated.
If he chooses field A, the opportunity costs are the lost yield or benefit that field B would have provided.
Raw materials are not available indefinitely; therefore their use must be planned.
tactical_explanations:
Natural resources are included in the resource list alongside time, money and means of production. Water for the fields is scarce as soon as both areas cannot be fully supplied. Alternative uses force the decision on what the limited amount is used for.

The statement is true.

Origin from nature does not stop scarcity. Air, water and soil are precisely the media, where the importance of scarce resources becomes clear. Two fields rival the same limited amount of water. Option A against option B remains. Occurrence in nature is not a free letter for Infinity.

The importance of dealing with scarce resources is particularly evident when it comes to the use and load of air, water and soil. Anyone who declares water inexhaustible because it is natural denies this very point. opportunity costs arise as soon as the irrigation of A excludes that of B. Naturalness of the resource does not change the definition.

The statement is false.

Adding A plus B would treat both yields as if they were attainable at the same time. However, the water is not enough for both. opportunity costs measure the lost yield of the abandoned alternative, not the sum of both projects. Addition repeats the mistake of summing up all discarded options.

The sum of both fields assumes that the waiver is both at the same time. The waiver is only the unchosen field. The scarce amount prohibits the irrigating of two areas at the same time. The addition does not measure the next best alternative, but an unreachable double operation.

The statement is false.

opportunity costs are the yield of option B, which is dispensed with because you have chosen option A. A is the irrigation of field A, B is the lost benefit of field B. Not the pump calculation of A alone, but the abandoned field load.

The statement is true.

Raw materials, machines, labor, financial resources and much more are not available indefinitely. Therefore, the use must be planned precisely with them. In this logic, irrigation water is a raw material or a natural resource.

The statement is true.

title: Confronting the Consequences of the Election
context: Evaluate the following statements to reflect economic decisions:
statements: opportunity costs include what you have given up or what you have given up on, because you have chosen an option and excluded others.
An economic decision is only well thought out when one is aware of these consequences, including the opportunity costs.
Anyone who sees only the immediate advantage of the chosen option already fully meets the criterion of the reflected decision.
Any attachment of time, money, means of production or natural resources to Option A is also the decision against Option B.
Once a decision has been taken, the excluded options may be treated as never existing.
tactical_explanations:
The consequence of the choice is thus taken: opportunity costs include the given up because a certain option excludes others. It is the waiver that arises with the decision itself, not only a later invoice.

The statement is true.

The decision is well thought out and reflected only with awareness of the consequences. These consequences include the opportunity costs. Anyone who only sees the advantage of A and hides B does not fulfil this criterion.

The statement is true.

The immediate advantage of A without a view of the waiver is precisely the unreflected pattern. The section requires to be aware of the consequences; the opportunity costs are included. The criterion would only be fully fulfilled if the given is thought. The sentence declares the requirement fulfilled, although the core is missing.

Without this awareness, the choice remains unreflected. One sees the advantage of the chosen layer, the foundation or the bed and hides training, securities or the meadow. The economic decision is well thought out only when the opportunity costs are thought as a consequence. The advantage of A alone is not enough.

The statement is false.

Any decision to use resources for something, for example Option A, means simultaneously the decision against an alternative use, for example Option B. This creates opportunity costs. The A-against-B logic applies to time, money, means of production, natural resources and sinks.

The statement is true.

Excluded does not mean that they never existed. opportunity costs measure precisely the benefits of the excluded option. Treating them as never existing would make the waiver invisible and the reflected decision impossible. The alternatives were real and were not chosen; that remains the consequence.

The options were open during the election. After binding the scarce resource, they are not undone afterwards, but abandoned. Whoever declares them to be never existing, cancels the definition of opportunity costs. Consciousness for consequences presupposes seeing B as a abandoned possibility, not as an illusion.

The statement is false.

title: Today and future generations
context: Evaluate the following statements on sustainable management within the meaning of this Section:
statements: Sustainable economic activity means not only thinking about your own benefits, but also including impacts on other people and the environment, today and for future generations.
Short-term own benefits without looking at other and later generations already fully fulfils the requirement of sustainable economic development.
Short-term decisions can cause long-term environmental damage and environmental problems and economic challenges.
Companies can ignore effects on others because long-term success depends only on their own benefits.
Environmentally friendly ingredients and equipment, energy-efficient processes or sustainable logistics are examples of how to include effects on others.
tactical_explanations:
Not only to think about your own benefits, but to include impacts on other people and the environment, both today and for future generations: this is the determination of sustainable economic activity in this section. Both time horizons are parallel.

The statement is true.

Only the short-term own benefit is exactly what the presentation describes as insufficient. Short-term decisions can generate environmental damage and already today's environmental problems as well as economic challenges. Fully fulfilled would be sustainable economic management only with the inclusion of other people and the environment in both time horizons.

The next generation is standing next to those who are affected today. Whoever isolates their own benefit follows the attitude that rejects the presentation. The requirement is not fulfilled if others and the environment stay away. Short-termness here is the risk pattern, not the proof of good economics. The sentence reverses the definition.

The statement is false.

Climate science analyses show that short-term decisions can not only cause long-term environmental damage, but often already present environmental problems and economic challenges. The doubling of later and now is essential.

The statement is true.

All economic operators, including companies, can only be successful in the long term if they sustainably manage and take into account the effects of their decisions on others responsibly. Ignoring the effects contradicts this condition of success.

Long-term success is bound to sustainable business, especially for companies. Responsible inclusion can be based on ingredients, resources, energy-efficient processes or logistics. The claim that success depends only on its own benefits and effects should be ignored is the opposite to the section.

The statement is false.

The inclusion of effects on others is made more concrete: environmentally friendly ingredients and equipment, energy-efficient production processes, sustainable logistics solutions. The above-mentioned paths are examples of responsible business in the company.

The statement is true.

title: Ecology, Economy and Social Affairs
context: Evaluate the following statements on the three dimensions of sustainable thinking:
statements: Sustainable thinking involves ecological, social and economic considerations.
In this understanding, sustainability only includes the ecological dimension; economy and social affairs remain outside.
Economic and social objectives must also be achieved for social cohesion and for the acceptance and success of environmental measures.
Sustainable action aims to play out ecology against economy and to set social goals.
Sustainability encompasses and links the three dimensions of ecology, economy and social affairs and aims to reconcile them.
tactical_explanations:
The presentation explicitly links the three sides: in addition to ecological and social and economic considerations. Sustainability is not a pure environmental label here, but a composite understanding. The statement reflects this breadth.

The statement is true.

Sustainability encompasses and links the three dimensions of ecology, economy and social affairs. Those who leave out economy and social affairs, remove two of the three pillars. The section does not build sustainability as an isolated environmental issue. The limitation to ecology is wrong.

Three dimensions: ecology, economy and social affairs. Outside of leaving two dimensions destroys the understanding in which sustainability includes and links. Ecology alone would not bear cohesion and acceptance of ecological measures if economic and social goals were not to be met. Therefore, narrowing is inadmissible.

The statement is false.

Social cohesion and the acceptance of environmental measures are dependent on economic and social goals being achieved. Ecology alone, without these goals, does not support the text's argumentation. The statement makes the statement without seeking later chapters on state or cycle.

The statement is true.

Sustainable action aims to reconcile the three dimensions, not to play out ecology against economics and to put social issues back. Stinting would be imbalance, the goal is harmony. The direction of the sentence is reversed to the text.

The goal is to reconcile each other. Playing out and setting aside would be conflict instead of linking. Anyone who sets ecological goals against company accounts and sacrifices social goals misses the three dimensions. The section requires coordination, not ranking with residual social items.

The statement is false.

In this context, the three dimensions of sustainable action are to be reconciled. The sentence holds together determination and goal without bringing Brundtland formulas or later chapters into the Earth system via embedding.

The statement is true.

title: Lowering, efficiency and consistency
context: Evaluate the following statements at the end of the section on scarcity and sustainable decision-making:
statements: Time, money, means of production, natural resources and sinks are resources whose use includes decisions against alternative uses.
Efficient use of resources requires recognition of scarcity as a reality.
Once a company produces energy efficient, social and economic goals can be ignored, because one dimension of sustainability is sufficient.
The importance of scarce resources is particularly evident in the use and exposure of air, water and soil.
Air, water and soil are unlimited because they grow back; therefore sustainable economic activity is eliminated.
tactical_explanations:
The list of resources to be used specifically includes time, money, means of production, natural resources and sinks. Any use for Option A is also the decision against Option B and generates opportunity costs. Lowering, such as absorption capacity of air, water and soil, are in the same logic.

The statement is true.

The essence of economic activity is the recognition of scarcity as a reality and of a social organization that allows the most efficient use of resources. Without this recognition, planning of the operation remains empty. Efficiency depends on the recognized limit, not on its denial.

The statement is true.

Sustainability links ecology, economics and social affairs; sustainable action aims to reconcile them. Energy efficiency primarily serves the ecological and partly economic side, but does not replace social and economic goals that are necessary for cohesion and acceptance. One dimension is not enough.

One dimension is not enough because sustainability links the three dimensions. Energy efficiency can help ecologically and economically while leaving social goals open. Economic and social goals must be achieved for cohesion and acceptance. Ignoring after a technical measure contradicts the agreement.

The sentence makes an example a free letter that the representation does not give.

The statement is false.

The importance of scarce resources is particularly evident in the use and exposure of air, water and soil. Short-term decisions show ecological and economic consequences. The sentence makes this increase without trying to list greenhouse gas emissions in later chapters.

The statement is true.

Unlimited regrowth is not the statement of the text. Especially air, water and soil are at the centre of the discussion because they are scarce and resilient. Sustainable economic activity follows from the fact that effects on other and on future generations must be included. Infinity would remove this obligation and deny scarcity.

Those who declare this media unlimited turn the point: the section sharpens scarcity there. Short-term decisions can damage them, today and in the long term. Then sustainable economic activity does not disappear, it becomes more urgent. The justification unlimited growth does not bear and contradicts the resource list including sinks.

The statement is false.

title: Niemand wirtschaftet allein
context: Evaluate the following statements on the topic of economics as an exchange:
statements: Nobody manages for themselves.
Economics means entering into exchange relationships from which the exchange partners benefit.
Those living alone in an apartment are outside any economic exchange relationship.
The exchange relationships create a cycle, the so-called economic cycle.
The only way to manage is to produce all the goods in your own household and to renounce any exchange.
tactical_explanations:
Eating breakfast alone or paying the bill alone does not change the baseline. In this section, business does not mean self-sufficiency behind closed doors, but relationships in which someone gives something and someone else gets something.

The sentence "No one alone manages for himself" is therefore at the beginning: a person who lives alone buys bread, pays rent or works for wages. Without one another there would be no exchange and thus no economy in the sense of the text. The private household remains a participant, not an island.

The statement is true.

Exchange is not a zero-sum game here. Both sides are to benefit from the relationship: the household of goods or income, the company of sales or labor performance, the state of taxes and the consideration of public tasks. This mutual advantage makes individual purchases and sales a network.

If you think of economies as one-sided taking, you miss the core of the section.

The statement is true.

Living alone does not separate from the economy. A person who lives alone remains private household and enters the same cycle as families: she often offers work, buys products and services and pays taxes. The claim that single people are outside of any exchange relationship confuses living forms with economic isolation.

Isolation in this sense does not exist in the text of the teaching.

The only living people buy electricity, pay rent, use roads and hospitals and often work in a relationship. These are exchange relationships with companies and the state, not a closed-off life of their own. The section begins with the fact that nobody manages for themselves.

The statement is false.

Many individual exchange records become a cycle because goods and money run back and forth between the same groups. The text of the teaching calls this cycle the economic cycle. It does not arise through an authority that orders it, but through the exchange relationships themselves. Anyone who sees only individual purchases overlooks the circular connection.

The statement is true.

Self-baking on Sunday does not refute the section. Here, economics means entering into exchange relationships from which the exchange partners profit. Whoever wanted to produce all goods himself and cancel every exchange would remain exactly with that single economy that excludes the representation.

Households can do some themselves, but the core of the economy in this chapter is exchange, not total self-production.

The statement is false.

title: From exchange to circulation
context: Evaluate the following statements on the emergence of the economic cycle:
statements: The economy is initially concerned with households and businesses.
Another key economic operator is the State.
The economic cycle is created because all economic operators exchange goods for money.
Exchange relationships exist only between two households, never with companies or the state.
Between households, businesses and the state, circular movements are created in which goods and services are exchanged for money.
tactical_explanations:
The section first mentions two groups without which everyday life does not work: private householders ask for and offer work performance, companies produce products and services. "First of all, here is the basic character, not that the state would later be unimportant. If you only count companies or just families, you leave one side of the exchange away.

Both must occur so that goods can be exchanged for money and a cycle is created at all.

The statement is true.

The state is not on the sidelines as a spectator. It is another central economic operator: public institutions, legal framework, taxes, infrastructure, schools, hospitals. Without it, exactly the third corner, which is running through taxes, public goods and transfers, was missing in the simple cycle.

Households and businesses alone describe the exchange incompletely as soon as public tasks and taxes are included in the picture.

The statement is true.

Because households, companies and governments exchange goods for money, relations with a circle are closed. Wages flow back to labour, purchase price to goods, tax to the state, public service. The cycle is therefore not an extra besides the exchange, but the form that the exchange takes between these participants.

Without the exchange of goods for money, these circular relationships would not be in the manner described.

Goods for money, or another means of exchange, is the common parenthesis. Private householders, companies and the state are in such relationships, not in separate islands. This results in the circular exchange relationships that the representation calls the economic cycle. Exchange is the cause, the circle the form.

The statement is true.

The text describes the relationships between households, companies and the state, not just a trade between neighbours. Work performance for wages, products for purchase price, taxes for public services: these are the axes. The restriction on two households removes companies and the state from the picture and contradicts the section.

The statement is false.

Goods and services run in one direction, money in the other, and both are linked to the same three groups. The presentation explicitly speaks of circular movements in which goods and services are exchanged for money and other means of exchange. This is the short form of the economic cycle in this section.

The statement is true.

title: Disorders are taking hold
context: Evaluate the following statements on how economic problems spread in the cycle:
statements: The economic cycle can rapidly expand economic problems in one area to other sectors and other economic operators.
When private householders consume less in lockdown, companies can come under pressure.
Companies that could not sell their products and services had to reduce staff in some cases.
A fall in household consumption is always limited to households and never reaches companies or the state.
The state has supported both households and businesses in the pandemic.
tactical_explanations:
A circle has no isolated corner. If something increases with a participant, the next one lacks demand, income or taxes. The text of the teaching makes this exactly the result of the cycle: Problems in one area or with certain economic operators expand rapidly to others. Anyone who understands the cycle expects this spread, not closed islands.

This is precisely why a lockdown can reach companies in households and later also the state.

The statement is true.

Less consumption means less sales. In the lockdown example, private householders have consumed less, which has put pressure on some companies. The pressure is not generated by a whim of management, but by the interrupted exchange relationship. Households buy less, companies sell less, the chain is the same.

The statement is true.

If you don't sell anymore, you can't keep the workforce you have worked so far. The presentation is cautious: you cut off some of your personnel, not every company releases them. The direction remains clear: lack of sales hits the jobs. Wages and employment depend on the sale of goods, not on a separate world.

Lack of sales means missing income. Companies pay wages from these revenues. If products and services can no longer be sold, this source breaks down, and staff cuts will result for some of the businesses. The theory describes exactly this chain without claiming that each company has deleted all jobs.

"Partially, the statement keeps the text.

The statement is true.

The pandemic example shows exactly the opposite. Less household consumption puts pressure on companies, the reduction of personnel again hits households, the state jumps in with support. The cycle connects the three groups. The claim that households are permanently restricted denies this very spread.

In the lockdown, private householders have consumed less, which has put pressure on some companies. Companies that have not been able to sell any more have had to cut off some of their personnel. The state has supported households and companies. Each set of the chain refutes the isolation thesis. A fall in consumption does not stop in the household cycle.

The statement is false.

Support ran in both directions, not just to a group. The state supported both households and companies during this time. This is in line with the role of the state in the cycle: it not only takes taxes, it also makes payments when the exchange between private participants stops.

The statement is true.

title: What the State includes
context: Evaluate the following statements on the role of the State as an economic operator:
statements: The state comprises all public institutions.
The state provides the legal framework within which economic relations take place.
The government collects taxes and other taxes from households and businesses.
The state only includes private banks, but not schools or hospitals.
The state is doing its job by building roads, bike paths, parks, public authorities, digital infrastructure, hospitals and schools, for example.
tactical_explanations:
The term includes all public institutions. Authorities, schools, hospitals and other public bodies belong to this, not just a ministry. Whoever narrows the state to one person or office, undercuts the definition of the section.

The statement is true.

The state provides the legal framework within which these relationships take place: contracts, property, tax law. Without this framework, exchange and circulation would not be possible in the form described above. The state is therefore not only buyer and payer, but also the legislator.

The statement is true.

Taxes and other taxes flow from private households and from companies to the state. With this money he fulfills his tasks. The revenue side is part of his active participation in the economic life, not a marginal topic next to the cycle. Whoever thinks the state only as an issuer without income leaves away the opposite direction.

Private householders and companies pay taxes and other taxes. The state uses these funds for roads, schools, hospitals and other public tasks. The levy is the money stream to the state, the public performance of the counter-current. Both belong to the description in the text. The statement correctly meets the revenue side.

The statement is true.

Banks are simply associated with companies because they offer financial services. Schools and hospitals explicitly refer to the presentation as tasks that the state has to finance and build with taxes. The reversal that state is only private banks and not education or health, twists both.

The statement is false.

The list is the description of the tasks, not the decoration. Roads, bike paths, parks, authorities, digital infrastructure, hospitals and schools are examples of what the state uses the money it has collected for building. Thus, it actively participates in the economy: it awards contracts and provides public infrastructure.

The examples show breadth, not a single authority as a whole state.

The statement is true.

title: Haushalte: Arbeit gegen Lohn
context: Evaluate the following statements on the position of households in the economic cycle:
statements: Private householders offer work performance and receive money in the form of wages and salaries.
With pay and salary, private households can buy products and services.
Private households appear in the cycle exclusively as buyers and never as providers of work.
Companies produce products and services that can purchase private household, other companies and the state for money.
Household labour performance remains in the cycle without compensation, because wages are outside any exchange relationship.
tactical_explanations:
Households are not only at the store. They offer work performance and receive money, wages and salaries for it. This is the one direction of the exchange with the companies: work in, income out. Without this side there would be no income in the cycle from which later is bought.

The text therefore represents the supply of labour and the purchase of goods as the corresponding roles of the same private household, not as two different groups of persons.

The statement is true.

The money received is not an end in itself. With wages and salaries households buy products and services. Income from work returns as demand to the companies. This return makes two separate files a cycle.

The statement is true.

Being only a buyer would be half the figure. The text of the teaching puts both things side by side: offering work and buying goods. Whoever cuts the offer side of the households interrupts the cycle at the first step, because then no wage will arise from which could be bought.

Private householders offer work performance and receive wages and salaries. With this money they buy products and services. Both roles belong to the description. The claim that households are exclusively buyers and never providers of work performance, cuts the income side. Without labour supply there would be no wage flow in the model of this section.

The statement is false.

The sales are not only for families. Companies produce what private householders, other companies and the state acquire for money or another means of exchange. Intermediate services between enterprises and public contracts belong to it. The circle is trilateral, not only household against company.

The statement is true.

Wages and salaries are precisely the consideration for work performance. They are at the center of the exchange relationship between household and company, not outside. The assertion of a work without compensation directly contradicts the section.

The statement is false.

title: Taxes and public services
context: Evaluate the following statements on taxes and public benefits in the cycle:
statements: Companies and households pay taxes and other taxes to the state and receive government services, i.e. public goods.
The State may award contracts to companies to provide infrastructure.
Public goods flow in the cycle only to companies, never to private households.
The state needs money to pay people for their work, such as teachers, police or judges.
Taxes interrupt the economic cycle permanently, because there is no government compensation after that.
tactical_explanations:
Tax and performance belong together. Households and companies pay taxes and other taxes and receive government services, public goods. Streets, schools, legal frameworks and authorities are such compensations, even if they do not go like a loaf of bread over the shop counter. The cycle closes over this public side.

If you only see the tax book and cancel the service, this is exactly the opposite direction.

The statement is true.

The government orders to make roads, digital infrastructure, hospitals or schools available. Thus, money flows from the state to the company, and goods or construction services flow back. The public task becomes visible in the cycle as an exchange with the company side.

The statement is true.

Public goods are also used by households: schools, hospitals, parks, cycle paths. The presentation explicitly mentions these examples as tasks of the state vis-à-vis society, not as equipment only for companies. The restriction to companies alone is too narrow.

Streets, schools and hospitals use private householders daily. The state fulfils precisely such tasks with taxes and is in exchange with households, not only with companies. Anyone who only ascribes public goods to companies leaves away the household side of the state's performance. The text describes both sides.

The statement is false.

The state not only buys concrete, it employs people. Teachers, police officers, judges receive money for their work. This is also a stream in the cycle: from the state as an employer to private households as income-producing persons.

The statement is true.

Taxes are a withdrawal of purchasing power in households and companies, but the section also describes the return flows: public goods, contracts, wages in the public sector, support payments. Permanently without consideration is not the picture of the text of the teaching.

The statement is false.

title: Transfers to families and founders
context: Evaluate the following statements on State support payments:
statements: The state provides support to private householders, for example to families with children.
The state provides support to companies, for example to business founders.
There are numerous exchange relationships between the state and private households, as well as between the state and the company.
Government transfers to households end the cycle because recipients are no longer allowed to spend money.
Support payments are provided in the teaching text exclusively to large banks and never to families or the founder.
tactical_explanations:
In addition to taxes and public goods, there are payments without direct purchase of a piece of infrastructure. The state provides support payments to private householders, such as families with children. The money changes from the state to the household and can return to the cycle as consumption.

The transfer is therefore a power in the reverse direction to the tax, not the end of the economic relationship.

The statement is true.

The company side also receives transfers. The company founders are named as an example. Support to the founder is thus a stream state to enterprise, not only a social policy sentence over families. Both directions are in the same paragraph.

The statement is true.

Taxes, public services, contracts, public sector wages and transfers result in many relationships, not a single one-way street. The presentation states that there are numerous exchange relationships between government and households on the one hand and companies on the other.

"Many" contradicts the image of a state that collects a tax only once a year and otherwise lacks it.

Taxes flow back to the state, public goods and transfers, orders go to companies, wages to teachers and police. Each of these movements is an exchange or payment relationship in the cycle. The text of the teaching summarizes them as numerous relationships between the state, households and companies.

The statement correctly reproduces this diversity without making a relationship the only one.

The statement is true.

Transfers replace or support income. Nothing says that recipients should not spend the money. On the contrary, the household remains a demander of products and services. A transfer that would end the cycle would be the opposite of the integration described.

The statement is false.

The examples are families with children and the cause, not large banks. Banks later appear as financial services providers in the money cycle, not as the only transfer recipient. The shift to large banks alone contradicts the above examples.

The statement is false.

title: Goods cycle and money cycle
context: Evaluate the following statements to the two cycles within the economic cycle:
statements: Within the economic cycle, a goods cycle and a money cycle are distinguished.
In the goods cycle, products and services move between economic operators.
The goods cycle and the money cycle are two names for the same electricity, because goods and money always flow in the same direction.
Banks and other financial services companies play a key role in the money cycle.
Without any money stream, the model described would nevertheless have the same complete economic cycle of exchange goods for money.
tactical_explanations:
One economic cycle, two directions of view. The representation distinguishes goods and money circulation within the same event. The distinction does not separate two economies, but two sides of the same exchange: what passes in real terms and what runs counter to payment.

The statement is true.

Products and services are the goods side. They run from companies to households, to other companies and to the state, while work performance goes from households to companies and to the state. This is the goods cycle that the section has developed to the exchange relationships before.

The statement is true.

Same name, same direction: that would be the confusion. Typically, goods run in one direction and money in the opposite direction. Whoever sets both flows identically can no longer explain why wages are the equivalent of labour and the purchase price is the equivalent of the goods. The distinction exists precisely for this reason.

Goods and services are exchanged for money. This presupposes opposite movements, not the same way in the same direction. Within the economic cycle, the representation therefore distinguishes the goods cycle and the money cycle. Whoever claims that both names denote the same flow in the same direction, strikes precisely this opposite.

Then it would remain unclear what households get for work and what companies get for products.

The statement is false.

Banks are central on the money side. They and other financial services companies play an essential role in the money cycle: payments, deposits, loans, advice. Without these services, the flow of money between the other participants would not be organised in the manner described.

The goods cycle can be told without it, the money cycle of this section cannot.

The statement is true.

The exchange is goods for money or another means of exchange. A model without any money stream would be a different picture than that of the section. The complete economic cycle of this chapter contains both sides. The assertion of a complete cycle without money stream contradicts the definition.

The statement is false.

title: Banks in a simple cycle
context: Evaluate the following statements on the classification of banks in the economic cycle:
statements: In the simple economic cycle, banks are assigned to companies.
Banks include those companies that offer services related to money.
Banks are in a simple cycle exclusively part of the state, because only the state is allowed to spend money.
Private householders and businesses can use banking services, such as payments, deposits or loans.
Financial services companies do not play a role in the money cycle because money wanders between participants on its own.
tactical_explanations:
The graphic of the simple cycle has three corners: households, companies, state. Banks are sitting in this simplified picture with the companies, not as the fourth independent pillar. This is an assignment of the model, no claim that banks are bakeries. They remain specialists for money, but count to the company side.

Those who strike it at the state or draw it as their own economy leave the simple scheme of the text.

The statement is true.

The assignment follows the activity. Banks are those companies that offer a range of services related to money. Payments, receipt of savings and investment money, lending and advice are the mentioned services. The definition depends on these services, not on the building with counter.

The statement is true.

Many participants are allowed to spend money: households buy, companies pay wages, the state makes transfers. Banks assign to the state because only it is allowed to spend money, mixes two things that separate the representation. In the simple cycle, banks belong to the companies.

The state spends public money on tasks, households spend wages, companies pay for intermediate payments. Banks organize the money cycle as financial services providers and are assigned to the companies. The thesis that only the state is allowed to spend money and banks therefore belong to the state, finds no support.

It doubles the state and cuts the company's allocation.

The statement is false.

Payments, savings and investment, credit needs and advice concern households as well as companies. The presentation speaks of economic operators who save or need money, not of a single customer group. Use of banking services by households and companies is therefore provided in the model.

The statement is true.

Money does not migrate by itself in an orderly form through accounts, transfers and loans. Banks are essential to this. The claim that financial service providers did not play a role contradicts the sentence that attributes exactly this role to them.

The statement is false.

title: Payments by banks
context: Evaluate the following statements on payment transactions:
statements: Banks carry out payments.
For many ways of paying, a bank account is required.
Without a bank account, all means of exchange are impossible in the text of the teaching, including cash and natural exchange.
Payments practically combine the flow of money between households, businesses and the state.
Banks are allowed to make payments only between two companies, never by a private household.
tactical_explanations:
The first banking service is payment transactions. Transfers, card payments and similar routes run through institutions that run accounts. Without this implementation, many payments would have to be made in cash or in other cumbersome form. The money cycle needs precisely this infrastructure.

The statement is true.

Not every payment, but many. The presentation adds: not least because a bank account is required for many ways of paying. Account is therefore often a prerequisite of the chosen payment method, not just an extra. Whoever thinks only coins, underestimates how the text describes the everyday life of the money cycle.

Bank transfer, card payment and similar routes are linked to this infrastructure of banks.

The statement is true.

The section knows money or another means of exchange. Cash and other forms of exchange are not declared impossible as soon as someone has no account. "Many ways of paying is not "all means of exchange." The absolute impossibility assertion overlays the representation.

The payment of the banks is essential because many payment methods need an account. This does not exclude cash or any other exchange. Whoever makes the account requirement for many ways the impossibility of all exchange means without an account, turns "many" into "all."

That is not what the text says.

The statement is false.

Wage, purchase price, tax, transfer: all these are payments between the three groups. Banks carry out this traffic and make the money cycle suitable for everyday use. The practical connection is the sense of the first enumeration, not a separate banking world without reference to the household and the state.

The statement is true.

Private householders pay rent, buy goods, transfer taxes. Payments include them. The restriction to two companies cuts the household side, although households are central participants in the cycle.

The statement is false.

title: Saving, investing and lending
context: Evaluate the following statements on deposits and loans:
statements: Banks accept money from economic operators who want to save and invest.
Banks provide money to economic operators who need money, for example in the form of loans.
Those who save will finally withdraw any further use of money from the cycle, because deposits will never be lent again.
Credit means in this section that the bank provides funds to those participants who need money.
Only the state can save; private households and companies never invest money in banks.
tactical_explanations:
Saving and investing are the deposit side. Banks accept money from other economic operators who want to do just that. The money is not just below the mattress, but from a financial service provider who continues to use it in the money cycle, for example for loans.

The statement is true.

The opposite side to the deposit is the provision. Anyone who needs money can get it from the bank, for example as a loan. Households, companies and in the logic of the cycle other participants with financing needs are on this side. Without this function a central service of the banks was missing.

Saving and credit therefore belong together in the picture, not as two separate worlds without reference.

The statement is true.

The money would only be definitively withdrawn if it locked the bank away and never left it out again. The presentation puts deposit and credit side by side: take savings, make available to the needy. The bridge between both is just the passing, not the final disappearance.

Banks receive savings and investment money and at the same time provide funds to those participants who need money. Both are listed in the same list. Whoever saves, hands over purchasing power to the bank, which can enter the money cycle as a loan. The thesis of final withdrawal without any lending contradicts this double role.

Saving interrupts the savings' purchase of goods, but does not end the money cycle as a whole.

The statement is false.

Credit is the form in which banks provide money when someone needs funds. The wording remains close to the text and does not invent interest rates or types of credit that the theory does not call it. The core is the provision of money to the needy in the money cycle.

The statement is true.

The state is the only one that saves and invests economic operators. Households and companies belong to these participants. The claim that the state alone is allowed to save is exactly what the customers who serve banks in the text of the teaching are doing.

The statement is false.

title: Advice and the full banking set
context: Evaluate the following statements on banking services:
statements: Banks advise on financial matters.
These banking services include payments, receipt of savings and investment money, lending and advice.
In the text of the teaching, advice replaces payments completely, because no one needs any more transfers as soon as a conversation has taken place.
Financial matters on which advice is given concern economic operators who deal with money, such as households and businesses.
Banks do not offer any service related to money.
tactical_explanations:
In addition to account, deposit and credit, the advice is provided. Banks advise on financial matters. This is the fourth service, not a footnote. Anyone who thinks banks are only money carriers, leaves this role away.

The statement is true.

The list is closed and concrete: carry out payments, receive money from savers and investors, provide money as a loan, advise on financial matters. All four are part of the picture of banks in the money cycle. A sub-list without advice or credit would be incomplete compared to the text.

The section defines banks via exactly this bundle, not via a single switch activity.

The statement is true.

Advice declares or recommends that it does not transfer by itself. Payments remain their own service, expressly in the first place. A conversation does not cancel the need for accounts and payments. The substitution claim mixes two services that lead the presentation side by side.

Banks first carry out payments, not least because many payment methods need an account. After that, deposits, loans and advice follow. The order shows supplement, not replacement. Anyone who makes the consultation the sole successor of the payment system, removes accounts and transfers from the money cycle.

This infrastructure remains in the text of the teaching, even if it is discussed.

The statement is false.

Financial matters are those that save, invest, pay or need credit. These are economic operators in the cycle, typically households and companies, and in the broader sense others too. Advice is attached to these matters, not to a secret fourth population group.

The statement is true.

The whole paragraph defines banks through money services. The negation "nothing contradicts each of the four bullets. It is the gross reversal of the section.

The statement is false.

title: Three participants, two streams
context: Evaluate the following statements on the interaction of households, companies and the state:
statements: Income from labour can flow back to companies as a demand for products and services.
Taxes are a cash flow to the general government, public services and transfers are counter-flows to households and businesses.
In the simple cycle, government, banks and foreign trade never occur, because the representation knows only two isolated households.
Companies can obtain orders from the state and pay taxes at the same time.
The goods cycle describes real benefits, the money cycle the opposite payments, in which banks play a major role.
tactical_explanations:
Wages are generated at work, buying at the shop counter or bill. Both are linked to the same groups. Households offer labor, receive money, buy goods: income returns as demand. This is exactly how the circle between household and company closes before the state joins.

The text describes this return flow as part of the circular exchange relationships, not as a coincidence after the payday.

The statement is true.

The government is taxed and other taxes paid. Public goods, infrastructure, public service wages and support payments flow back. If you see the tax only, you know half the state. If you see the transfer only, you know the other half. The section demands both.

The statement is true.

The simple cycle of this section knows households, companies and the state. Banks are assigned to the enterprises. Isolated two households are not exactly the model. Government in the sense of the state occurs, banks occur. Foreign trade deals with a later part of the same chapter, but does not belong to the assertion that the representation knows only two households.

The statement is wrong in its entirety.

Private householders, companies and the state are the main participants. Banks sit with the companies and carry the money cycle. The presentation begins with the fact that nobody manages alone, and ends with the cut in the banking services used here. Two isolated households without companies, state and banks do not correspond to this cut.

The absolute "never" about state and banks does not apply.

The statement is false.

The same company can be a contractor of the state and a tax payer. The text of the teaching mentions both: contracts for infrastructure and taxes of the companies. The two roles do not exclude each other. They are two relationships on the same axis state-company.

The statement is true.

Real against monetary, with banks on the money side: that is the distinction between the section. Goods and services against money, banks for payments, deposits, credit and advice. The statement summarizes the core without foreign topics.

The statement is true.

title: Lockdown as a circular chain
context: Evaluate the following statements on pandemic as an example of mutual dependencies:
statements: The pandemic has quickly made circuits and interdependencies visible.
Less household consumption, pressure on companies, possible staff cuts and government support form a coherent chain in the text.
The reduction in staff again affects private householders because wages are not enough, thus increasing the disruption in the cycle.
State support in the crisis does not change the fact that the state does not raise taxes in the normal cycle or fulfil public tasks.
Mutual dependencies mean that one participant can have consequences for another, not that each participant remains completely independent.
tactical_explanations:
The Coronavirus example is not a jewelry. It is intended to show what the cycle logically says: Dependencies become visible as soon as an area becomes stagnant. Lockdown and less consumption are the triggers, the rapid spread to companies, employment and state proof. The sentence meets the intention of the text.

Without a circuit, the lockdown would remain an isolated household history that the section is not telling.

The statement is true.

Four links, one story. Households consume less, some companies are under pressure to cut off some of the personnel, the state supports households and businesses. The chain is the didactic point: a shock does not remain local. If you cut a link, the example is broken.

The statement is true.

The next consumption may continue to fall. The representation does not express the backlash on households in every sentence, but it follows directly from the role of households as recipients of wages and buyers.

The circular logic makes the setback plausible and compatible with the section.

Wages and salaries finance consumption. If wages are reduced by staffing, the household lacks purchasing power. Less purchasing power means less sales in companies. This can increase the disturbance, precisely because the cycle connects the groups.

The text shows the direction from consumption to staff; the backlash on households is the same mechanism, only one step further. Independence of households after job losses would be incompatible with this picture.

The statement is true.

Support in the crisis is a form of payment of the state, not the proof that it does nothing else. In the normal cycle, the state raises taxes, sets the legal framework and performs tasks from the road to the school. The crisis supplements transfers, it does not extinguish the other roles.

The statement is false.

Dependence means: consequences can be skipped. Independence of each participant would be the opposite of the cycle. The section explains the spread of problems precisely with the cycle, not with isolation.

The statement is true.

title: Public service and infrastructure contract
context: Evaluate the following statements on State, employment and contracts:
statements: If the state pays teachers or police, money goes to private householders for work performance.
Infrastructure is often created in the model described by the government's task to build companies.
Legal framework, levies and concrete buildings such as hospitals are common to the active participation of the state in the economy.
Public institutions are outside the economic cycle because only private companies are allowed to produce goods.
The same household can receive wages for public employment, pay taxes and receive transfers such as family support from the state.
tactical_explanations:
Teacher, policeman, judge: they are called as persons who pay the state for work performance. Recipients are private households. The electricity is similar to the wage flow of companies, only the money comes from public funds. Employment by the state is thus part of the cycle, not a special room without income.

The statement is true.

"Letting build" shows the way of order. The state needs companies to be ready for roads, digital infrastructure, hospitals or schools. The order is the exchange: public money for construction or service. Infrastructure does not fall from the sky and not only from official workshops, as far as the representation is concerned.

This creates one of the numerous exchange relationships between the state and the company.

The statement is true.

Three layers, one figure. Legal framework arranges the relationships, finances taxes, buildings and businesses such as hospitals and schools perform tasks. The representation combines them to actively participate. Whoever lets only one layer apply, reduces the state below the level of the section.

The state includes public institutions, provides the legal framework and collects taxes and other taxes to perform tasks. Examples of tasks range from roads and bike paths to public authorities, digital infrastructure, hospitals and schools. Active participation means: setting frameworks, raising funds, providing services and buildings.

The three elements are not as alternatives, but as parts of the same role.

The statement is true.

Public institutions are the state, and the state is a central economic operator. It creates or lets create, buy, employ and transfer goods. The ban on the production of goods only private companies does not stand. It would define schools and hospitals from the cycle, although they are explicitly present.

The statement is false.

Rolls pile up in the same household: someone teaches and receives salary, pays taxes, maybe gets family support. The section describes exactly these relationship types side by side. They do not exclude each other. The cycle allows multiple flows between the same corners.

The statement is true.

title: Money cycle with credit and consumption
context: Evaluate the following statements on the interaction of banks, households and companies:
statements: A household can sell work, receive wages in an account and spend the same amount on goods, with banks carrying out payments.
An enterprise may hold deposits or borrow to finance production and sell later to households, other companies or the state.
Credit to businesses or households can support the money cycle by getting funds to participants they need.
The Bank's advice changes the fact that banks are assigned to companies in a simple model and offer money services.
Because nobody alone manages, households, businesses, governments and banking services are sufficient to understand the simple cycle described in this section.
tactical_explanations:
Three steps, a daily routine. Work against wages, pay in the account, account payment for goods. Bank payments combine the steps, because many payment methods need an account. The household remains a partner in exchange, the bank remains a service provider on the money side. This is the way the cycle looks when you read it from the pay slip.

Private householders offer work performance and receive wages and salaries. With money they buy products and services. Banks carry out payments. Together, the precisely described sequence results: income arises, is transferred, is spent. No step requires isolation.

The text of the teaching supplies all three blocks without linking them in a single sentence; the chain follows necessarily from the blocks.

The statement is true.

Companies produce and sell to households, other companies and the state. For this they often need money before the sales proceeds are there. Banks provide funds to such participants, for example as credit, and in reverse receive money that is to be invested. Deposit and credit are the financial side of the same corporate role in the simple cycle.

The statement is true.

Those who need money receive it from the bank in the form of loans. This is the bridge to households with financing needs and to companies under pressure, for example, when sales are increasing. The loan does not replace the goods cycle, but it keeps the money cycle moving. That's what "provide."

The statement is true.

Advice is the fourth service, it does not postpone the assignment. Banks remain in the simple circle with the companies and remain providers of money services. The advice does not change this classification; it supplements payments, deposits and credit. The claim that advice changes the assignment or definition is wrong.

In the simple economic cycle, banks are assigned to companies. They offer payment transactions, receipt of savings and investment money, loans and advice. Advice is part of this list, not an argument to add banks to the state or to remove them from the money services.

Anyone who says that advice changes the assignment or fact of money services, reads into the fourth point something that will cancel it. The point adds, he does not recall.

The statement is false.

The section of this subsection ends with the banks in the money cycle. Understand: nobody manages alone, cycle of exchange, three participants, goods for money, banks with payments, deposits, credit and advice. That's enough for the simple cycle here. What follows later in the same chapter does not belong to this substance.

The statement is true.

title: Supply and demand
context: Evaluate the following statements on supply and demand:
statements: The offer of a good is the entire amount of this good offered for sale.
Demand only includes the desire to buy, regardless of whether economic operators can pay for the goods.
Buyers of a good and sellers of this good meet in a market.
The offer of a good consists only of the quantity that a single supplier has in his warehouse.
The total amount of cocoa beans that all consumers want and can buy represents the total demand for cocoa beans.
tactical_explanations:
Put for sale, not hoarded anywhere: The theory defines the offer of a good as the total amount of this good offered for sale. It is about the quantity offered, not about wishes, plans or already completed purchases. This is exactly the amount that is opposed to demand as soon as buyers meet in a market.

In the cocoa example, the quantity of cocoa beans offered by all suppliers, not the harvest of a single farm and not the goods already delivered. Offer measures what is now for sale. Anyone who confuses the offer with the wish, plan or final delivery does not measure the quantity available for sale.

The statement is true.

The demand is the total amount of a good that economic operators want and can buy. Those who only want to buy but cannot pay for it do not count to the total demand. The restriction to the mere desire deletes the second half of the definition and makes the sentence wrong.

The statement is false.

Market means the meeting here. Buyers of a good and sellers of this good meet on a so-called market. Without this encounter from both sides there would be neither the opposite supply nor the demand in the sense of the section. The sentence represents exactly this starting position.

The statement is true.

A warehouse of a plant is not the market. The offer covers the total quantity offered for sale by all suppliers, in the cocoa example the quantity offered by all suppliers of cocoa beans. Whoever counts only one supplier, the remaining sellers of the same good undermines. The definition is aggregated, not operational.

A full warehouse without a sale intention counts just as little as the quantity of a dealer if others also offer the same goods. That is why the limitation to a single warehouse is wrong.

The statement is false.

Cocoa beans serve as an example for both sides of the theory. The total quantity that all demanders want and can buy is the total demand for cocoa beans. Wants and skills belong together: Buying intent without solvency counts as little as payment ability without intention.

The example transfers the general definition of demand to a concrete good. Economic operators who want and can buy together make this quantity, not a single wish, and not the already purchased delivery of yesterday. The theory needs this example so that will and ability are not misunderstood as two separate markets.

The statement is true.

title: Kakaobohnen am Markt
context: Evaluate the following statements on supply and demand for cocoa beans:
statements: The quantity of cocoa beans offered by all suppliers of cocoa beans represents the supply of cocoa beans.
The demand for cocoa beans is the total quantity that economic operators want and can buy.
If you want to buy cocoa beans, but cannot use any exchange means for them, then you already have the entire demand.
Demand is in line with the entire supply of a good.
The offer of cocoa beans includes only the quantity that has already been sold and delivered.
tactical_explanations:
All suppliers are included. The following applies: The quantity of cocoa beans offered by all suppliers of cocoa beans represents the offer of cocoa beans. It is the sum of the quantities put up for sale, not the harvest of a single farm and not the deliveries already made. This is exactly the total quantity offered is the offer of the good.

The statement is true.

The demand side is analogous: the total amount of cocoa beans that all demanders want and can buy represents the total demand for cocoa beans. Economic operators must want and can buy. The example repeats the general definition of demand for the concrete good. Both conditions remain binding.

The statement is true.

The definition requires the quantity that economic operators want and can buy. If the ability is lacking, for example because no money or other means of exchange can be used, this desire does not belong to the whole demand. The claim that the mere desire is already the whole demand contradicts the "and can".

If you want to, you are not yet a demander in the sense of the section. The intention and ability are coupled. A household that would like cocoa beans but cannot acquire them does not increase the defined demand. That is why the sentence is wrong.

The statement is false.

The next step is to be faced with the definitions. Demand is in contrast to the entire supply of a good. Supply and demand are therefore two sides of the same market for the same good, not two separate worlds. Only this counterpart makes the encounter on the market understandable.

The statement is true.

Offers are put for sale, not already sold. The offer is the total quantity offered for sale. Quantities already sold and delivered are processed deceptives, not the quantity offered. Whoever narrows the offer to the already delivered, twists the definition.

The goods sold have already left the market. What is still offered can be bought; what is already delivered is no longer available. The theory measures the offer at the quantity of all suppliers offered for sale. The restriction on completed deliveries is therefore wrong.

The statement is false.

title: Physical and virtual markets
context: Evaluate the following statements about what is meant by a market:
statements: Markets are exclusively physical places such as shops or stock exchanges.
Electronic markets are considered virtual places where supply and demand come together.
Market is also not understood as physical means of bringing supply and demand together.
Without a shop with a counter, no market can exist.
Buyers can relate to a market even if they do not meet in the same building.
tactical_explanations:
Businesses and exchanges are examples, not the whole definition. Market is not only understood as physical places of meeting supply and demand. Other, non-physical possibilities are also included, for example virtual places such as electronic markets. The restriction to exclusively physical places strikes this second part.

The statement is false.

Virtually counts explicitly. Electronic markets are called virtual places through which supply and demand come together. Thus, a market does not need a sales building as long as buyers are connected via this mechanism. The electronic platform is thus market in the sense of the section.

Electronic markets are not beside the definition, but in it. They are the mentioned non-physical possibilities of meeting. Whoever only lets the market hall apply, overlooks this sentence.

The statement is true.

The market is not a physical part of the market concept. Other possibilities through which supply and demand come together are encompassed, for example virtual places. The market is thus wider than the address of a business. The sentence hits the extension that follows the theory according to the physical examples.

The statement is true.

The counter is not a mandatory feature. Physical places such as shops and stock exchanges are examples; virtual places such as electronic markets are part of it. A market can exist without someone selling through a shop counter. The claim that there is no market without a shop contradicts the opening to non-physical possibilities.

Samuelson and Nordhaus describe the market as a mechanism with which buyers and sellers relate. A mechanism can be electronic. Whoever binds the existence of a market to a building confuses an example with the definition.

The statement is false.

Relationship instead of space: The market is a mechanism with which buyers and sellers relate to each other to determine price and quantity. This relationship can arise in a business, on a stock exchange or on an electronic market. The same building is not necessary for this. The sentence adheres to this broad version.

The statement is true.

title: Market as a mechanism
context: Evaluate the following statements determining the price and quantity on the market:
statements: The market is a mechanism by which buyers and sellers relate to each other to determine the price and quantity of a commodity, service or asset.
A market exists only where an authority sets each transaction price.
In a market, the price and quantity of a service can be determined, not just that of a physical commodity.
Services cannot be traded on a market because they are invisible.
Assets may also be the subject of price and quantity determination on a market.
tactical_explanations:
Samuelson and Nordhaus deliver the short formula adopted in theory. The market is a mechanism by which buyers and sellers relate to each other to determine the price and quantity of a commodity, service or asset. Mechanism, relationship and determination of price and quantity belong together.

The statement reflects this determination.

The statement is true.

The official fixing of each price is not a feature of the market term in this section. Buyers and sellers relate to the determination of price and quantity; this is the mechanism described. An obligation for an authority to set each transaction price does not stand here. The restriction "only there is therefore wrong.

Price formation is created by the combination of supply and demand and is an essential task of markets. This is different from the assertion that markets existed only when the official price was set at a complete level. The sentence distorts the task and the condition of existence.

The statement is false.

The quoted provision is called goods, services or asset. The price and quantity of a service can therefore be determined on the market. Whoever narrows the market on physical goods, cuts two of the three mentioned items.

The statement is true.

Invisibility does not exclude the market. Services are defined in the definition of the goods. Buyers and sellers can relate to the price and quantity of a service, for example in physical or electronic markets. The claim that invisible services are not marketable contradicts the quoted sentence.

Repair, advice or other services can be offered and sought. The theory treats goods as products and services; here the service is explicitly included in the market formula. Invisibility is not an exclusion criterion.

The statement is false.

The price and quantity of an asset can be determined on the market as soon as buyers and sellers relate via the mechanism. Thus, the market term is not limited to everyday products. The rate follows the third category.

The statement is true.

title: Types of markets
context: Evaluate the following statements to different types of markets:
statements: Depending on the product, different types of markets are distinguished, for example the consumer goods market or the labour market.
There is only one market where all goods are traded together and indistinguishably.
The real estate market, the capital market and the commodity market are examples of market types.
The labour market is not one of the market types, because it only deals with salaries and does not generate prices.
The emission allowance market is an example of a market type.
tactical_explanations:
The good determines the type of market. Depending on the good it is, different types of markets are distinguished. Consumer goods market and labour market are in the sample series. Different goods, different markets: exactly that is what the section says.

The statement is true.

A single market for everything contradicts the distinction between goods. These include consumer goods market, labour market, real estate market, capital market, commodity market and emission certificate market as different types. Anyone who claims that there is only one, indistinguishable market for all goods, will break this structure.

Local boundaries such as the Austrian labour market or the world market for crude oil are also coming in. That is why the idea of a single common market is too gross and wrong. Good and territory are combined, not merged into a pile. A market for consumer goods is not the same market as that for labour or raw materials.

The statement is false.

Three other examples from the same list: the real estate market, the capital market and the commodity market. They stand side by side as market types, not as synonyms.

The statement is true.

Work has its own market: the labour market. There, too, supply and demand meet, only here is the price called salary or wage instead of purchase price. A salary is nothing else than the price of a work performance that forms between bidders and demanders. The claim that there are no prices there confuses the term with the function.

If you remove the labour market from the market concept because another word is used for price, you contradict the classification of market types according to the traded goods.

The statement is false.

Emissions certificates are included in the sample series of market types. The emission certificate market is considered as an example in addition to consumer goods, labour, real estate, capital and raw materials.

The statement is true.

title: Local markets
context: Evaluate the following statements to markets in a local area:
statements: If the market for a particular commodity is considered in a specific local area, then the Austrian labour market is referred to.
The European capital market is the capital market in a local area.
The world market for crude oil is an example of the market for a particular good in a spatial context.
Markets can never be defined locally, but exist only as a single world market of all goods.
The Austrian labour market and the world market for crude oil are the same type of market in the same place.
tactical_explanations:
Place plus good is the name. If the market for a particular property in a specific area is considered, for example, the Austrian labour market. Work is the good, Austria the area. The sentence literally reflects the example.

The statement is true.

Capital market plus Europe: The same idea applies to the European capital market. The good is capital services, the area is European. The name separates this market from the Austrian labour market or the world market for crude oil.

The statement is true.

Crude oil on the world market follows the same logic. The world market for crude oil is called as an example if the market for a particular commodity is meant in a spatial context. The world market is the broad spatial version, crude oil the commodity. The example is in a series with labour market and capital market.

Spatial version does not mean that all goods are piled up. Crude oil remains crude oil, labour remains labour. The world market for crude oil is the market of this good in the world view, in addition to the European capital market and the Austrian labour market as further combinations of goods and territory.

The three book examples are deliberately located on different levels of good and space.

The statement is true.

The theory does not say that there is no localisation. It explicitly mentions the Austrian labour market, the European capital market and the world market for crude oil. Local determination is therefore provided for, not prohibited. The assertion of a single world market of all goods contradicts the distinction between good and territory.

The statement is false.
