Various goods, different areas. Labour market in Austria is not the same market as the world market for crude oil. Type of market and place fall apart: work against crude oil, Austria against world. The equation is wrong.

Consumer goods, labour, real estate, capital, raw materials and emission certificates are separated as species. In addition, local determination is added. To mix two examples from the list, exactly this separation is lifted. Whoever puts both into one misses both good and territory at the same time.

The statement is false.

title: Price formation on markets
context: Evaluate the following statements on pricing:
statements: The combination of supply and demand leads to price formation.
Pricing is an essential task of markets.
The price usually expresses in money units how much to pay for a good.
Prices arise regardless of whether supply and demand meet in a market.
Markets have nothing to do with price formation.
tactical_explanations:
The combination of supply and demand results in price formation. Without this comparison of the quantity offered and the quantity that demanders want and can buy, the described process is missing. The sentence follows this order.

The statement is true.

Task, not secondary: Pricing is an essential task of markets. Markets bring buyers and sellers into relation, and this results in price. Anyone who thinks markets are warehouses only, overlooks this task.

The mechanism and task fit together. The price and quantity of a commodity, service or asset are determined by the relationship between both sides. This is the essential task that the sales attribute to price formation. Without the combination of supply and demand, this process is missing.

Pricing remains the main task of whether the place is a business, a stock exchange or an electronic market.

The statement is true.

Money units are the rule. The price usually expresses in money units how much to pay for a good. "In general, other means of exchange are conceivable, but they call money as the usual standard. The sentence reflects this formulation.

The statement is true.

Regardless of the meeting, the price does not arise in this section. First, supply and demand on the market lead to price formation. Whoever claims independence separates the price from its described origin.

The price is not part of the presentation here without this meeting. Therefore, the sentence is wrong. The price is usually to show in money units how much to pay, and that after this meeting, not before in an airless room.

Independence from market activity would deny the essential task of price formation.

The statement is false.

Nothing to do with price formation: The opposite is true. Price formation is an essential task of markets. The market as a mechanism determines price and quantity. The rejection of any connection is wrong.

The statement is false.

title: Price as a scarcity indicator
context: Evaluate the following statements at price as an indicator of scarcity:
statements: Price is also an indicator of the scarcity and extent of the scarcity of a good.
If supply is small, but demand is high, a high price usually develops.
Prices are only a receipt and do not give information about the scarcity of a good.
If demand is low and supply is high, a low price is usually formed.
The scarcity of a good can never be seen at the market price.
tactical_explanations:
The indicator is called an indicator, not just a ticket. The price is also an indicator of the scarcity and the extent of the scarcity of a good. In addition to the information on how much to pay, it shows how scarce the good is. The rate hits both halves: scarcity and its extent.

The statement is true.

Small and high usually results in high. If the supply is small, but the demand is high, a high price usually arises. This is formulated as a typical connection, not an invariably natural constant. Within this formulation the sentence is correct.

Shortness becomes visible because few units offered are faced with many prospective and viable demanders. The high price shows the extent of this shortage. That is what the indicator means.

The statement is true.

Only receipt, no shortage information: The opposite applies. The price expresses how much to pay and is also an indicator of scarcity and its extent. Whoever cuts the scarcity signal effect leaves away the second function. The sentence is wrong.

The price is linked to supply, demand and scarcity. A mere document function without information about scarcity is not available there.

The statement is false.

The reversal is analogous. If demand is low and the supply is high, a low price is usually formed. Many units offered meet few who want to buy and can. The low price then shows low scarcity in this sense.

The statement is true.

Reading never contradicts the indicator. Precisely because the price indicates scarcity and its extent, a high or low price can be read about scarcity, usually in the pattern described. The absolute lock "never is wrong.

Small supply and high demand, high price; low demand and high supply, low price. These are the rule contexts mentioned in the book. Whoever basically refuses to read, rejects the indicator concept. The price remains the amount that is usually to be paid in money units and the signal for the extent of scarcity.

The statement is false.

title: High price and more offer
context: Evaluate the following statements how a high price affects suppliers:
statements: A high price could motivate providers to increase the offer.
New suppliers would enter the market to benefit from the high price.
A high price keeps all potential suppliers permanently from entering the market.
If supply is small and demand is high, a high price usually arises, which can be the reason for more supply or new suppliers.
Small supply and high demand usually result in a particularly low price.
tactical_explanations:
Motivation to expand: A high price could motivate providers to increase the offer. Existing sellers then put more quantity for sale. This is formulated as a possible result of the high price, not as a duty of any operation. Within this possibility the sentence is correct.

The statement is true.

Entry as a second episode. Or new suppliers would enter the market to benefit from the high price. Thus, the high price not only affects already active suppliers, but can attract additional salespeople. Profiting from the high price is the motive mentioned.

Both can come together: more amount of old people and new ones' entrance. The sentence isolates the entry, which is explicitly called. It remains true. High price is incentive, not barrier. Those who want to benefit from the high price come as new provider, not as spectators behind a barrier.

The statement is true.

The high price can encourage new providers to enter to benefit from it, and existing providers to increase the offer. Whoever claims that the high price keeps all potential providers permanently away, reverses the described incentive.

The words all and permanently overlay the incentive. The theory speaks of motivation and entry, not of a lock. Therefore the sentence is wrong.

The statement is false.

Chain of regular price and reaction: Small supply and high demand usually make a high price. This high price could increase the supply or attract new suppliers. The set combines both book places in the order of the paragraph.

The statement is true.

Especially low in scarcity: The opposite is true. Small supply and high demand usually lead to a high price. A low price is part of the reverse situation with low demand and high supply. The rate exchanges the rule.

The statement is false.

title: Increasing supply and falling prices
context: Evaluate the following statements on price developments after an increase in supply:
statements: Increasing supply would lead to a fall in prices if demand remained stable.
If demand remains the same and supply rises, prices typically fall.
Higher supply with unchanged demand usually increases prices.
The high price can give the impetus that supply is growing, which means that prices are falling with constant demand.
The same demand does not play a role in the price reduction described after an increase in supply.
tactical_explanations:
Condition of constant demand: An increasing supply would lead to a decrease in prices if demand remained constant. More quantity placed for sale meets unchanged demand that was willing to buy and able to buy. Price pressure goes down. The rate is the book order according to the high price.

The statement is true.

Typically, this is the same episode in other words. Supply is rising, demand is still rising, prices are falling. This is not a new law, but the repetition of the sentence about rising supply with constant demand.

The statement is true.

Increasing supply with the same demand contradicts the text. There, prices fall as supply rises and demand remains the same. Whoever claims to rise, reverses the described movement.

The high price was the starting point that could trigger more offer or entry. The next stage is sinking, not another climb just because of the larger offer. Therefore, the sentence is wrong.

The statement is false.

The impetus and consequence in one line: High price motivates to increase the supply or to enter. If the supply increases and remains the demand, the prices decrease. The set combines motive and subsequent price reduction as the sales put it in a row.

Without the high price, the incentive described was missing. Without constant demand, the price reduction would not be formulated in this way. Both elements are in theory.

The statement is true.

No role for the constant demand: The theory explicitly depends on this condition. If it is missing in the sentence, the prerequisite of the described episode is missing. The assertion that it does not matter is wrong.

Increasing supply alone is not described as an isolated price reduction without a view of demand. The presentation says: with constant demand. Whoever cancels this clause changes the mechanism. The clause belongs to the described price reduction, it is not an ornament on the edge. Without constant demand, the sales do not describe the decline of prices in this way.

The statement is false.

title: Low price and market exit
context: Evaluate the following statements at low price and the withdrawal of companies:
statements: If demand is low and supply is high, a low price is usually formed.
A low price typically results in companies that cannot be profitably driven at this price leaving the market.
Withdrawal may mean that companies close or focus on other goods and services.
A low price forces all providers to further expand the offer.
Unprofitable companies always remain in the market at low prices because it is impossible to leave.
tactical_explanations:
Reverse of the shortage situation: Low demand and high supply usually make up a low price. Many units are compared to few who want to buy and can. The price then shows low scarcity. The rate follows the second rule of the paragraph.

The statement is true.

Typically, those companies that cannot be run profitably at such a low price are exiting the market. The low price is the reason, not a voluntary hobby. Typically, not in every individual case without exception, so the theory.

Profitability is the threshold. Anyone who can no longer work economically below the low price goes. This is the described reaction of the provider side. Without this threshold there would be no reason for the exit. The low price filters about the lack of profitability, not about a duty to stay.

The statement is true.

Two forms of exit are in brackets: either close or focus on other goods and services. Exiting is not just insolvency and dark windows. A change of the assortment is planned. The sentence calls both ways.

The statement is true.

Further expansion at low price is the wrong move. Typical is the withdrawal of unprofitable companies, not the expansion by all providers. "All" and "expand" contradict the described pressure downwards.

High prices can increase the offer. Low prices drive those who do not remain profitable. Not to exchange directions is the core of this place.

The statement is false.

Always stay, leaving impossible: The exit is described as a typical result. Close or focus change is possible. The absolute impossibility of leaving and the permanent remaining is wrong.

Unprofitable at such low price is the condition for the outcome. Whoever replaces it by a ban on withdrawal, takes the mechanism the second half after the high price.

The statement is false.

title: Less offer after withdrawals
context: Evaluate the following statements on the consequences of market exit:
statements: The withdrawal of unprofitable companies leads to a lower offer and a rise in prices.
After withdrawals, the offer is lower than before because suppliers have left the market.
After the withdrawal of unprofitable companies, prices continue to fall because the offer is increasing.
A lower offer after withdrawals can make prices rise again.
Market exits leave the offer unchanged because other suppliers immediately replace the same size.
tactical_explanations:
This in turn leads to a lower offer and a rise in prices. "This means the withdrawal of those who do not remain profitable at low prices. Less suppliers, less offered quantity, then rising prices. The rate is the final stage of the sales.

The statement is true.

Leaving reduces the quantity offered. Whoever closes or places other goods in the center, offers the previous goods no longer to the previous extent. The offer, defined as the total quantity offered for sale, becomes lower. This is the immediate quantity sequence of the exit.

The statement is true.

The result is that the offer is rising: both are contrary to the result. Withdrawal is lowering the offer and prices are rising. Whoever claims falling prices and rising offer after the withdrawal is distorting cause and effect.

Increasing supply with constant demand lowers prices, that was the phase after the high price. After the low price and exit the opposite movement applies. The phases do not mix, keeps the mechanism straight. The correction after exit shows upwards, not further down.

After the exit, the quantity offered is smaller, and that is why prices are rising again.

The statement is false.

Let it rise again: That's exactly how the presentation closes. Lower offer after withdrawals, then a rise in prices. The low price triggers the exit, the exit corrects the price upwards over less quantity. The sentence makes this correction.

The statement is true.

Unchanged offer by immediate replacement is not in theory. The withdrawal leads to a lower offer. An automatic, complete replacement by other providers would cancel this result. The claim is wrong.

New suppliers enter at high price to profit. This is another part of the mechanism. When leaving due to low price, the presentation describes a reduction in quantities, not an immediate equivalent replacement. Replacement of all the excluded to the same extent does not describe the sales.

The statement is false.

title: Kakaohandel in Wien
context: In Vienna, retailers offer cocoa beans, partly in a warehouse, partly via a trading platform on the net. Rate the following statements:
statements: The quantity offered by all suppliers of cocoa beans represents the range of cocoa beans.
Only the wish for purchase without solvency counts as the total demand for cocoa beans.
Both the warehouse and the platform on the network can be markets where supply and demand come together.
If a high price is created because of scarce supply and high demand, new suppliers can enter to benefit from it.
The high price prevents existing suppliers from increasing the range of cocoa beans.
tactical_explanations:
The quantity offered by all suppliers of cocoa beans is the range of cocoa beans. Whether the beans are offered in Vienna, elsewhere or on a platform, the sum of the quantities put up for sale remains the offer. A single dealer is only a part of it.

The statement is true.

Demand is the quantity that economic operators want and can buy. Roastings or households that would like to buy but cannot do it do not form the whole demand. The sentence scrapes the skill and is wrong.

The total quantity that all consumers want and can buy is the demand for cocoa beans. Payability and buying intent belong together, in Vienna as in the example of teaching.

The statement is false.

Physically and virtually side by side. Shops, stock exchanges and other physical places count, as well as virtual places as electronic markets. The warehouse and the platform on the net are precisely these two ways of bringing together supply and demand. Both can be market.

Buyers and sellers are related to determine price and quantity, which can be done at the ramp or via the screen. The market term does not require either or between the hall and the net. Hall and net are two ways of the same market term, not two rival definitions.

The statement is true.

Short supply, high demand, usually high price. This high price could encourage suppliers to increase the supply or attract new suppliers who want to benefit from the high price. The entry of new cocoa dealers is the second reaction mentioned in theory. The rate remains within this framework.

The statement is true.

Preventing the increase is the wrong effect. A high price could motivate suppliers to increase the offer. Existing dealers would rather put more beans for sale, not less. The rate reverses the incentive.

Profiting from the high price applies to new and old people who expand. A barrier against more offer does not stand here. Therefore, The statement is false.

The statement is false.

title: Electronic market for used bicycles
context: On an electronic platform, suppliers of used bicycles and households meet who want to buy a bike and can buy it. Rate the following statements:
statements: The platform is a virtual place where supply and demand come together, and thus a market.
Without a shop, there is no market for the bicycles offered.
The price on this platform usually expresses in money units how much to pay for a wheel.
Price formation is not a task of this market because it is not physical.
Buyers and sellers can use this mechanism to determine the price and quantity of bicycles.
tactical_explanations:
Electronic markets are called virtual places of meeting. Offer is the quantity of wheels offered for sale, demand the quantity that households want and can buy. The platform brings both together. It is thus market, not just a blackboard without market character.

The statement is true.

Shop-place is a mandatory feature. Non-physical possibilities are included. An electronic market exists without counter. The claim that without shop-place there is no market for the wheels contradicts the opening to virtual places.

Businesses and stock exchanges remain examples of physical places. They do not exclude the platform. Whoever binds existence to rent and shop window confuses example and term.

The statement is false.

Money units remain the rule, also online. The price usually expresses in money units how much to pay for a good. The used bike is the good, the displayed sum of the price. Virtuality does not change this expression.

The statement is true.

The combination of supply and demand leads to price formation; it is an essential task of markets. Electronic markets are markets. The rejection of price formation due to lack of physis is wrong.

Mechanism means: Buyers and sellers are related to determine price and quantity. This is exactly what a trading platform does when offers and purchase decisions meet. The task remains. Virtuality does not change the task, only the place of meeting.

The statement is false.

The definition of price and quantity is the Samuelson formula that takes over the theory. Here was: the bicycle. Relationship about the electronic mechanism. The sentence transfers the definition to the platform without overstretching it.

The statement is true.

title: Wohnungen am Immobilienmarkt
context: In an Austrian city, the offer of rental apartments is small, the demand high. Rate the following statements:
statements: The real estate market is a market way of bringing supply and demand together.
If supply is small and demand is high, a high price usually arises.
A high price could motivate providers to increase the offer, or encourage new providers to enter.
Housing markets exist only as a world market and never in a local area.
A low price with high supply and low demand typically leads to unprofitable suppliers expanding the supply rather than withdrawing.
tactical_explanations:
Real estate market is included in the list of market types alongside consumer goods, labour, capital, raw materials and emission certificates. Supply and demand meet there, physically, for example through brokerage offices or virtually through advertising platforms. Apartments are the good of this market. The sentence is the application of the species distinction.

The statement is true.

Small amount for sale, many who want to buy or rent and can: Usually high price. The price is also an indicator of the scarcity and its extent. The city scene is the everyday case of this rule, not an exception to it.

The statement is true.

High price as an incentive: Providers could increase the offer, new providers could enter to benefit from the high price. On the real estate market, this means offering more apartments or additional landlords. The mechanism is the same as in general sales.

If supply rises later on with constant demand, prices would fall. This is the subsequent stage that the high price can set in motion. The rate remains at the first reaction and is true.

The statement is true.

Only world market, never locally: markets are explicitly called in a locally precisely defined area, for example the Austrian labour market. The same logic applies to a property in an area, i.e. also for apartments in a city or in Austria. The barrier against local markets is wrong.

The world market for crude oil is another example of spatial design, not the proof that apartments can only be thought of worldwide. Good and territory are combined.

The statement is false.

The typical result is a reversal of the trend rather than a low price. At low prices, companies that cannot be run profitably will exit by closing or changing their focus. This will lower the offer and make prices rise again. Further expansion of all unprofitable ones is not the described reaction.

Typically, exit, then lower offer, then rising prices. Those who force expansion take its correction function from the low price. The statement is false. Expanding would be the reaction to a high price, not an unprofitable low.

The statement is false.

title: Shortness signal and entry or exit
context: Evaluate the following statements on the interaction of price, supply and demand on the market:
statements: The price shows the scarcity: If the supply is small and the demand is high, a high price usually develops.
A high price can increase supply and attract new suppliers, and then prices will fall if demand remains stable.
Low demand and high supply usually lead to a low price and typically to the withdrawal of unprofitable companies.
After such withdrawals, the offer decreases and prices rise.
Demand is just the desire to buy, not the ability to buy, and a market is only a physical business.
tactical_explanations:
The price shows scarcity and its extent. Small supply, high demand, usually high price. This is the starting point of the adaptations described, not a special law next to the market.

Buyers meet on physical or virtual markets. This meeting is the main task of price formation. The high price in the scarcity situation is precisely this signal.

The statement is true.

Incentive upwards, amount downwards, price downwards: High price could motivate suppliers to increase the supply, or encourage new providers to enter. Increasing supply, with constant demand, then leads to falling prices. The rate keeps the order of the sales.

The same demand is the condition for sinking. Without it, the theory does not formulate this price reduction. With it, the arc from the scarcity signal to relaxation over more quantity closes.

The statement is true.

Mirror image of the other location: Low demand, high supply, usually low price. Typically, those who do not remain profitable at this price will exit by closing or other goods. The set combines regular price and exit without introducing later curve terms.

Profitability is the threshold, not a moral duty to stay. Low price filters out providers. That's what it says.

The statement is true.

Final stage: withdrawal, lower offer, rising prices. The reduction in quantities after the exit of unprofitable companies makes prices rise again. This closes the circle to the scarcity indicator, without further additional assumptions.

Lower supply means: The total quantity offered for sale is smaller. Demand is in contrast to this, i.e. the quantity that wants to be bought and can be. Less supply with given demand makes the good scarcer, the price rises in the described consequence. The sales result in supply, demand, price and entry or exit.

The statement is true.

Two mistakes in one sentence. Demand is the quantity that economic operators want and can buy, not the mere desire. Markets are not only physical business, but also stock exchanges and virtual places such as electronic markets. Both cuts contradict the definitions at the beginning of the section.

Without the ability, demand would be only wishful thinking. Without the virtual places, the market concept would be limited to the market hall. The section opens both. Therefore, The statement is false.

The statement is false.

title: Foreign countries as a further player
context: Evaluate the following statements on the simple economic cycle and cross-border exchange relations:
statements: The simple economic cycle shows a strong simplification of economic relations within a country.
There are also cross-border exchanges with economic operators in other countries.
The simple economic cycle already covers all foreign trade completely, so that no other actor is necessary.
In order to simplify these relations, foreign countries are often shown as a further player in the economic cycle.
Cross-border exchanges are only possible in very large economies, never in a small country.
tactical_explanations:
Households, companies and the state exchange in a simple picture, especially within the national borders. The section explicitly says that this cycle shows the economic relations within a country greatly simplified. Simplified means: many details are missing, the basic direction remains domestically related.

Those who consider the simple cycle to be the whole world economy overestimate the scheme.

The statement is true.

There are also cross-border exchanges with economic operators in other countries. Exports, imports and other international contacts are part of the reality, even if the simple scheme leaves them out. The next step is precisely this enlargement, not the claim that the economy ends at the border.

The statement is true.

Without the additional player abroad, foreign trade would remain invisible. The simple cycle is domestically related and greatly simplified. Precisely because cross-border relations exist, foreign trade is often extra-marked. The claim that the simple cycle already covers the entire foreign trade is contradicting this step.

In the scheme without foreign countries, imports and exports are missing as their own relations with participants outside the country. The presentation adds the foreign country to close this gap. Whoever declares the simple cycle complete, scrapes the extension that the section establishes. Completeness in the sense of foreign trade requires the further actor.

The statement is false.

The extended scheme also includes foreign countries, in addition to households, companies and the state. The text of the teaching explains this by the fact that one wants to simplify the cross-border economic relations. Actors here means: another corner in the cycle, not a single foreign company. This is the usual presentation that the section speaks of.

The statement is true.

The size of the country does not change the existence of cross-border exchange relations. The presentation introduces the foreign country and then emphasizes the importance for a small inland country like Austria. Small countries do not stand outside the international exchange. The restriction to very large economies is wrong.

Whether a country has many inhabitants or few, imports and exports remain relations with participants in other countries. Austria is the counter-example in theory: small, domestic and yet strongly integrated. Never in a small country would mean that the additional actor abroad only applies to large states. That is exactly what the section does not teach.

The statement is false.

title: Small open Austria
context: Evaluate the following statements on the importance of international exchange relations for Austria:
statements: Exchange relations with other countries are of great importance, especially for a small inland country like Austria.
Membership of the European Union has facilitated trade with other Member States.
Around 70 percent of Austrian exports and imports are made with EU member states.
Austria deals exclusively with third countries outside the EU and not with Member States.
Trade with third countries, especially the USA, the UK and China, does not play a role in Austria, which is an export-oriented country.
tactical_explanations:
Small and domestic means not self-sufficient. The section represents Austria as a small inland country, for which exchange relations with other countries are of great importance. Less internal market area and open borders for exchange make foreign trade a daily occurrence, not a special case. Anyone who thinks Austria as a closed island misses the starting point.

The statement is true.

Membership reduces barriers in the Union. Trade with other member states has been facilitated, not made more difficult. Eased here means: fewer borders in the internal market, not that each contract comes about by itself. The direction of the sentence corresponds to the text of the teaching.

The statement is true.

The size of the region, not the decimal place, is the point. Around 70 percent of exports and imports are carried out with EU member states. The lion's share of Austrian foreign trade is therefore in the Union, the rest with other partners. Anyone who wipes out 70 percent as a negligible number underestimates the concentration on the EU area.

Anyone who wants to memorize an exact number misses the qualitative findings.

The figure sets this order of magnitude to show that trade with member states dominates. Third countries remain important, but they do not have the same share. The statement adheres to this order.

The statement is true.

Only third countries would remove the EU share. The presentation mentions around 70 percent with member states and additional trade with third countries. Both exist. The claim that Austria only acts outside the Union reverses the weights.

Eased trade in the EU and the high share of exports and imports contradict a purely third country model. The USA, the UK and China are examples of third countries, not the only partner. Therefore, the formula of exclusivity is wrong.

The statement is false.

Export orientation does not end at the EU external border. Trade with third countries, especially the USA, the UK and China, plays a major role in an export-oriented country like Austria. To claim no role, exactly this sentence is not mentioned.

Large role and around 70 percent of the EU's share can stand side by side: one describes the focus, the other the remaining, but important partners.

Third countries are not the main bloc, but they are not zero. An export-oriented country sells and buys beyond the Union. The denial of any role contradicts the section.

The statement is false.

title: Export ratio and external trade
context: Evaluate the following statements on the export ratio and the role of foreign trade in Austrian economic performance:
statements: The export ratio measures exports of goods and services as a percentage of total economic output, i.e. gross domestic product.
If the export ratio is about half, five out of ten euro generated in Austria come from external trade.
The export ratio is the difference between imports and exports to euro.
A high export rate shows that a country's economic performance depends heavily on external trade and is not only driven by domestic consumption.
The export quota only counts the sale of confectionery to tourists.
tactical_explanations:
The top exports of goods and services, the bottom total economic output, measured by gross domestic product. Percent, not a euro amount. This is exactly how the box defines the export ratio. Those who share exports by GDP follow this definition. Those who share something else by something else do not measure the quota of the definition.

The statement is true.

Half of the output, half of the euro: the same ratio in everyday language. The presentation links the export ratio of 50 percent to the rate, five out of ten euro generated in Austria came from foreign trade. It is about the scale of openness, not about memorizing an import figure in billions.

Anyone who understands 50 percent as an export quota can read the rate with the five out of ten euros as a conversion.

The statement is true.

Difference is a balance, not a quota. Imports minus exports result in a surplus or deficit in euro, not the share of exports in GDP. The export ratio is a percentage ratio, exports relative to the gross domestic product. Those taking the difference confuse trade balance and openness measure.

A country can have imports and exports at a similar level and still have a high export ratio if both are large in relation to GDP. This is precisely what the presentation for Austria suggests: high openness, lastly small difference. The definition of the difference destroys this measure. That is why The statement is false.

The statement is false.

A high export rate means that a large part of what is generated in the country goes to sales abroad, including trade with third countries outside the EU. Orientation outwards means that foreign trade is a factor, not that nothing is produced or sold domestically.

The statement is true.

Sweets are popular examples, not the definition of quota. The export rate includes exports of goods and services as a whole as a percentage of GDP. Mozart balls, waffles or Sachertorte do not list the list. Machines, vehicles, processed goods and chemical products do so. A quota only from tourist sweets would be another much tighter measure.

Five out of ten euros from foreign trade refer to the whole of foreign trade, not to a confectionery. Services such as tourism count with, but not as the only position and not instead of the exports of goods. The narrowing of confectionery makes the sentence wrong.

The statement is false.

title: What Austria really exports
context: Evaluate the following statements on the composition of Austrian exports of goods and services:
statements: The lion's share of exports does not make Mozart balls, hazelnut waffles or Sachertorten.
Machinery, vehicles, manufactured goods and chemical products shall list the export goods.
Austria exports only food specialties and no other goods.
In the case of services, Austrian companies sell mainly tourism, transport, technical services and information services to foreign customers.
Sachertorte and Mozartkugeln are the only goods that are bought abroad.
tactical_explanations:
Not the same as big ones are known. Mozart balls, hazelnut waffles and Sachertorte are popular examples of goods that are bought abroad. Nevertheless, they do not form the lion's share. The section warns against this confusion of image and statistics.

The statement is true.

The most important of these are the positions with which Austria denies most of its exports of goods. Anyone who thinks of souvenirs only reads the wrong list.

The statement is true.

Only speciality products would be deleted from machinery, vehicles, chemicals and processed goods. The presentation mentions these groups as leading and the confectionery only as popular examples. Austria is not a pure food export country here.

Export to more than 200 countries and a high export quota are compatible with a wide shopping cart, not with a single product family. Food can be part of the export, they do not replace the mentioned industrial groups. The exclusivity makes the sentence wrong.

The statement is false.

Services have their own ranking list. Tourism, i.e. holiday and business travel, transport services, technical services and information services, Austrian companies sell to foreign customers. This complements the goods, it does not replace them. Those who only count goods leave this page away.

The statement is true.

Only goods abroad would be a souvenir stand, not an external trade. The description says that those confectionery would like to be bought abroad, but the lion's share lies in machinery, vehicles, processed goods and chemicals. Services are added. The formula of the only goods is wrong.

Many Austrian products are bought abroad, not just two brand articles. The popular examples serve for the view, not the limitation of the export basket. Whoever narrows the basket on Sachertorte and Mozartkugel, contradicts the list of leading articles.

The statement is false.

title: Imports, exports and tourism
context: Evaluate the following statements the relationship between imports and exports and the international involvement of Austrian companies:
statements: For many years, imports have exceeded exports.
The difference between imports and exports was last small.
This difference is offset by surpluses in other areas, such as tourism.
In Austria, an import surplus can never be offset by other areas.
Austrian companies export to more than 200 countries.
tactical_explanations:
Buy more than sell, over years: this is how the section describes the flows of goods. Imports have been exceeding exports for many years. This is a finding of the direction of the difference, not the invitation to memorize a billion-dollar figure. Whoever excludes from this, Austria exports nothing, reads too much in the sentence.

A country can also be export-oriented and import more net goods. This is the combination that captures the representation before it mentions the small difference and the balance of tourism.

The statement is true.

The illustration shows that the difference was small at the last time. The direction of import surplus remains, the extent is small. This nuance prevents the long-term overhang from making a dramatic sluggish situation.

Small and for many years beyond it belong together: the overhang is the rule, but its height is not far at last. Without this second indication one would derive from the first sentence a large gap that the section does not claim to be so.

The statement is true.

Other areas can be counter-booked. Surpluses, for example, in tourism, rebalance the difference. Weighing up means: the gap in one field is compensated by a plus in another field, not that imports and exports are identical. Tourism is the example mentioned, not the only conceivable one, but the one in theory.

The statement is true.

Never balance the sentence about tourism. The section says explicitly that the difference is offset by surpluses in other areas. An import surplus for goods can therefore be offset by surplus services, here tourism. The word "never makes the sentence wrong.

The trade flows and the flow of services are not the same. Anyone who sees only the goods side considers the import overhang to be incomparable. The text of the teaching divides both and calls the compensation. Therefore, the assertion of an impossible compensation does not apply.

The statement is false.

The range is not narrow. Austrian companies export to more than 200 countries around the world. This underlines the global integration in addition to the EU focus. More than 200 is a scale of width, no drill on an exact country list.

The statement is true.

title: Internal market and four fundamental freedoms
context: Evaluate the following statements on international regulations that shape the Austrian economy:
statements: As a member of the European Union, Austria is subject to the internal market with its four fundamental freedoms.
The four fundamental freedoms include the free movement of goods, persons, services and capital.
The EU Customs Union and trade agreements with third countries facilitate access to international markets.
EU membership concerns cultural exchanges only and does not define conditions of trade and competition.
Global rules such as those of the World Trade Organization shape the framework conditions of foreign trade.
tactical_explanations:
Membership is linked to the internal market. Austria is subject to it with its four fundamental freedoms. Underlies here: the rules apply, not that every company automatically sells in each member country. The legal framework of the internal market is the first international block that the section calls after the mere trade volume.

Without this membership, the legal area in which goods, persons, services and capital should be freely traded was lacking. Trade with member states is not only common, but also legally facilitated.

The statement is true.

Four, not three, not five, and precisely these four. Free movement of goods, people, services and capital constitute fundamental freedoms. Anyone who cuts one of these or replaces one with another does not have the list of definitions. Together they describe what should be moved freely in the internal market.

Passenger transport is part of the economic area as well as the flow of goods, capital and services. A shortened list would misunderstand the internal market as a mere tariff reduction.

The statement is true.

Access is facilitated, not guaranteed without a treaty. EU customs union and trade agreements with third countries describe the presentation as instruments that facilitate access to international markets. The right level remains to be eased: fewer customs and agreement barriers, not the abolition of any competition. Third countries are partners here beyond the Union.

The statement is true.

Only culture would hide directives, regulations, customs union and competition rules. The section says that many directives and regulations set the conditions of trade and competition. Membership is an economic framework, not a cultural association. The narrowing to cultural exchange is wrong.

Four fundamental freedoms concern goods, persons, services and capital, i.e. economic movements. Anyone who reads this as a mere cultural exchange fails to comply with the subject matter. Conditions of trade and competition are expressly part of the text. Therefore, the statement of the examination does not stand up.

The statement is false.

The EU is not the only one that sets the framework. Global rules such as those of the World Trade Organization shape the framework conditions for external trade. The WTO stands alongside the internal market and agreements, not instead of theirs. Those who think of foreign trade as a bilateral business without global rules leave this level aside.

The statement is true.

title: Standards and trade agreements
context: Evaluate the following statements on environmental, social and financial standards and trade agreements:
statements: Environmental, social and financial standards such as EU taxonomy, OECD guidelines for multinational companies or Basel regulations in the financial sector influence business strategies and market conditions.
International regulations and agreements are of no importance to the Austrian economy.
Trade agreements such as the EU-Mercosur agreement or bilateral agreements with states such as the US or China play a central role.
Such agreements only secure higher tariffs and prohibit any market access.
The above agreements also set standards for sustainable economic and fair trade.
tactical_explanations:
Standards are part of the control, and not only in brochures. EU taxonomy for sustainable investments, OECD guidelines for multinational companies and Basel regulations in the financial sector influence business strategies and market conditions.

Influence means that companies must include them in plans and markets, not that any investment would automatically be green or any bank rule would be superfluous.

The statement is true.

The whole second half of the section is without meaning. In addition to international trade, international regulations and agreements are of central importance for the Austrian economy. EU internal market, customs union, WTO, taxonomy, OECD, Basel, Mercosur and bilateral agreements are precisely this level. The negation of all meaning is wrong.

Trade without rules would be another chapter. The presentation links flows of goods to legal framework. The central meaning is the formula, not a marginal note. Anyone who declares regulations to be irrelevant, will delete the sentence with which the section introduces this list.

The statement is false.

The central role, not marginality. EU-Mercosur and bilateral agreements with states like the USA or China call this presentation by name. They stand for market access beyond or at the edge of the pure internal market. Whether a certain agreement is politically controversial does not change the theory that they attribute this role.

The statement is true.

Higher tariffs and bans on market access are all over the board, and the agreements guarantee market access and equal competition, which are intended to facilitate access, and the only way to prevent them is to impose higher tariffs on trade agreements within the meaning of the text.

Market access and equal competition are the objectives mentioned above. In addition, there are standards for sustainable economic and fair trade. An agreement that prohibits any market access would not be an instrument of relief. That is why The statement is false.

The statement is false.

Not only quantities and tariffs. The same agreements also set standards for sustainable business and fair trade. The section represents this alongside market access and equal competition. Sustainability and fairness are part of the contract architecture here, not a substitute for trade.

The statement is true.

title: What GDP includes
context: Evaluate the following statements on the definition of gross domestic product:
statements: Gross domestic product includes all goods, i.e. products and services, at market value, produced during a given period within the boundaries of a country.
Der Marktwert entspricht Menge mal Marktpreis.
Intermediate products or intermediate consumption are deducted because they are already included in final production.
GDP only counts material products and basically leaves away services.
GDP measures economic output independently of the place of production and only by nationality of the producers.
tactical_explanations:
Three brackets hold the definition: what, how evaluated, where and when. All goods, products and services, at market value, in a period, within the national borders. This is the gross domestic product as a measure of total economic performance. If one bracket is missing, one measures something else, for example only goods or only domestics worldwide.

The statement is true.

The so-called market value is precisely this product. A larger quantity at the same price also increases the value, a higher market price at the same quantity. Therefore, an increasing GDP can come later also from prices, not only from more pieces.

The statement is true.

Double counting should be prevented. Intermediate products or intermediates are deducted because they are already included in the final production. Wool in the sweater, sheet metal in the car: the final value already carries the pre-value. Without deduction the same output would be twice in total.

The statement is true.

Services are among the goods of this definition. Products and services together, at market value, within borders. Those who only count material products halve the measure. Tourism, transport, technical services and information services would then be invisible, although they are performance.

Goods are both here. The section repeats products and services in the definition of GDP as before in the cycle. Basically, leaving out services contradicts the wording. Therefore, The statement is false.

The statement is false.

Place counts for GDP, not nationality. It is produced within the borders of a country, in a period. Whether the production factors belong to nationals or foreigners is the logic of the gross national product, not of GDP. Whoever measures GDP only according to the pass of the producers, exchanges the two measures.

A foreign commuter working in Austria generates income in the country: that belongs to GDP. Nationality would treat her differently in the BNP. Measuring independently of the place would not be a domestic product. The statement mixes the concepts and is wrong.

The statement is false.

title: Pullovers, wool and double counting
context: Evaluate the following statements on the treatment of intermediate consumption in the calculation of GDP:
statements: When sweaters are produced, the market value of the wool used shall be deducted from the market value of the sweaters.
Without this deduction, the value of the wool would be recorded twice.
Intermediate products are intentionally counted twice to make GDP appear as high as possible.
Intermediate consumption is already included in final production.
GDP adds up each invoice in the supply chain without deduction of intermediate consumption.
tactical_explanations:
Pullover minus wool, not pullover plus wool. The market value of the sweater produced is deducted from the market value of the wool used for production. The final value remains, the intermediate value goes out. The example makes the general rule of intermediate consumption concrete.

The statement is true.

The same wool, once as wool, once in the sweater: this is not to happen. Without a deduction, the value of the wool would be recorded twice. The warning before double counting is the reason for the deduction, not an accountant's mood. Whoever adds both fully, artificially blows up the measured performance.

The statement is true.

Intentionally, twice count to increase GDP, the rule reverses. Intermediate products or intermediate consumption are deducted because they are already included in final production. The aim is to avoid double counting, not maximizing statistics.

A higher GDP by double counting would not be a higher economic output, but a distortion of calculation. The sweater contains the wool already in the market price. To book the same wool once more as its own final performance would be exactly the error that the presentation excludes. Therefore, the intentional statement does not hold.

The statement is false.

Included means: already in the final price. Intermediates are in the final production. Therefore, it is not allowed to add them extra to the sum of the final goods. The sentence gives the reason for the definition without needing the sweater example, and still remains the same thought.

The statement is true.

Any invoice without deduction would be the double counting in series. Wool, yarn, fabric, sweater: four invoices, one performance at the end when measuring final production. GDP deducts intermediate products. Whoever adds all invoices to the full, measures turnover cascades, not the defined overall economic performance.

The market value of the final goods minus intermediate consumption, not the sum of all supplier invoices. The sweater example shows the deduction at one stage, the logic applies to the chain. Without deduction, the value of the wool would be recorded twice, with further stages even more. The statement contradicts the definition and is wrong.

The statement is false.

title: GDP and economic growth
context: Evaluate the following statements on the link between GDP, price level and growth:
statements: GDP is used to determine economic growth.
A higher GDP year-on-year shows real growth, even if only market prices have increased.
The assessment of growth must take into account the development of the general price level.
Higher GDP could have been achieved not only by increased economic output but also by higher market prices.
If the nominal GDP at current prices is adjusted for inflation, real GDP is obtained.
tactical_explanations:
Growth needs a measure, and often it is GDP. If it increases year-on-year, the representation of a grown economy speaks with the later restriction about prices. To attract is: it is used for not that any other measure is forbidden. The rate remains on this use.

Without such a measure, there would be no bridge from the definition of production to the question of whether the economy has grown compared to the previous year. The bridge is GDP, and then comes the price review.

The statement is true.

The restriction is always real, even if only prices rise. A higher GDP could otherwise have been achieved not only by increased economic output but also by higher market prices. Nominal increase without a view of price level does not prove real growth. The word " Always" makes the sentence wrong.

Year-on-year comparison of untested GDP mixes quantity and price. Inflation raises market values, even if the produced quantity remains the same. That is precisely why the distinction between nominal and real GDP follows. Anyone who denies the price path considers each plus to be real performance.

The statement is false.

Price levels are not a piece of jewellery according to statistics. The section says that the development of the general price level should be taken into account. Otherwise, you confuse more expensive goods with more goods. Consideration means: see whether the increase in quantities or prices comes.

The statement is true.

title: GDP per capita as a measure of prosperity

title: Price and quantity offered
context: Evaluate the following statements the relationship between price and quantity offered:

tactical_explanations:
Usually, not as a natural law without exception: The section places the price level at the beginning of the market mechanisms. If the price rises, usually the quantity that providers want to sell increases. This is the one of the two baselines, even before curves, balance or shifts follow.

The reverse conclusion is explicitly the other way around in the text. If the achievable selling price is lower, the quantity offered is the lower, not the higher. If you have more to offer if the price decreases, the offer function twists. Providers hold back or produce less if the sale does not bring in much.

Low price means lower willingness to market existing quantities and lower incentive to use capacity. The claim that there is an increase in supply at lower price contradicts this line.

The statement is false.

Before the price attracts the quantity, production technology limits the possible. The quantity offered naturally depends on how much can be produced with the existing resources at all. Apart from that, the selling price comes as the second reason for determination.

If you see only the price, you overlook the resource limit; if you see only the resources, you overlook the price incentive.

Doing away or forsaking: At high prices, consumers try to buy or completely renounce a similar good at a lower price. Both lower the required amount of the original good. The presentation calls these reactions immediately after the laxity argument.

Substitution and waiver are therefore part of the same price-quantity relationship, not a later chapter.
