The bidder's sales volume would be significantly larger than the offer, i.e. an imbalance at too high price. In balance, the quantities correspond. The assertion of a permanent surplus on the part of the offerer fails to compensate for the market clearance price.

The statement is false.

title: At low price and lack of quantity
context: Evaluate the following statements at a price below balance:
statements: A lower price than the equilibrium price leads to an imbalance.
At a price too low, demand is rising and supply is decreasing.
There is an excessive demand and a shortage due to the scarcity of the good.
A price below balance will allow the market to be even more perfect than the market clearance price.
The shortfall arises because at low price more wants to be bought and can be offered while less is offered.
tactical_explanations:
The text of the teaching says this directly: a lower price leads to an imbalance, because demand increases and at the same time the supply decreases. Balance depended on the quantity equality. This equality is broken here. Whoever considers the lower price to be an even better eviction, confuses cheaply with balanced.

The market clearance price was, for example, 3.50 euros, below which the shears of the quantities opened.

The statement is true.

Two movements at the same time: demand rises, supply decreases. This is exactly how the sales describe the situation below the equilibrium price. The demanders want and can do more, the suppliers want and can do less. From these scissors the lack arises, not from a single curve alone.

The supply function provides the smaller quantity, the demand function the larger; together they are the lack.

Low price dampens supply because the price that can be achieved is falling and stimulates demand because more households can bear the price. Both sets of the mechanism are simultaneously working. The representation needs this "at the same time", otherwise there would be only one one-sided history.

The statement is true.

Excessive demand and lack of quantity: The presentation links both to the scarcity of the good in this price situation. Lack means that the quantity required exceeds the quantity offered. Shortness is visible at the too low price, because the price no longer achieves its coordination in balance. That is the underprice side of the mechanism.

If you say "many people want to buy", without the simultaneously decreasing offer, the shortfall has only half explained. The paragraph needs both sides, and the statement mentions both consequences.

The statement is true.

Perfect eviction is part of the equilibrium price, the market clearance price. Among these, a shortage of resources is occurring: the market sides no longer fit together. An even lower price does not allow for better, it deepens the imbalance. The statement distorts the coordination function.

The statement is false.

More will to buy and purchasing power, less offer: This creates the lack of content, even if the word is only in the next sentence of the text. Low price stimulates demand and dampens supply. The difference is the uncovered rest. The sentence translates the two quantity movements into lack without inventing another cause.

The scarcity of the good is visible in this price situation, because more is demanded than is offered.

Excessive demand is the same situation with a view to the buyer side. Missing quantity names the rest that is not served. Both follow from scissors, not from a coincidence outside of price, supply and demand.

The statement is true.

title: At high price and oversupply
context: Evaluate the following statements at a price above balance:
statements: A higher price than the equilibrium price also leads to an imbalance.
At too high a price, the supply increases and demand decreases at the same time.
There is an overhang in the offer.
A price above equilibrium in this section creates a shortage of scarcity.
Both differences show the coordination function of price: price coordinates the decisions of suppliers and demanders.
tactical_explanations:
The text explicitly sets the higher price in addition to the lower one: also an imbalance. Quantity equality is lost again, only with the opposite sign. Whoever only considers the underprice situation as a disturbance, has not read the second half of the paragraph.

The statement is true.

Supply is rising, demand is falling: this is the volume response above the equilibrium price. Suppliers want and can sell more, demanders want and can buy less. The scissors open to the other side than in the case of the lack. Both movements run simultaneously, not one after the other in any order.

The statement is true.

The overhang is the name of this location. More is available for sale than is and can be bought. The surplus is on the supplier's side, not as a shortage of buyers. The term is firmly at the high price in this section.

Overhang and lack of quantity are mirror images. Whoever swaps them has misallocated the price relative to the balance. Here the price is too high, so overhang.

The statement is true.

Lack of quantity and scarcity in this sense are part of the low price. In the case of the too high price, the goods are not too scarcely offered, but too abundantly relative to the demand: oversupply. The statement adheres to the underprice consequences to the overprice situation and is therefore wrong.

The statement is false.

Coordination through price: This is precisely what the presentation reads from both imbalances. Price coordinates the decisions of suppliers and demanders. Higher prices stimulate supply and dampen demand, low prices do the reverse. Without this function, deviations would be merely numbers, not a mechanism.

The supplier decides on sales and production, the buyer on purchase and waiver. The common signaling device is the price. The sentence holds this role without formulating the tendency of price return; which follows in the next step of the paragraph.

The statement is true.

title: Prize as coordinator
context: Evaluate the following statements on the coordination function of the price:
statements: Higher prices stimulate supply and dampen demand, so that prices tend to fall again.
Low prices stimulate demand and dampen supply, so prices tend to rise again.
Der Preis hat in diesem Abschnitt keine Koordinierungsfunktion.
Both a price too high and a price too low lead to an imbalance.
Only the demanders are coordinated by the price; suppliers always ignore the price.
tactical_explanations:
Stimulate and dampen upwards: higher prices attract supply and slow demand. The result is a pressure that tends to lower prices again, towards the compensation. The text describes not only the situation, but the return movement. Tendually, it means: direction, not a guarantee for every week.

Supply overhang is first created; the overhang itself is the reason why the price does not have to stay up.

More quantities offered for smaller quantities of demand make unsold goods or unused capacity visible. Suppliers then tend to undercut themselves, the price is falling. Thus, the high price coordinates the return by pulling the quantities apart and producing the exact counter pressure.

The statement is true.

Mirror image downwards: Low prices arouse demand and dampen supply, so prices tend to rise again. Lack of quantity and excessive demand create upward pressure. Together with the other trend, coordination closes to a circle around the equilibrium price.

The low price dampening follows from the supply function, stimulating demand from the demand function. The price sets both in motion simultaneously. The rate includes exactly this double effect and the rising price tendency.

The statement is true.

No coordination function to claim, cancels the final rate of the equilibrium section. Price coordinates the decisions of suppliers and demanders. Higher and lower prices trigger counter-measures of volume and counter-price trends. Without this function, lack of quantity and overhang remained unsettled.

The statement is false.

Both deviations, one finding: Lower price and higher price lead to an imbalance, only with a shortage here and oversupply there. The market clearance price is the exception without price tendency. Whoever only makes one of the two situations considered an imbalance halves the mechanism.

Coordination needs both mirror images, otherwise there would be only one way of adapting.

The statement is true.

Providers do not ignore the price. The supply function and the capacity and entry reactions depend on the price that can be achieved, the marginal cost decision as well. Coordination affects both sides. The restriction to demanders and the "always" make the sentence wrong.

The willingness to sell, increase in quantities, enter and exit the markets in the surrounding sales are supplier reactions to the price. Whoever denies them only retains the demand curve and loses half of the coordination.

The statement is false.

title: Income shifts demand
context: Evaluate the following statements how the income of the demander influences the demand curve:
statements: Demand is influenced by, among other things, the available income of the demander.
If income increases and demanders can afford more, the demand for quantity usually increases at any given price level, and the demand curve shifts to the right.
If income falls, the demand curve shifts to the left.
A higher income usually shifts the demand curve to the left.
With lower incomes, many consumers cannot afford the goods in this quantity, so the demand for the quantity decreases at any given price level.
tactical_explanations:
Income is included in the list of other factors influencing the economy, alongside preferences, comparable goods and complementary goods. It is no longer a question of moving on the curve at other prices, but rather of factors that shift demand itself. Anyone who sees income as a private matter without a market reference fails to see this paragraph.

The statement is true.

More, more quantity at any price: If income rises, the required quantity usually rises at any given price level. Graphically, this is a shift of the demand curve to the right. The price remains fixed in this consideration, the whole curve wanders. This is something different than a slide on the same curve, because the price of the good itself falls.

The statement usually holds the text. Not every good has to react in this way; the teaching text sets the typical direction. Right shift means: At 3.50 euros as with any other price more is demanded than before.

The statement is true.

In the case of loss of income, if income falls, the opposite happens, says the section. The curve shifts to the left. Again, at any given price level, not only at one point. Left means less demanded quantity on the whole price scale.

The statement is true.

The direction described turns left at higher income. Higher income usually shifts to the right, lower to the left. The statement takes the wrong side and is wrong.

The statement is false.

No longer afford in this amount: Many demanders can no longer afford the goods, the demanded quantity decreases at every given price level. The representation justifies the left shift. It is the same logic as with the high price, only that here the income falls, while the goods price is recorded in the curve view.

Leasibility links demand to skill. Less income, less skill, less quantity on the whole curve. The rate remains within the paragraph about income changes.

The statement is true.

title: Preferences and bicycle demand
context: During the Coronavirus pandemic, demand for bicycles increased. Evaluate the following statements about preferences and this example:
statements: The preferences or preferences of the buyers play a role in their demand.
If there is a trend towards a particular product or service, demand for it is increasing.
Bicycles were a means of transport in the pandemic with a lower risk of infection and a sport opportunity when sports facilities were closed.
Buyer preferences do not play a role in demand.
Production could not keep pace with increased bicycle demand; many buyers had to wait for months.
tactical_explanations:
Preferentials include: The section explicitly mentions preferences or preferences as an influence on demand, alongside income and other goods. Demand is not only price and purse, but also what households consider desirable. A trend can bundle these preferences and shift the curve without the price of the good itself being the trigger.

The statement is true.

Trend as a boost to demand: If there is a trend towards a particular product or service, demand increases. This is the general rule before the bicycle example makes it clear. Increasing demand here means the shift of the whole demand, not just a point on the old curve.

The statement is true.

Two reasons in the lesson example: hard to infect when cycling, and sports when sports facilities had to close. Both are changed preferences and benefit expectations in the pandemic, not a falling bicycle price as the only reason. The sentence gives the reason for the text.

Transportation and replacement sports explain why households suddenly wanted to buy more bikes and could buy them. The preference shifted to the bike. That's exactly how the example is under the heading of changed preferences.

The statement is true.

No role of preferences is claimed, one of the factors mentioned is eliminated. Preferentials, trends and the bicycle example would be superfluous. Sales exist precisely because preferences determine demand. The statement is false.

The statement is false.

Production did not keep pace: Many buyers had to wait for months for the ordered bicycle. The example shows a demand that runs away from the supply, i.e. a kind of shortage in the short period, triggered by the preference boost, not by an administratively too low fixed price. The presentation maintains this delay in delivery.

Waiting here is the visible form that the requested quantity exceeds the short term offered. The rule of preferences and the concrete example interlock. The sentence remains on the teaching text.

The statement is true.

title: Complementary and comparable goods
context: Evaluate the following statements on the influence of complementary and comparable goods on demand:
statements: If there are additional new and meaningful complementary products or services, demand can increase overall.
If comparable goods are more innovative or cost less, the demand for the original goods is decreasing.
If buyers can evade another product or service, the demand for the original product is decreasing.
Additional goods always reduce the demand for the raw material in this section.
Comparable cheaper goods always increase the demand for the more expensive original goods.
tactical_explanations:
Addition as a demand increase: New and meaningful complementary products or services can increase demand overall. The bike needs lock and helmet, the smartphone a cover: the presentation remains general, the direction is clear. Addition supports or expands demand, it does not replace the original goods.

The opposite is exactly the case in the next sentence for comparable goods. Whoever throws both in the same pot loses the difference between co-use and replacement.

The statement is true.

Comparable, innovative, cheaper: then demand for the original good decreases. That is the opposite of the supplement. Substitution deducts purchasing power. Anyone who only knows supplementation does not understand why a new model weakens the old one.

Innovative or less cost: The presentation calls both triggers. It does not have to be both at the same time. Even one of the two characteristics of comparable goods can push the original demand.

The statement is true.

The mechanism behind substitution is to avoid it. If buyers can switch to another product or service, the demand for the original product is falling. This follows on from the earlier reaction to high prices, but also applies here because the alternative has become better or cheaper.

The demand curve of the original product then shifts to the left, not because the income fell, but because a comparative product became more attractive.

More innovative, less expensive, or both: the sales leaves these paths open. As soon as it is possible to avoid, the original goods no longer carry the same demand. The sentence adheres to this causality.

The statement is true.

The section notes the exact opposite of substitution. "Still reducing the role of complementary goods is twisted and is wrong. Lock to the bicycle does not make the bike superfluous. Meaningful supplement does not relieve the demand, it does not pull it off. The absolute downsizing claim fails this direction.

The statement is false.

Cheaper comparators are pulling demand off, they do not increase it for the more expensive original goods. Evacuating lowers the original demand. "Always increase the reverse substitution and thus wrong. The text says the opposite: comparable goods that are more innovative and/or less cost the demand for the original goods is pushing.

Those who think the original product more expensive and the comparative product more favorable expect emigration, not a boost in demand during the teuren. The absolute increase word choice reverses the described direction.

The statement is false.

title: Market entry and supply curve
context: Evaluate the following statements to make the offer change:
statements: If more suppliers enter a market because they consider it profitable, the quantity offered increases and the supply curve shifts to the right.
If the offer is so high that prices are starting to fall, no more suppliers will push into the market.
Technical developments and falling costs for the necessary resources could lead more suppliers to enter the market.
Market entry of additional suppliers always shifts the supply curve to the left.
Only the demand curve can shift; the supply curve remains immobile in this section.
tactical_explanations:
Profitable, so enter, so more quantity: The supply curve shifts to the right. This is the supply side of the curve shift, parallel to the right shift in demand at higher incomes. More suppliers mean a larger quantity offered at given prices, not just one point higher up on the same old curve.

Ceteris paribus along the curve would be just another price of goods; here the number of suppliers changes, i.e. the whole curve.

The statement is true.

Falling prices as a stop signal: If the offer is so high that prices start to fall, no more suppliers are pushing into the market. Entry ends when profitability decreases. The presentation thus combines volume expansion and price response before price expectations follow as their own factor.

The right shift has a limit. Infinitely many newcomers despite falling prices do not assume the paragraph. The sentence returns this limit.

The statement is true.

Technology and cheaper resources: Both could cause more suppliers to enter the market. Lower costs improve profitability, technical development as well. The offer then increases not only above the price of goods itself, but above the cost side of production. The text puts these factors at the end of the supply influences.

The marginal costs in a wider sense make the expansion of quantities more viable, because the price that can be achieved covers the additional units more easily.

Entry from this direction shifts the supply curve to the right, as long as the market is considered profitable. This is the same graphic movement as when entering due to high prices, only with other triggers. The rate remains with technology and resource costs.

The statement is true.

To the left, if you enter, less offer would be despite more companies. The representation shifts to the right. "Still to the left, the wrong direction of the offer curve is wrong. More providers, higher offered quantity, curve to the right: that is the chain. Left shift would mean exit or cost shocks to the top, not the described entry.

The statement is false.

Claiming immovable supply pushes the whole sales over factors of influence on supply. Entry, price expectations, technology and resource costs shift the supply curve. Demand shifts exist beside it, they do not monopolize the graphics.

Those who only allow the demand side to wander can no longer graphically represent market entry and falling costs.

Right on entry, stop at falling prices, reaction to expected prices: all these are movements or attitudes of the supply curve. The assertion of permanent immobility is wrong.

The statement is false.

title: Price expectations of suppliers
context: Evaluate the following statements on the role of price expectations on the supply side:
statements: Price expectations play a decisive role in the offer.
If the suppliers expect more and more prices for their goods, they will remain in the market and increase their offer.
If the providers expect falling prices, the opposite is the case.
Price expectations of the providers do not play a role in the offer.
In the expectation of falling prices, the providers inevitably increase their offer further.
tactical_explanations:
The text formulates the price expectations, immediately after the stop of further admission at falling prices. It is not only about the price today, but about the price that providers expect for the future. This expectation controls staying, going and the quantity offered. Anyone who only knows the current market price does not yet have this factor.

Ceteris paribus's offer function holds on to other things; expectation is just another factor that can shift the offered quantity.

Today, low prices and yet more offer would be conceivable if rising prices were expected and stored or invested. The presentation remains with the simple rule: increasing expectation, staying and increasing; falling expectation, the opposite. The decisive role is precisely this setting.

The statement is true.

Increasing prices expected: Then the suppliers stay in the market and increase their offer. Hope for higher proceeds keeps them and expands the quantity. This reinforces the right side of the supply curve as long as the expectation bears. The rate is the positive half of the expectation mechanism.

Staying and increasing belong together. It is not only a renunciation of exit, but an active set reaction. The representation says both.

The statement is true.

The opposite is expected. Providers do not stay in the same way and do not increase the offer; logic turns around. Sales just take this as the opposite, after formulating the rising expectation. Those who still expect to start with volume expansion have not read the opposite.

Withdrawal or withdrawal of quantities will fit to falling revenues in the future, not additional entry.

The statement is true.

No role of expectations is contrary to the sentence of the decisive role. Current price, entrance and cost factors were then sufficient, the expectation of the future was not. The section calls it specifically. The statement is wrong because it removes an expressly mentioned influence.

Staying or going also depends on where the price is going, not only on where it stands today.

The statement is false.

Indispensably further increase in expected falling prices is the opposite of the text rule. Falling price expectations dampen the offer, it does not drive it. "Undoubtedly" makes the wrong direction additionally rigid.

Note: The text speaks of a "decisive" role; meaning the strong meaning of expectation alongside today's price, not another technical term.

The statement is false.

title: Gleichgewicht, Verschiebungen, ceteris paribus
context: On the grain market of the example, the market clearance price is 3.50 euros per kilogram. Evaluate the following statements about the interaction of the mechanisms:
statements: The quantity offered and requested at the market clearance price is consistent and usually price trends are missing upwards or downwards.
If the income of the demanders increases, the demand curve usually shifts to the right, i.e. to a higher quantity at given price level.
Technical developments can encourage more suppliers to enter the market and thus increase the offer.
Under ceteris paribus conditions, the higher the price, the higher the quantity required.
Meaningful complementary goods can increase demand overall, while innovative or cheaper comparator goods can reduce demand for the original goods.
tactical_explanations:
Clearing and calm: 3.50 euros in the example equals the quantities. The market is completely cleared, the price therefore also means market clearance price. Usually there are no price trends upwards or downwards. This is the point of reference from which the lack of quantity, overhang and curve shifts are first understood.

25 tons on both sides of the lesson make the agreement tangible. Without this equality of quantities, there would not be the described rest. The sentence combines definition and ordinary price tendency.

The statement is true.

Income to the right: At any given price level, i.e. also at 3.50 euros, more is usually asked. The curve wanders, the old equilibrium price is no longer a matter of course the new compensation. The sales of further factors separates this shift from the movement on the curve, which only changes the price of goods.

The statement is true.

Technology attracts entry: Technical developments and also falling resource costs could cause more suppliers to enter the market. More suppliers increase the quantity offered, the supply curve shifts to the right. On the grain market, this would mean that more grains are for sale at the same kilogram prices. The rate is consistent with this supply channel.

Entry from profitability and entry from cheaper technology are related. Both wide the range of offers. The teaching text specifically mentions the technical page, so that costs and innovation are not confused with the price of goods themselves.

The statement is true.

Ceteris paribus on the demand side runs the other way around: the higher the demand for the lower the price. A higher price usually lowers the demand for the quantity. The statement distorts the demand function and mixes it with the supply function, where the higher price increases the quantity.

Note: Movement on the curve (price of the good itself) is not the same operation as a shift of the curve through income, preferences or other goods.

The statement is false.

Complement and comparison as opposites: New useful complementary products can increase demand overall. Comparable goods that are more innovative or cost less reduce demand for the original product because buyers evade. The final part of the demand sales needs both directions, otherwise only the income would remain as a shift factor.

Bicycle plus lock is supplement; a cheaper e-bike as a replacement for the old bike is comparison. The statement holds this duplication and remains in the teaching text.

The statement is true.

title: What determines the competitive situation
context: Evaluate the following statements on the determination of the competitive situation on the market:
statements: The competitive situation on the market is primarily dependent on the number of suppliers for a particular commodity.
It is also important whether or not there are comparable goods that can replace the goods.
The market form is based solely on the number of customers and never on the number of suppliers.
Without looking at replacement goods, the description of the competitive situation remains incomplete.
As soon as any good is traded, the same competitive situation is always present, regardless of the number of suppliers and substitutes.
tactical_explanations:
First, how many sellers offer the same good. One supplier, few or very many: depends on the rough classification. The section puts the number of suppliers at the beginning, not the taste of the clientele and not the legal form of the businesses. Who counts only the demander misses the first line of the text.

The statement is true.

In addition to the number of the sellers, the replacement question is also raised. If there are comparable goods, one can avoid them; if there is no such thing, one remains with the goods offered. This is precisely the alternative or lack of them, which determines how hard competition works.

The statement is true.

Demanders later play a role in Monopson and Oligopson, but they do not replace the number of suppliers as the first size. Only and never delete exactly what the presentation precedes: the number of suppliers for a particular good. Reading a market form only from the demand side distorts the order of the section.

The competitive situation depends primarily on the suppliers. Comparable goods are added. The demand side defines special cases like the monopson, not the whole typology. Whoever declares suppliers to be irrelevant can no longer distinguish monopoly, oligopoly and polypole. The absolute restriction on demanders is therefore wrong.

The statement is false.

Replacement goods decide whether customers are bound or can change. If this look is missing, only one head count remains without alternative. The text of the teaching mentions both: number of suppliers and comparable goods. Incomplete would be a description that allows only one of the two sizes.

The statement is true.

Cocoa, rail and mobile are not the same world of competition, just because something is sold. Number of suppliers and substitutes differ from monopoly, oligopoly and polypole. Constantion always maintains the same situation, where the section introduces different situations. Trade itself does not create a uniform market form.

Bringing a good on a market is not enough. A single railway operator, three mobile operators and a thousand farmers are in completely different circumstances. Without the number of suppliers and without the question of replacement, the situation remains undetermined. The assertion of an always same situation contradicts the whole subsection.

The statement is false.

title: Only one supplier: the monopoly
context: Evaluate the following statements to monopoly as a market form:
statements: If there is only one supplier and a larger number of respondents, it is a monopoly.
In market economy regimes, monopolies are rare, but possible.
A monopoly requires that the same seller worldwide dominates the entire production of all related goods.
In some countries, for example, there is only one provider of rail transport.
Ein Monopol liegt nur dann vor, wenn es weder Nachfrager noch irgendein handelbares Gut gibt.
tactical_explanations:
One seller, many buyers: that is the basic figure. The presentation links both, not the sole supplier without customers. Railways in some countries is the school example. Anyone who confuses monopoly with no market at all, reads the monologue of the provider side wrongly.

The statement is true.

Market economy does not mean that only providers are impossible. They rarely occur, but the section explicitly allows them. Rarely is not never. Possibility and frequency are two sentences, both in the text.

The statement is true.

The monopoly refers to a certain good and the number of suppliers for it, not to the world domination over all related products. A railway monopoly in the domestic market remains a monopoly, even if buses, aircraft or other railways exist elsewhere. The worldwide omnipotence is an invention that takes the definition of the local and goods-related boundary.

Only one supplier of a good is enough to meet many of the demanders. Related goods in other markets or in other countries are not a condition of definition. Those who demand total global control almost never make a monopoly on a clear case. The text of the teaching is more narrow and concrete.

The statement is false.

Rail transport with a single provider is the example of the section. It illustrates that monopolies exist without any country having to be organised in such a way. The example bears the definition, it does not replace them with a duty for all states.

The statement is true.

Without a demander there would be no market where a single supplier could set prices. The monopoly needs a larger number of demanders. Only then, if no one buys and nothing is traded, the figure turns around. Empty space is not a monopoly.

The condition neither the buyer nor the good describes the opposite of a market. Absolute words like only and neither-nor make an empty quantity of a market form. That does not apply to the definition.

The statement is false.

title: State and railway monopoly
context: Evaluate the following statements on the role of the State in monopolies:
statements: If there is a monopoly, the state is usually involved.
The economic interest may be that the company offers services at affordable prices, such as rail connections to sparsely populated areas.
State participation in a railway monopoly excludes any public interest in affordable prices.
Monopolies are completely impossible in market economies by law and therefore never occur.
The State may have an interest in serving routes with low population density.
tactical_explanations:
The text of the teaching is linked to the public sector alone. Not every private kiosk is meant, but typical large cases such as rail transport. Generally, exceptions are allowed, but they describe the normal case of participation. Without the state, the picture of the section would be incomplete.

The statement is true.

Thinly populated areas often do not count on the ticket price alone. Nevertheless, the connection can be economically desirable. Easy-to-use prices and surface areas belong to each other: the state is bound by the monopoly, because supply and price should not be left to the chance of less payable passengers.

The statement is true.

The opposite is the case. Participation does not mean prohibiting affordable prices, but rather securing them in the public interest. Anyone who declares state role and cheap tickets incompatible, twists the example of the railway. Interest in affordable prices is the reason, not its exclusion.

The way into the area, prices that remain viable: that is the motive. A state that participates does not do so in theory in order to eliminate any price interest. The absolute formulation that any public interest is excluded does not hold up any line of the section.

The statement is false.

Rare, but possible: this is the market economy line. Completely impossible and never stronger words than the representation are allowed. Rail monopolies in some countries prove the possibility. Anyone claiming total legal impossibility contradicts example and formulation.

Market economy does not exclude monopolies from the world. It makes them unusual, not unthinkable. The word never turns a cautious statement into a false absolute. The railway example alone suffices as a counter-evidence.

The statement is false.

The density of the settlements and the network of routes are divided: where few live, few travel, but the connection can still be desired. The description calls for the macroeconomic interest. The state depends on the monopoly, so that such routes do not simply disappear.

The statement is true.

title: Monopson on the demand side
context: Evaluate the following statements to monopson in contrast to monopoly:
statements: If there were only one buyer on the demand side and many suppliers, this market form would be called monopson.
Monopson and Monopol are the same market form because both words start with Mono.
The Monopson is the only one on the demand side, not a single provider.
Many respondents and only one provider describe a monopson.
The distinction between monopoly and monopson depends on the market side of the single.
tactical_explanations:
The parenthesis of the text turns the figure around: one buyer, many sellers. That's what the name Monopson stands for. It's the mirrored monogram, not a second word for the same sole supplier. Without this page, only the monopoly would remain in sight.

The statement is true.

The common beginning of the word does not create a common market form. Monopoly: one supplier, many respondents. Monopson: one buyer, many suppliers. Whoever puts the two into one confuses Vorsilbe with definition. The presentation expressly separates them.

Mono marks the number, but does not say which side it sits on. The supplier side and the demand side give two forms. Making the same market form out of it deletes exactly the sentence in the parenthesis. The equation is wrong. Whoever hears only the common word beginning, overlooks that the text of the teaching sets the parenthesis extra: one demander, many suppliers.

Without this page specification Mono would remain an empty label. Railways with an operator remain monopoly, a single state shopping center would be Monopson compared to many suppliers. The words are related and still not interchangeable.

The statement is false.

One buyer, many suppliers: the special feature is when buying, not when selling. The sole supplier is a monopoly. Whoever thinks the monopson from the only seller has switched pages. The text of the lesson holds the demand side.

The statement is true.

Many respondents plus a provider is the definition of the monopoly. The monopson demands the reverse structure. The assignment in the sentence is side-floated and therefore wrong.

A railway company compared to many passengers is not a monopson. Monopson would be a single purchasing place compared to many supplying companies. The swapped numbers make the right concept the wrong picture. That's not how it stands.

The statement is false.

Single number at the supplier or single number at the buyer: this is the dividing line. The same head number on the other side gives the other name. Without page specification mono-words remain blurred. The sentence keeps the classification of the text.

The statement is true.

title: Theatre buffet and mountain hut
context: Evaluate the following statements to monopolistic positions in certain situations or regions:

title: Fleisch gegen Kleidung
context: Evaluate the following statements on the topic of money as an exchange medium in the economic cycle:

tactical_explanations:
Without generally accepted money, only the immediate exchange of goods for goods remains. Named for ancient and early historical societies and the everyday example of meat for clothing. Both sides must then offer a good that the other wants. Exactly this narrowness makes the exchange difficult or impossible, as soon as the wishes do not fit together.

The meat seller must want clothes at the same time, otherwise the mutual fit is missing. If he does not need a jacket or if he wants it later, the meat remains unsold, although both goods are present. Money breaks this blockade, because the seller receives a generally accepted equivalent value and can later buy something else.

The text of the teaching makes this moment the basic problem of exchange without payment.

The statement is true.

Acceptance as a means of payment opens the circle of possible shops. Whoever gives meat, advice or repairs takes money because he can trust to use it again for products and services. Once everyone acknowledges the same exchange means, the search for a suitable counter-good at the same moment is no longer necessary.

Many exchange relationships in the cycle are thus only practical.

The statement is true.

According to the text of the teaching, the economic cycle needs money precisely because exchange relationships without this means are difficult or impossible to achieve. To exchange goods for goods fails as soon as a page does not want the offered goods. The claim that without money the exchange is always easy or even better puts the starting position of the section on the head.

The statement is false.

Anyone who sells meat for money does not have to ask for clothes, bread or a service from the buyer at the same time. Money stores the possibility of buying until the next business. This is exactly how the exchange agent solves the problem that both sides need exactly the good of the others at the same moment.

The statement is true.

title: Trust in exchange value

Trust means that you can buy it again later. Whoever accepts money today does so because he can expect to use the same amount as a means of payment tomorrow. The money value does not depend in the text of the teaching on the beauty of the banknote, but on the security to receive products and services. If you can buy with the amount, the money carries exchange value. If this security is reduced, the reason for accepting money also disappears. The value is thus measured in the future purchase possibility, not in a mere imprint.

Paper or metal alone do not explain the money functions as long as this exchange value remains uncertain.

The statement is true.

Without this trust, the functions remain on paper. Exchanges, value meters and value-keeping devices presuppose that economic operators acknowledge the exchange value and give or accept money. The section explicitly states that trust in this exchange value is a prerequisite. Without it, the other functions do not operate.

The statement is true.

Acceptance does not arise from paper or metal by itself. If no one accepts the money later, you can buy nothing with it, and the exchange value collapses. Being a means of payment means being accepted by all. The claim that money works without later assumption contradicts the condition of trust.

The statement is false.

The fact that all accept the same means is the short form of acceptance. The standard is the same as the means of exchange and means of payment in this context: money is accepted by all as means of payment (tauschmittel). This very general assumption makes an object a generally usable means of exchange in the cycle.

The statement is true.

Exchange relations without common unity remain couples: meat for clothing, bread for advice. Every new commodity needs new relations with all others. Money as a value measure replaces this net with a uniform measure. Direct exchange of goods is exactly the case, which the representation describes as difficult or impossible if desires do not fit together.

In terms of money units, the values are comparable without any need to renegotiate each pair.

The statement is true.

Two names, two tasks. Exchange means the acceptance of the business. Value measure means the expression and comparison of goods values in monetary units. It applies side by side and adds the value retention as a third. Whoever merges the first two into a single function, erases this distinction.

To be a means of payment means to be accepted in exchange. To be a value measure means to make prices and relative values visible in a unit. Both need trust, but they are not the same actions. A sign in euro compares, a transfer pays. The assertion of identity is wrong.

The statement is false.

If there is a euro amount on the sign, the value of the good is expressed in monetary units. This is exactly what the value measure describes. The amount allows comparison with other goods, which are also awarded in euros. The price is thus the everyday form of this function, not a separate idea.

The statement is true.

Services are among the goods whose value can be expressed in money. The exchange value of money is precisely to be able to buy products and services. A consultation, treatment or repair carries a price in money units as well as bread or clothing. The restriction on physical products is therefore too narrow.

The statement is false.

title: Wertaufbewahrung durch Sparen
context: Evaluate the following statements on money as a value-storage instrument:
statements: Money can save value, for example by saving.
The amount of savings can be measured in money.
Value-added means that money may be held exclusively in coins under the mattress.
Those who save use money as a measure of the amount covered and as a carrier of the stored value.
As soon as money is a means of exchange, any value retention function ceases, because each amount must be issued immediately.
tactical_explanations:
Saving is the textbook case of storing value. The amount covered remains available in money until it is later used for goods. Thus, one does not preserve the concrete bread of today, but the exchange value in a generally accepted form. This is exactly how the representation describes the third function alongside the means of exchange and value measure.

Without this holding option, every inflow would have to turn into a good at the same moment.

The statement is true.

Measurement and storage are combined. The amount of savings is expressed in money units, not in pieces of meat or in meters of fabric. This number makes the value travelled comparable and predictable. The section mentions both in one sentence: measure and keep the value with money.

If you can only measure, but can't hold, or just hoard, without being able to specify the height, the book formulation only hits half.

The statement is true.

Under the mattress is only one possible form, and theory does not force anyone to do so. Cash in coins and banknotes is familiar, book money in the account is also money. Value retention means keeping the value in money, not a certain hiding technique. The restriction on coins under the mattress is therefore wrong.

Cash and book money are both forms of money as long as the trust in the exchange value carries. Savings can be on the account and still fulfill the value retention function. Anyone who only lets coins under the pillow apply confuses a vivid scene with the definition.

The statement is false.

Two sides of an action: the saving amount has a value in money, and the same money carries the value through time. The representation explicitly connects measurements and retention. Whoever saves uses value meters and value storage devices at the same time, without one of the two functions replacing the other.

The statement is true.

Being a means of exchange does not mean having to spend every amount on the same day. It is precisely because money is to be used as a means of payment that it can be kept between two purchases. The retention of value relies on this trust. The assertion that means of exchange redeem storage, deletes the third function, which the theory specifically calls.

The statement is false.

title: Cash and book money
context: Evaluate the following statements to forms of money:
statements: Cash is available in the form of banknotes and coins.
Book money is money in bank accounts.
Money is also available in different currencies.
Only coins are considered money; banknotes and bank accounts do not count.
Book money is something abstract that you cannot see and attack, and yet of the utmost importance.
tactical_explanations:
Coins in the pocket and notes in the cash register are the familiar form. Cash is explicitly called banknotes and coins. This physical form remains a means of payment as long as it is accepted. However, it is not the only form of money.

The statement is true.

Account balances are book money. The amount exists as credits on a bank account, not as stacks of coins in the drawer of the bank. Transfers move exactly this book money. The section juxtaposes cash and book money as the first distinction of the forms of money. Currencies form the second level; both are forms of money, not rival definitions.

The statement is true.

Besides the distinction between cash and book money, the presentation of currencies is called a second form. The same economic means appears as euro, franc or dollar, depending on which money a state recognises as a means of payment. Thus, the variety of currencies is one of the forms of money, not on a later, foreign subject.

The statement is true.

Only coins are allowed to apply, and banknotes and book money are removed. These include banknotes for cash and account balances for book money. Both are forms of money. The narrowing on coins contradicts the enumeration and would make the vast majority of the money circulating invisible.

Banknotes are cash as well as coins. Book money in the account is money, even if you cannot grasp it. Whoever only makes hard money, misses both lines of the section: the physical form is wider than the coin, and the abstract form is even the larger circulation part.

The statement is false.

Abstract means: not visible, not tangible, and yet central. Book money gains further in importance through cashless payment. It is available by order, for example by bank transfer, not by coin stack. According to the text of the teaching, invisibility does not reduce the meaning nor, if there is trust, the value towards cash.

On the contrary, the far greater part of the money being circulating is precisely this invisible form.

The statement is true.

title: Giral money in the account
context: Evaluate the following statements on book money or giral money:
statements: Book money is also called giral money and is not physically available in contrast to cash.
Book money exists only in one account.
Because book money is not physical, it is inevitably worth less than the same amount in cash.
Book money is provided by giving the order to transfer a certain amount.
Book money and cash are used as long as people trust to exchange money for products and services.
tactical_explanations:
Two names, the same thing. Book money or giral money is in contrast to cash, because it is not physically, not physically, available. It is not a coin on the table, but an entry in the account. The lack of grippability is the defining feature, not a blemish that devalues the amount.

If you think that Giralgeld is something other than book money, you can double the term of the text without need.

The statement is true.

Only in the account does this amount exist as book money. Without an account there would be no carrier for Giral money. The disposition runs through orders to the bank, not via passing on a note. The section places existence on the account and disposition by transfer into a direct connection.

The statement is true.

Non-physicality does not automatically reduce value. Of course, even if book money is not physically available, it is still worth as much as cash. The prerequisite remains the confidence to be able to exchange both products and services. The assertion of an inevitably lower value contradicts this sentence.

A euro on the account and a euro as a coin should bear the same exchange value as long as both are accepted. Whoever concludes a depreciation from the abstraction confuses visibility with value. The text of the teaching explicitly separates both.

The statement is false.

The order is called order. The bank is given a certain amount to transfer, and thus moves book money without drawing any notes out of the pocket. Most deposits and withdrawals to a bank account are thus cashless. The transfer is the typical form of use of the Giral money.

The statement is true.

Trust bears both forms. Cash like book money remain in use as long as people expect to be able to exchange them for products and services. If this trust breaks, neither the bill in the hand nor the number in the account will benefit. The section binds the value of both forms to the same expectation.

The statement is true.

title: Transfer, withdrawal and cards
context: Evaluate the following statements available on book money:
statements: Most deposits and withdrawals to a bank account are made cashless by transfers.
Buchgeld kann durch Abhebungen vom Konto in Bargeld umgewandelt werden.
The account can be accessed particularly easily by using bank and credit cards.
Book money can never be converted into cash because it exists only as an abstract number.
Cashless payment options make the importance of book money more increase than decrease.
tactical_explanations:
Everyday life in the account means money transfer, not coin counting. Salary receipt, rent, online purchase: The greater part of the movements is cashless. It is to be noted that most deposits and withdrawals are made to a bank account. Book money is thus the working level of many payments, not a marginal phenomenon.

Withdrawals remain possible, but they are not the main way on which accounts fill and empty.

The statement is true.

Taking off translates the balance into notes and coins. The amount changes the form, not necessarily the value, as long as the trust bears. So book money can be converted into cash. The bridge between the two forms is just the withdrawal at the machine or at the counter.

The statement is true.

Cards make access to the account easy in everyday life. Paying at the cash desk or on the net draws book money without anyone having to count cash. The presentation explicitly calls bank and credit cards as particularly easy access. The card is a tool of disposal, not a third currency separate from the book money.

It does not replace the account or trust in the exchange value, it only facilitates access to it.

The statement is true.

Being abstract does not mean inconvertible. The text of the teaching describes the transformation by withdrawing explicitly. Whoever draws notes at the machine has transferred book money into cash. The assertion that abstract existence blocks any transformation contradicts this sentence.

Existence only in the account concerns the form, not the possibility of a change of form. Transfer remains within the book money, withdrawal changes into cash. Both presuppose the account. Inconsistency does not follow from this, otherwise there would be no bridge between the two forms.

The statement is false.

Paying cashless means using book money. The section expects many different cashless payment options to further increase the importance of book money. Invisibility and meaning are increasing here, they do not exclude each other. The direction is increase, not loss of meaning.

The statement is true.

title: Interest income on cash and balances
context: Evaluate the following statements on the remuneration of cash and book money:
statements: Cash doesn't pay interest.
Bank accounts are usually subject to interest, although sometimes very low.
With an account balance you can get such a low interest income.
Cash in the wallet yields the same interest income as an interest-bearing account balance.
A very low interest rate on the balance means that cash is paid higher than book money.
tactical_explanations:
The presentation contrasts the cash with the account balance: While balances are usually interest-bearing, cash does not interest. Whoever holds the amount as cash, does not give up this income, however small he may be in the account.

The choice of form between the stock exchange and the account is thus also a choice about possible interest income, not only about palpability.

The statement is true.

As a rule, the rate is typically yes, the rate can be small. Bank balances are interest-bearing, sometimes only very low. The text nevertheless states that interest yields are generated. Minority does not change the direction: the account can bear interest, the cash does not. From a low rate does not follow the equality with the zero interest-bearing of the notes in the wallet.

The statement is true.

Low income remains a return. Anyone who leaves the amount on the account will receive at least this small increase, which cash does not deliver. The section links the interest rate of the balances to this point. The amount may be low, the possibility of interest income remains.

The statement is true.

Equal income would only be conceivable if cash also pays off. The opposite applies: cash does not interest, balances usually do. The wallet does not provide any interest flow, the account can deliver you. The equation of income is therefore wrong.

Note: The later teaching of interest rates (price of money, creditors and debtors) is outside this section. Here only the form comparison counts: account can bear interest, cash can not. Even a very low account interest breaks the alleged equality with the zero of cash.

The statement is false.

Very low in the account is still more than zero in the wallet. From a small account interest does not follow that cash would be higher interest. Cash does not bear interest. The reversal of the ranking twists the comparison.

The statement is false.

title: The largest part of the money
context: Evaluate the following statements on the volume and value of book money:
statements: The vast majority of the money in circulation is in the form of book money.
Book money is worth as much as the cash despite lack of physical knowledge, provided that trust in exchange value bears.
Because most people know coins, the greater part of money must be cash.
Both forms of money are used as long as people trust to be able to trade them for products and services.
If the trust is lacking, book money remains unreservedly valuable, but cash does not.
tactical_explanations:
The money is familiar, the book money is larger. The much larger part of the money is written on accounts as book money. Coins and notes shape the image in the head, not the quantity ratio in circulation. Whoever only counts what he can grasp, massively underestimates the share of the Giral money.

The representation divides view and circulation content consciously: familiar is not the same as predominantly. That is why the section warns against considering the abstract as insignificant.

The statement is true.

Equal exchange value despite invisibility: An amount as book money should be worth as much as the same amount as cash. The condition is the common trust to be able to exchange both in goods. Physis does not replace this condition, and missing Physis does not cancel it. Value equality is therefore equal to trust, not material equality.

The statement is true.

The fact that coins and banknotes are familiar does not change the sentence, the greater part of the money is book money. View and circulation are falling apart here. The conclusion from the everyday image on the larger part is therefore wrong.

Cash is called familiar and book money abstract, but of the highest importance. Precisely because book money remains invisible, the misconception is obvious, it is the smaller size. The representation contradicts this: The far greater part is book money. Confidentiality does not replace circulation invoices.

The statement is false.

Both forms are based on the same trust. As long as people expect to be able to exchange money for products and services, cash and book money remain in use. So the use is bound to expectation, not to the physicality of the note. The sentence applies to both forms in common.

The statement is true.

Trust is both at the same time, and without trust, neither bear in the sense described. The presentation binds the value of book money and cash to the same expectation of trading. An asymmetry, after which book money would remain valuable without trust, but cash does not, does not stand. The unilateral exception is wrong.

The statement is false.

title: Currency and euro in Austria
context: Evaluate the following statements on the subject of currency:
statements: The currency is the money that is recognized as a means of payment by the state in a given country.
The currency recognised in Austria is the euro.
From Austria's perspective, foreign currencies are different from the euro.
Currency means cash only; book money in euro is not a currency.
Each country must use the same currency as Austria, otherwise the money there is not considered to be the currency.
tactical_explanations:
Recognition by the state makes money a currency of a country. It is not about the metal colour of the coin that applies there. The text of the teaching defines currency exactly as: the money that is recognized as a currency by the respective state in a particular country.

Other means of payment may exist alongside them, and from this point of view they are often foreign currencies. The definition is territorial and legal, not bound to the denomination in coins.

The statement is true.

In Austria, the euro is valid. This is the recognized currency, not the shilling, and not the dollar as domestic means of payment. Anyone who writes prices and pays taxes in Austria does so in euros. The section explicitly states this recognition. From an Austrian point of view, other currencies are foreign currencies, even if they are elsewhere recognised money.

The statement is true.

Foreign currency is a question of perspective. From the point of view of Austria, the currencies of the Swiss franc, the krona, the yen or the dollar are different from the euro. They are foreign to the country where they are recognized, but from the Austrian point of view.

The statement is true.

Currency means the recognized money of a country, not only notes and coins. Euro-book money on an Austrian account is euro, i.e. the same currency in another form. Cash and book money are forms of money, currency is state recognition. The equation of currency with cash alone is therefore wrong.

Euro as currency includes the accepted means of payment, whether as a note or as account balance. Whoever takes out book money from the currency mixes the form level (cash/book money) with the currency level. Both levels are to be separated.

The statement is false.

Each country has its recognised currency and they do not have to be identical. Swedish crowns, Swiss francs or yen are valid in other countries. The fact that Austria uses the euro does not compel other states to the same choice. The assertion of a worldwide obligation to the euro distorts the definition of currency.

The statement is false.

title: Austria in euro area
context: Evaluate the following statements on the single currency and the euro area:
statements: Austria's currency is the euro because Austria is a member of the euro area.
Some EU countries, including Austria, have gradually introduced a single currency, most recently as cash.
The aim of the single currency was, among other things, to strengthen the economy and strengthen the Union.
Austria uses the euro, although it does not belong to the euro area.
Each EU country is required to pay in euro with cash, regardless of membership of the euro area.
tactical_explanations:
Membership explains the currency choice. Austria belongs to the euro area, therefore the euro is the recognised currency. The sentence in theory is causal, not accidental: because Austria is a member. Without this affiliation the euro would not automatically be domestic currency.

EU membership alone is not enough in the logic of the text, as countries with their own currency within the Union show.

The statement is true.

Step by step introduction, cash as a later step: Some EU countries, including Austria, have built up a common currency. As a last step, cash came from 2002 onwards. The common currency has therefore been a process, not a one-off coin exchange without a history.

The statement is true.

Strengthening the economy and strengthening the Union calls the presentation as a purpose. The common currency is thus politically and economically justified, not only as a convenient means of travel payment. Anyone who sees the holiday rate only, undermines this target.

The text of the teaching is intended to strengthen the Union's economy and strengthen it. This is the motive behind the introduction, regardless of future exchange rate debates with third countries. Cash from 2002 onwards was the visible last step, not the only motive.

The statement is true.

Without the euro area, no automatic euro as a domestic currency in this argument. Austria's euro is coupled to membership. The claim that Austria pays in euro, although not part of the euro area, contradicts this causal exus.

The statement is false.

Not every EU country belongs to the euro area. The presentation later explicitly mentions countries with other valid currencies, such as Swedish krona. EU membership alone therefore does not force euro cash in the domestic market. The equalisation of EU and euro cash is too far.

Note: Figures on the size of the euro area (members, users) serve as classification and do not have to sit by heart as audit statistics. The decisive thing remains: Euro in Austria because of the euro area, not because of the mere EU membership of each country.

The statement is false.

title: Foreign currencies
context: Evaluate the following statements on foreign currencies from the euro area perspective:
statements: From the euro area perspective, Swedish krona, Swiss franc, Japanese yen and US dollar are foreign currencies.
Other currencies are valid in other countries.
The US dollar is both a currency in the United States and a foreign currency from the Austrian perspective.
Swiss francs are considered to be domestic currency in the euro area because they are used in Europe.
A currency ceases to be a currency as soon as it is called a foreign currency from an Austrian point of view.
tactical_explanations:
The series of examples in theory is clear: crowns, francs, yen, dollars are foreign currencies from the perspective of the euro area. They are means of payment where the respective state acknowledges them, but not the domestic currency of Austria. Foreign means the perspective, not the impracticalness of money itself.

The same franc is foreign currency in Switzerland and Vienna without losing its character as money.

The statement is true.

Validity follows the state recognition in the respective country. Other countries, other currencies. The euro is considered to be the only recognised currency in the euro area, not automatically worldwide. The rate holds this territorial bond.

The statement is true.

In the USA, the dollar is the recognized currency. If you are in Austria, the same dollar is a foreign currency. Both descriptions are true because currency and foreign currency are perspective dependent. The section works precisely with this distinction. Recognition in the country of origin and foreignness from the euro point of view do not exclude each other.

The statement is true.

Europe is not a currency limit in the sense of the text. The Swiss franc is a foreign currency from the euro area's perspective, even if Switzerland is in Europe. Austria's domestic currency or the euro area remains the euro. Geography does not replace state recognition here.

The situation on the continent does not make up a euro. The presentation explicitly lists the franc as a foreign currency. Anyone who concludes domestic currency from a European neighbourhood confuses the continent and the currency area. The euro remains the domestic currency in the euro area; the franc remains foreign from this point of view, however close the border lies.

The statement is false.

Foreign currency remains currency, just that of another country. The dollar does not stop in the USA being a recognized means of payment, just because Austria calls it foreign. The term describes the view, it does not erase recognition in the country of origin. The assertion of a loss of status is wrong.

The statement is false.

title: Exchange rate as price
context: Evaluate the following statements on the exchange rate:
statements: The exchange rate indicates how much you have to pay in one currency to get another currency.
The exchange rate is the price of one currency, expressed in another currency.
Exchange rates can fluctuate, just like other prices.
If the price is 1 euro = 1.2 US dollars on a given day, it costs 1 euro at this time 1.2 US dollars.
Exchange rates are fixed by law forever and can never fluctuate.
tactical_explanations:
Exchange of currency for currency has a price. How many francs for one euro, how many dollars for one euro: that is the exchange rate. You pay in one currency to get the other. The section defines the price precisely by this exchange relationship.

Without this price indication, the exchange would remain an indefinite exchange pair like meat for clothing, just between two types of money. The price makes this pair a price.

The statement is true.

The exchange rate is this price. Thus, the foreign exchange market fits into the same language as other prices, even if money is exchanged for money.

Because prices can fluctuate, exchange rates may also fluctuate; the presentation expressly draws this comparison.

The statement is true.

The fluctuations can also be prices like other prices. If the relative supply and the relative demand rises or falls, how many units of one currency costs one unit of the other changes. Rigidity is not the rule that describes the presentation. Movement belongs to the exchange rate.

The statement is true.

The book's example of numbers is to be read literally. On the day you get for a Euro 1.2 US Dollar, or otherwise: a Euro costs 1.2 Dollar. It is a snapshot, not an eternal ratio. The reading meets the quantity quotation used here.

The statement is true.

The rate never fluctuates, exchange rates could fluctuate like other prices. From fluctuations follow up and devaluations: More or less dollars per euro, more or less francs per euro. A legal fixation of all prices is not in this section. The absolute is wrong.

Price fluctuations are the reason for the later examples with dollars and francs. If prices were fixed forever, there would be no more purchasing power in the dollar country with rising euro or less purchasing power in Switzerland with rising franc. The claim of immobility cancels this mechanism.

The statement is false.

title: Valuing, foreign exchange and direction of exchange
context: Evaluate the following statements at value, exchange rates and exchange rate fluctuations:
statements: For cash, value rates are to be applied, otherwise foreign exchange rates are to be applied.
The bank distinguishes the purchase price at which it purchases foreign currency from the selling price at which it sells foreign currency.
If the value of the euro rises against the dollar, you get more dollars for one euro and you can afford more in a dollar country.
If the value of the Swiss franc rises against the euro, you have to pay more euros to buy a certain amount of franc, and tourists from the euro area can afford less in Switzerland.
If the Swiss franc rises against the euro, holidays in Switzerland will automatically be cheaper for euro area travellers, because more euros will buy the same amount of Swiss francs.
tactical_explanations:
Two markets, two types of exchange. If you change bills and coins, you have to deal with values. If the exchange does not run via cash, foreign exchange rates apply. The text requires that you pay attention to this distinction. So the same currency pairing can carry different prices depending on the form.

Cash and book money remain forms of money; the relevant currency exchange codes are valid and foreign exchange.

The statement is true.

The Bank buys foreign currency at one price and sells it to another. In between is its range. Anyone who changes, pays or receives the same rate in both directions. The section shows exactly this two-sidedness. One "the price" without direction is a failure to buy and sell.

The statement is true.

Euro increases, dollar per euro increases. One euro gives you more dollars and can buy more goods in the dollar country, unless the prices there are opposites. The presentation leads to this case explicitly. Upgrade of your own currency increases the possibility of buying abroad, which prices in dollars.

The statement is true.

The euro area travellers exchange more expensive and can afford less in Switzerland. The section describes precisely this tourist consequence. The appreciation of the foreign currency expresses the foreign purchasing power of the euro holders.

The statement is true.

The holiday would be more favourable if you needed less euros for the same amount of franc, so if the euro rose against the franc. But here the franc rises. More euros for the same amount of franc means more expensive exchange, not more favorable. The direction of purchasing power is vice versa to the claim.

Note: Don't confuse with the dollar scene. If the euro rises to the dollar, the purchasing power in the dollar country increases. If the franc rises to the euro, the purchasing power in Switzerland decreases. The same mechanics, other direction depending on which currency becomes more expensive.

The statement is false.

title: External value and quotation
context: Evaluate the following statements at the external value of a currency and at quantity and price quotations:
statements: The external value of a currency, for example the euro, is the exchange rate of that currency against a basket of foreign currencies.
The external value combines bilateral exchange rates at a multilateral exchange rate, usually weighted by the volume of trade with the domestic currency area.
According to the volume quotation from the euro's point of view, the price indicates how many units of foreign currency one must pay to obtain a unit of domestic currency.
According to price quotation, the price shows how many units of domestic currency one gets for a unit of foreign currency.
Quantity listing and price listing are identical, and WU uses only price quotation for simplicity.
tactical_explanations:
Not only dollars, not only francs: the external value bundles the euro against many foreign currencies in one basket. It is an exchange rate against this basket, not against a single quotation. The bilateral exchange rate to a currency remains in place, but does not explain the external value alone.

If you only know a currency pair, you know a price, not yet the external value in the sense of the text.

The statement is true.

Many bilateral rates become multilateral. The weighting is usually based on the volume of trade with the domestic currency area, i.e. the economic proximity of the partners. Important trading partners count in the basket more than marginal. Thus, a bundle of paired rates becomes a single external value.

Without weighting, each partner would be equally loud, regardless of the trade weight. The presentation explicitly states the weighting, mostly according to the trade volume. The multilateral price is thus a compressed information, not a substitute for the individual daily price at the franc or dollar.

The statement is true.

From a euro point of view, how many dollars, francs or crowns for one euro. The example of 1 euro = 1.2 US dollars follows this convention. One can see how much foreign currency a domestic unit "buys".

The statement is true.

Price quotation turns the break. Now one asks how many units of the domestic currency are necessary for a unit of foreign, i.e. about euro per dollar. It is the same relation, only inversely read. The representation contrasts both ways and holds that prices can be given in two ways.

The statement is true.

The quotations are not identical, they are two spellings of the same relation. At WU, for simplicity, only the quotation of quantities, not the quotation of prices, are used. Whoever equates both and at the same time turns the WU convention to the quotation of prices, misses both sentences of the section.

1 Euro = 1.2 Dollar is volume quotation: foreign quantity per Euro. The price quotation would ask for Euro per Dollar. Simplicity at WU means: stay with the quantity quotation. The claimed identity together with false WU choice is therefore wrong.

The statement is false.

title: Interest as the price of money
context: Evaluate the following statements on interest as the price of borrowed money:
statements: Interest is the price of borrowing money.
If you borrow money, you get interest and you're a creditor.
If you borrow money, you don't pay interest because only the creditor pays.
Anyone who borrows money pays interest and is a debtor.
Interest is only incurred if two goods are exchanged directly against each other.
tactical_explanations:
Borrowing money has a price, and that price is called interest. The section thus places interest on the same level as other prices: they are paid for the money being left to you. Without this leave, there would be no interest in the logic of the text. The sentence gives the definition literally.

Neither the exchange of meat for clothing nor the mere existence of banknotes explains this price; it depends on the temporary giving of money.

The statement is true.

The amount is called loans. The borrowers are in this role. The borrowers receive the price, they do not pay it. The borrowers are not paid the price. The borrowers are not paid the price.

The statement is true.

The debtor pays interest, the creditor receives it. The claim that only the creditor pays and the borrower pays nothing, exchanges both sides. A borrower who finances a car pays the price for the money left over. The bank as the creditor receives it.

Whoever reverses the payment direction makes the price of borrowing a receipt of the debtor. That is not what the text says. Borrowing and borrowing are two directions of the same business: one side leaves the amount and collects the price, the other takes the amount and pays it. A sentence that saves the borrower the payment destroys this assignment.

The statement is false.

The debtor is the person who borrows the amount and pays the price for it. The borrower is named when buying a car and the bank that receives savings deposits. Both owe interest to the respective creditor. The role follows from borrowing, not from the profession or legal form.

The statement is true.

Interest is the price of money left over, not the price of a trade in meat for clothing. The immediate exchange without means of payment is earlier in the chapter and explains why money is needed. It does not explain why interest flows. Whoever binds interest to the natural exchange mixes two sections.

The statement is false.

title: Savers, Banks and borrowers
context: Evaluate the following statements to creditors and debtors in the case of savings deposits and loans:
statements: The saver who makes money available to the bank can be a creditor.
If the bank grants a customer a loan, the bank can be a creditor.
The borrower who takes a loan for the car purchase is an example of a debtor.
The bank that takes savings deposits is never a debtor to savers.
The same bank may be a creditor to the saver and to the borrower.
tactical_explanations:
Savings deposits are left to money. The saver lends the bank the amount and receives interest. This person is mentioned as a possible example for the creditor. The bank is opposed to him as a debtor because she accepted the deposit.

The statement is true.

The bank leaves the customer money and demands interest. Then the bank is a creditor, the customer is a debtor. This pair is explicitly applied alongside the pair of savers and bank. Creditor is attached to the loan, not to whether the institution is called bank.

The statement is true.

Autocredit is the everyday example of the text. The buyer borrows the purchase price and pays interest. Thus, he is a debtor. The bank that grants the loan is a creditor in this business. The example makes the abstract role tangible without introducing a second definition.

The statement is true.

The statement is false.

Two contracts, two directions. The bank accepts money from the saver and pays interest, i.e. the debtor. It gives money to the borrower and receives interest, i.e. the creditor.
