title: Dubiosenrisiko
context: Evaluate the following statements on dubious risk as a reason for interest:

Without any risk of default, interest would never exist because interest is only a penalty for late payment.
tactical_explanations:
The creditor gives the amount out of hand and wants a price for it. The first of the three reasons in theory is precisely this compensation for the risk taken. Interests are thus, among other things, a risk premium, not just a calculation size.

The statement is true.

Dubious risk is the technical name for the risk of default. The debtor can remain guilty of the amount. The creditor wants interest. The description explicitly links the term to the possibility that no payment is made. Whoever hears the name should think of this failure, not of exchange rates or taxes.

Three reasons are side by side. In addition to the dubious risk, the term "abuse" or "opportunity costs" is used as well as the money value risk. The statement is false.

The presentation counts three motives, not one. Penalty for late payment does not occur in this section. A saver who leaves money to the bank wants interest even if he considers the bank to be eligible for payment: he renounces consumption and bears the risk that the amount paid back will buy less. Dubious risk is one reason among several, not a necessary explanation alone.

title: Consumers' forfeiture and opportunity costs

The parentheses in the text are deliberately wide: lost income and/or consumer waiver. Both are opportunity costs of the creditor. He could have invested or spent the amount differently. Interest should compensate for this lost use. The wording "and/or" allows one of both to occur together.

If you only count lost interest on an alternative investment and cancel the unused consumption, or vice versa, you shorten the definition. The section keeps both ways of renunciation open.

opportunity costs are with the creditor who waives. The debtor uses the amount, for example for the car purchase, and pays interest for it. The statement is false.

title: Maturity risk as a reason for interest

Three reasons, not one. Dubious risk, opportunity costs and money value risk are listed. Those who only accept the money value risk will cancel out default and consumer waiver. Whether the bank closes or the borrower loses the contract would be a default of the debtor, i.e. dubious risk. Money value risk, on the other hand, presupposes that the amount returns, but buys less due to higher prices. Two names, two mechanisms.

title: Cheap money and credit demand
context: Evaluate the following statements on supply, demand and the level of interest:
statements: The level of interest is influenced by supply and demand as well as other prices.
Low credit rates mean that loans are cheap, that is, cheap money, which leads to higher demand for loans.

The price can stimulate too little demand. Lower interest rates make loans cheaper again and can stimulate demand. The presentation closes the cycle: high, then rising price and stop; too low, then falling price and stimulus. Stimulation is the counterpoint to dampening by rising interest rates.

Cheap money is exactly that in this section: a low loan rate that brings households and businesses back to the credit market without the price being fixed at zero in the long run.

The statement is true.

Gradually rising is the damper. Very strong demand raises the credit price. Higher interest rates slow further growth until demand no longer rises. This is the same amount-price balance as with other goods, only here for left money. The sentence follows the text step by step.

The statement is true.

title: How the Bank sets the loan rate
context: Evaluate the following statements The interest rate on loans granted by a bank:

The risk assessment of the loan is a risk cost to the interest rate.

Risk has a price. If the bank uses the loan as more risky, it demands more. The risk costs are called. A secure debtor and an unsafe debtor are not automatically at the same rate, even if the refinancing is the same. The assessment of the concrete loan counts.

After refinancing and risk, the operation and yield remain. Additional costs are to be covered and a profit is to be added. The interest rate is thus a sum of several components, not a single number from nothing. The third point of the list includes exactly this residual size.

The bank calculates its customer credit from its own procurement costs, risk costs, additional costs and profits. The saver's dubious risk explains why the bank wants interest, not the rate the bank calls the car buyer.

title: Interest rate and period
context: A balance of € 10,000 is interest-bearing at 2% per annum. Evaluate the following statements for the calculation of interest rates:

p.a. shortens per annual, i.e. per year. The interest rate is usually expressed as this. 2 % per year is two percent of the capital in twelve months, not two percent per month and not two euros independent of the capital. The spelling in the text is exactly this year's figure.

€2,000 would be 20%, not 2%. 10,000 × 0.02 = 200, not 10,000 × 0.20 = 2,000. Anyone who reads the percentage as a finished euro amount or postpones the comma will twist the bill. The interest rate remains a share of the capital for the period mentioned. 2% of €10,000 is €200 in one year.

The percentage and interest rate are the same name for the amount. The figure says: The amount of interest is usually given as a percentage, it is also called interest rate. 2% p.a. is exactly this. The Euro amount 200 € is then the application of this rate to 10,000 € in one year.

Rate of capital for one year: 10,000 × 0.05 = 500. This would be the pure annual interest rate if nothing but the 5% were incurred. The text needs this 5% to keep the fees against it. 500 € is the nominal interest charge of this year, not the entire charge of the business.

The statement is true.

The end of the quarter and the end of the year are common examples of such a date. This is the time when the bank will charge the interest and keep the tax. The period may be shorter or longer; the decisive factor is that there is a fixed settlement date at all. Without such a date, the retention would not be so.

The statement is true.

title: Interest rates on KESt
context: At the end of the year, the bank will write interest well, retain KESt and count the balance. Rate the following statements:
statements: The interest income reduced by KESt is added to the balance in the bank account.
In the next period interest is only paid on the old capital, never on the already credited amount of interest.
Interest is also received in the next period for this amount of interest (according to KESt) which is also allocated to interest; this is called interest.
Interest on the account continues after the tax deduction, because only the remaining capital gains are added to the balance.
The KESt shall destroy any further interest because no amount may be placed in the account after the retention.
tactical_explanations:
After the deduction, a reduced interest income remains, and this is exactly the rest of the income on account. It is called capital income and says that it is included in the balance. The tax flows to the tax office, the net interest remains with the saver as a higher contribution. Without this attribution, there would be nothing in the next step that could be reinterested.

Gross interest minus KESt, then addition to the old balance: this is the basis of the following period.

The statement is true.

Only interest on the old capital would cancel the second part of the rate. The presentation says that interest is also received for this amount of interest in the next period. The amount credited to KESt is part of the new base. Whoever takes it out of the interest rate calculates against the described interest rate logic.

The net means is not invisible. What lands on the account after tax is balances and is interest-bearing like the rest of the balances. The bank has already retained the KESt; the rest grows to the account and in the subsequent period itself pays interest. The claim that never the interest amount is therefore wrong.

The statement is false.

Interest rates after tax: This is the final rate of the section. The reduced interest income is added, and in the next period it also bears interest. The quotation marks in theory are located at "interest rates" exactly behind this mechanism. The tax deduction does not change the order, it only reduces the amount that is interest-bearing.

The statement is true.

The remaining income only grows to the balance, but this remainder is large enough to bear interest itself. Gross interest minus KEST, then new base, then set again times base. Thus, the presentation combines tax technology and interest rate without introducing a second formula.

The statement is true.

The account remains, the net interest is added, the next period also pays off this remainder. KESt reduces the income, it does not grant the balance. "No amount more" contradicts the addition to the balance. Interest rates would then be impossible, although it explicitly places them in this place.

The statement is false.

title: Value of money in time
context: Evaluate the following statements to the value of money in time:
statements: For money as a means of payment, value measure and value-keeping means, it is important that it retains its value over time.
Money will be less valuable if you can buy less goods and services than a year earlier for the same amount, about 100 euros, because of higher prices.
If the nominal amount remains unchanged, the value of the money remains unchanged, regardless of the prices.
Increased prices mean that the same amount of money buys less goods and services.
The value of the money depends only on the imprint on the banknote, not on what you can buy for it.
tactical_explanations:
Three functions, a common condition. Cash, value meters and value-keeping devices only work reliably when money carries possibilities of buying over time. Whoever accepts a note today wants to be able to shop with it tomorrow. Anyone comparing prices in euros needs a unit whose exchange value does not collapse from one day to the next.

Those who save value, not just a digit, are the ones who set value. That is exactly why the section stresses that money must keep its value over time so that these qualities remain sustainable.

The statement is true.

One hundred euros today and one hundred euros a year ago bear the same imprint, not the same basket. If the prices of many goods have increased, you buy less with the amount. The text takes exactly this example: A fixed amount of money loses value if you can afford less goods and services than at the time of comparison.

The loss in value is in the purchase quantity, not in a modified number on the note.

The statement is true.

The section explains the loss of value at the fixed amount of 100 euros: the number remains, prices rise, the purchaseable amount falls. Whoever equates the value with the imprint confuses nominal size and purchasing power. The sentence claims an immutability that expressly refutes the presentation.

The statement is false.

Price increases and lower purchase quantity are two sides of the same movement. If goods and services become more expensive, the same amount of money is sufficient for less pieces, less hours of service, less filling of the shopping basket. The text links the loss of value of money precisely to this lower purchase quantity. The sentence returns this coupling.

The statement is true.

The value of the item is measured by the fact that it is possible to buy products and services and shows the loss as soon as higher prices reduce this amount. A banknote that no one can buy with is worth a number, but not the exchange value that the money functions need.

The restriction on the print marks exactly this purchase page.

The statement is false.

title: Was Inflation bedeutet
context: Evaluate the following statements on the concept of inflation:
statements: Inflation is referred to as the decline in the value of money, because the prices of many goods and services are rising, thus increasing the general price level.
If only the price of a single product is rising in a business, inflation is already mandatory.
Inflation is reducing purchasing power because you can buy less for a certain amount of money at the end of a year than at the beginning.
Inflation is reducing the internal value of money.
Inflation is only available if all prices rise by the same percentage every day.
tactical_explanations:
Many prices, one level. The text binds inflation to the declining monetary value that arises because the prices of many goods and services rise and thus the general price level rises. It is not about a single price label, but about the breadth of the movement.

This is precisely the degree of inflation in the sense of the paragraph, which is only made of more expensive bread or electricity when it enters the general price level. An isolated price jump remains a relative change; the definition requires the increase of many prices and of the level as a whole.

The sentence repeats the definition in its logic without explaining the individual case as inflation.

The statement is true.

A single product in a single business can become more expensive without the general price level rising. Inflation requires the rise of many prices and the level overall. The increase of a position is not sufficient as mandatory proof. Relative price changes are part of the everyday life of the markets; inflation is the general movement.

The absolute "inflation already forcefully extends over the individual case.

The statement is false.

Purchasing power is the purchaseable quantity with the given amount. If the price level increases over the year, the same amount buys less at the end of the year than at the beginning of the year. The section mentions this exact comparison as a result of inflation. The loss of value of the money here appears as a lower purchase quantity, not as a changed number in the account.

Those who overlook this view nominal stocks as real buying opportunities.

The statement is true.

Domestic value means the value of money in the domestic market, i.e. domestic purchasing power. Inflation reduces this purchasing power because the same money buys less goods. The representation says explicitly: Through inflation the internal value of money decreases. External value and exchange rate are not yet decided; here it is about the domestic side. The sentence meets this domestic consequence.

The statement is true.

The presentation does not require a step-by-step approach of all prices on every day. A general price level is measured by a basket whose positions can develop differently. Some goods rise more strongly, others weaker or not at all. Inflation remains the rise of the level, not the demand for identical daily percentages on each label.

The condition "only if all prices are equal daily is too narrow and wrong.

The statement is false.

title: Purchasing power and fixed amount of money
context: Evaluate the following statements on the purchasing power of money:
statements: Purchasing power indicates how many goods can be bought for a certain amount of money.
Inflation can buy less for the same amount of money at the end of a year than at the beginning of the year.
If the general price level rises, the purchasing power of a fixed amount of money increases.
The internal value of a currency refers to the value of money in the domestic market, that is, to the purchasing power of money.
The internal value of a currency measures only how many units of a foreign currency one receives for one euro.
tactical_explanations:
The section specifically asks how many goods can be bought for a certain amount, and that is the purchasing power of money in the country. It is not the number on the note that counts here, but the quantity of goods and services that moves this number.

Anyone who holds 100 euros has as much purchasing power as the shopping cart gives at the current prices. This reading makes a nominal amount a real possibility.

The statement is true.

The text of the teaching is precisely this comparison as a result of inflation. The nominal sum can remain on the account, the real filling of the purchase is decreasing. Loss of purchasing power and inflation are the same movement here, only from the money side or from the money side.

read from the price page.

The statement is true.

Price level and purchasing power of a fixed amount are opposite. If many prices rise, the same amount buys less, the purchasing power decreases. The sentence claims the opposite: increasing level, increasing purchasing power. This contradicts the definition. If you think both equally, you confuse more expensive goods with larger purchase quantity.

A fixed amount of 100 euros remains 100 euros. If bread, energy and rent are more expensive, it is enough for less. That is exactly what declining purchasing power means. Therefore, the claim of increasing purchasing power with rising price level is wrong.

The statement is false.

Domestic, not foreign exchange switch: the domestic value refers to the value of money in the domestic currency and thus to purchasing power, i.e. to how many goods the amount buys in the own currency area. The representation contrasts this domestic reading with the foreign exchange.

Anyone who says internal value speaks about domestic prices and domestic goods, not about dollars or francs per euro.

The statement is true.

Foreign currency units per euro are part of the external value, not the internal value. The section clearly separates: domestic value is domestic purchasing power, external value is how many units of a foreign currency can be bought for a unit of its own currency. The restriction of the internal value to the foreign exchange rate exchanges the two sides.

An unchanged exchange rate does not exclude a fall in domestic inflation.

The statement is false.

title: Internal and external value
context: Evaluate the following statements at the internal and external values of a currency:
statements: The external value of a currency means how many units of a foreign currency can be bought for a unit of its own currency.
Internal value and external value are two different perspectives on monetary value in the text.
Internal value and external value are the same in the text of the teaching and are always identical in numbers.
If domestic price levels rise, the domestic value decreases, even if the exchange rate remains unchanged.
The internal value of a currency is the exchange rate against the US dollar.
tactical_explanations:
Foreign value asks for foreign currency units per unit of its own. Dollars, Swiss francs or other foreign currencies: How many of them buys one euro, or how many units of foreign currency are paid for one euro? The section places the foreign value precisely on this relation.

It is the external side of the monetary value, not the question of how many euro breads the domestically buys. Whoever only counts domestic goods measures the domestic value, not the external value.

The statement is true.

Two questions, two answers. Domestic: How many goods for the amount? Foreign: How many units foreign currency for the own unit? The text explicitly compares internal value and external value. The same currency can lose purchasing power in the domestic currency and simultaneously write more or less down against a foreign currency.

The separation of the angles is the point of the section, not its fusion.

The statement is true.

The internal value depends on domestic prices and purchasing power, the external value on exchange rates against foreign currencies. A numerical equality does not assert the representation. Whoever pulls both together at a single value makes the comparison unnecessary.

Domestic inflation lowers domestic value without the dollar's price having to be drawn in the same way.

The statement is false.

Domestic prices are rising, the euro is buying less domestically: the domestic value is falling, the exchange rate can remain unchanged because it measures a different relation. The section links the domestic value to domestic purchasing power, not to the foreign exchange rate. This is precisely why domestic inflation can hit the domestic value without the external value having to show the same movement.

The independence of the two sides bears the sentence.

The price of domestic goods is not a price-fixed price, but a price-fixed price does not change the price of the same euro amount. The text defines the domestic value of goods. Increasing price levels there lowers it, price down or down.

The statement is true.

The dollar is an example of an external currency, not the definition of the domestic value. Domestic value is domestic purchasing power. A single bilateral exchange rate, or only the dollar, does not replace either the domestic value or the external value as a basket measure from the previous exchange rate period. The narrowing to the dollar exchange rate as an internal value is wrong.

The statement is false.

title: Money supply and book money creation
context: Evaluate the following statements on monetary growth as a cause of inflation:
statements: Inflation is favoured if there is too much money in circulation relative to the goods and services offered.
Book money can be greatly increased by additional loans; this increase is called book money creation.
Money supply growth only plays a role in potential inflation if the increase in money remains exclusively with banks.
The increase in money supply is particularly effective when it is rapid and when money is received by households and businesses and spent on investment and consumption.
Central banks, according to the text, can never put money into circulation because only cash counts.
tactical_explanations:
Too much money, too little goods: then inflation is favoured. The section compares the circulating money supply with the goods and services offered. If the money side grows stronger than the goods side, more pay power pushes on the same supply quantity. Prices can rise.

The relativization "in relation to" is decisive: not every increase in money acts the same, but the disproportion of the quantity offered.

The statement is true.

Credit creates book money. If banks lend a lot, the giral money increases without having to print new notes. The text of the teaching calls this increase in book money through lending book money creation. Along with the permission to print more money, this is a way to increase the circulating amount.

Book money is as much money as cash, as long as confidence in exchange value carries.

The statement is true.

If the additional money remains with the banks, it does not come as demand for households and companies. The presentation says the opposite of the claim: The increase plays a role especially if the more money is not left with the banks, but spent on investment and consumption.

If you limit the effect to remaining with the banks, the condition turns over.

Parking of book money at credit institutions does not yet generate a demand-side for goods. Only expenditure for consumption and investment meets the supply of goods. Precisely this arrival at households and companies makes money-volume growth inflationaryly relevant. The restriction on remaining with the banks is therefore wrong.

The statement is false.

The rapid growth of money, which is important for households and businesses and is spent there, is due to goods and services. If the supply does not rise to the same extent, prices can rise. The section links the inflation relevance precisely to this chain, not to an abstract number in banking statistics alone.

If you only see the balance sheet total without spending, you see half the story.

The statement is true.

Central banks can get permission to print more money, and banks increase book money through loans. Both are part of the surrounding crowd. The claim that central banks could never put money into circulation because only cash counts contradicts both ways.

Book money is the far greater part of the circulating money and is relevant to inflation as soon as it is spent.

The statement is false.

title: Nachfragesog
context: Evaluate the following statements on the demand trend as a cause of inflation:
statements: If households and businesses have more money and their demand increases more than supply, prices for goods and services are rising.
A great demand drives prices upwards; the text of the teaching calls it a demand-sog.
A demand-side indicator only arises if the supply increases to the same extent as the demand.
Increasing prices may mean rising costs for companies and thus lead to cost pressures.
The causes of inflation are completely independent of each other and cannot be mutually dependent.
tactical_explanations:
More money in the hands of households and companies can increase demand for goods and services. If supply does not keep pace, more purchasing power meets scarcer or more consistent quantities. The text concludes that prices rise. The disproportion between demand growth and supply growth is the core, not the mere existence of money.

If you want to spend more and can than produce or be offered, the prices will be raised.

The statement is true.

The demand-side is the name for this traction force. The great demand drives prices upwards. The section represents the pull in addition to money-volume growth and cost pressure as a major cause. It is the same story as in the previous sentence, only put to the concept: The demand side pulls, the price level follows, unless the supply equals.

The term is exactly on this mechanism.

The statement is true.

The presentation of the demand sog is based on the fact that demand increases, but that supply does not rise to the same extent. Only then are prices driven upwards. The claim that the demand is only obtained with the same increase in supply reverses the condition.

Demand is catching up with growing supply; missing growth is increasing prices.

The statement is false.

Prices and costs are linked to the chain of the book. Increasing prices may mean rising costs for companies, and this leads to the next point, the cost pressure. The demand so-called remains not isolated: More expensive inputs, more expensive wages, more expensive energy can connect the cost side.

The presentation explicitly says that the causes can be mutually dependent. The sentence hits exactly this bridge.

The statement is true.

The statement approaches are not entirely independent of each other, but can be mutually dependent. Money supply, demand and costs intertwine, for example when more money generates demand and increases prices incur costs. From the demand so-called cost pressure can become the wage-price spiral, out of cost pressure.

Whoever claims complete independence, cuts this sentence of the text and cuts the chain that builds up the overview of the causes. The Absolute is wrong.

The statement is false.

title: Cost pressure and imported inflation
context: Evaluate the following statements on cost pressure and imported inflation:
statements: Increasing commodity prices, wage costs or more expensive imports can increase production costs.
Increasing production costs are reflected in rising prices.
Imported inflation is present when imports are rising.
Exchange rate changes cannot increase imports because prices are only generated domestically.
If more euro is to be paid for imports for a certain amount of foreign currency, imports are going to be more expensive.
tactical_explanations:
Three cost drivers call the presentation in one breath: raw materials, wages and imports. If they rise, production costs increase. Companies then produce more expensive before they adjust the final prices. The cost pressure starts at this operating cost side, not at the shop counter.

Raw materials, wages and imports are equally important examples, none of which is optional for understanding the mechanism.

The statement is true.

Costs have to land somewhere. The section says: Increasing production costs are reflected in rising prices. Companies continue to press on by increasing their sales prices. Cost-expression will increase prices, and price-increase is the substance of inflation. The chain is short and direct: producing more expensive, selling more expensive.

Those who decouple costs and final prices interrupt exactly this rate.

The statement is true.

Imported inflation is the name for more expensive imports. The text sets the exclamation mark behind exactly this formula: imports are higher, domestic costs are higher, prices follow. Causes can be foreign cost increases or exchange rate changes that require more euro per foreign currency amount.

The term is linked to the increase in imports, not to a domestic demand alone.

The statement is true.

Exchange rates are explicitly part of the import increase. If the price changes so that more euros are to be paid for the same foreign currency amount, imports become more expensive. Prices are not only domestic; imported costs and price changes are included. The claim that exchange rate changes cannot increase imports contradicts the text.

Domestic and foreign are linked by the import price.

A weaker euro compared to the delivery currency means more euro for the same foreign invoice. These extra euro are in production costs and can enter domestic prices. The section calls exchange rate changes as a way of import price increase. The restriction of all prices to purely domestic origin is therefore wrong.

The statement is false.

More euros per foreign currency amount is the price side of the same import history. The presentation precisely formulates this: For imports from abroad more must be paid because more euros are necessary for a certain amount of foreign currency. The import invoice in euro increases, even if the foreign price remains unchanged in foreign currency.

This is imported inflation above the exchange rate.

The statement is true.

title: Zinsen gegen Inflation
context: Evaluate the following statements on combating inflation through interest and lending:
statements: In order to combat inflation, central banks often increase interest rates.
If refinancing becomes more expensive for banks, they also raise the credit rates for their customers.
By limiting lending and by more expensive loans, the money supply is usually reduced again.
Higher central bank interest rates are intended to extend lending indefinitely to accelerate inflation.
More expensive loans always increase the money supply, because then more book money is created.
tactical_explanations:
More expensive money is intended to slow price increases. The section calls the rise in interest rates by central banks as a common means of fighting inflation. Higher interest rates make loans more expensive, dampen demand and increase in credit, thus counteracting demand and rapid money creation.

This is monetary policy about the price of money, not about a direct price stop in the store. The sentence meets the described practice.

The statement is true.

Refinancing is the price at which banks borrow money themselves. If this price becomes more expensive, banks pass on the burden: Credit rates for customers rise. The text describes precisely this transfer. The central bank starts at the refinancing rate, which follows customer interest rates.

Without this bridge, the key rate increase would remain in the bank balance sheet and did not reach households and companies.

The statement is true.

Less and more expensive loans reduce the creation of book money. The presentation says: By limiting the lending and by more expensive loans (higher interest rates) the money supply is usually reduced again. Less new book money means less additional demand, unless the money was in any case only with the banks.

The acceptance of the rule of the section is reduction, not expansion. That is exactly what is meant to counteract inflation.

The statement is true.

Extending and accelerating is the reverse intention. Higher central bank interest rates are meant to increase credit and generally reduce money supply, not to extend indefinitely. Accelerate inflation would be the opposite of the inflation fight, which describes the presentation. The claim distorts goal and instrument.

If you equate higher interest rates with credit boom, read the section against the line.

The statement is false.

More expensive loans dampen the demand for loans and thus the creation of book money, they do not necessarily blow up. The text links more expensive loans to the reduction of the money supply. "More and more book money is contrary to this rule. Loans continue to arise, but the impulse goes towards less, not towards unlimited multiplication.

The Absolute is wrong.

Note: The creation of book money is about lending. Higher interest rates are meant to increase and limit this award. Whoever equates more expensive loans with more and more book money confuses the mechanism of formation with the monetary policy throttling.

The statement is false.

title: Lohn-Preis-Spirale
context: Evaluate the following statements on the pay-price spiral:
statements: If prices rise, employees demand higher wages and salaries to maintain their purchasing power.
If wages and salaries rise, the costs for companies increase, which in turn increases their prices.
Increasing prices can again trigger demands for higher wages.
The wage-price spiral shows that wage and price increases never affect each other.
Those who demand higher wages to secure purchasing power are always interrupting the spiral completely.
tactical_explanations:
The aim of the paper is to provide a basis for the demand for purchasing power. If prices rise, the wage to date buys less. Employees demand higher wages and salaries so that their purchasing power remains. The text of the teaching sets this very first step at the beginning of the spiral. It is the same purchasing power logic as in inflation: fixed nominal wages, rising prices, falling real quantities.

Die Lohnforderung antwortet darauf.

The statement is true.

Wages are costs. If they rise, the costs of the companies rise, and the companies in turn increase their prices. The second step of the spiral is cost pressure from the wage side. The section explicitly links the steps: price increase, wage demand, cost increase, price increase again.

If you see wages as just household income and not as the cost of businesses, you see only half the spiral.

The statement is true.

The loop closes. Rising prices again cause demands for higher wages. The description ends with exactly this resumption, indicated by the continuation points. From two steps a cycle is created: prices pull wages, wages pull prices.

The spiral is this interaction, not a one-off wage supplement without consequence.

The statement is true.

The text of the teaching introduces the wage-price spiral to illustrate the interactions between the causes of inflation. Prices and wages push each other. The absolute "never cuts the whole mechanism. Whoever claims independence, contradicts the definition.

The statement is false.

The demand for wages for purchasing power is the entry into the spiral, not the break-off. Higher wages secure the purchasing power of the employees, but increase the costs and can drive prices further, which is what new demands follow. The presentation does not describe an automatic, complete break-off from the demand itself.

"Always interrupt completely is therefore wrong.

The same wage supplement that protects the household is in the company cost calculation. This double role keeps the spiral in motion. A complete break from the demand alone is not in the text of the teaching.

The statement is false.

title: Inflation rate and consumer price index
context: Evaluate the following statements on inflation measurement:
statements: The level of inflation is given by the inflation rate calculated on the basis of the consumer price index.
Each month, prices of certain goods and services are charged and compared with the previous month or year.
The goods and services taken into account in the measurement are called the contents of the shopping cart.
The inflation rate measures the price of a single product in the shopping cart.
The consumer price index never compares prices with the previous year.
tactical_explanations:
The inflation level appears as inflation rate, and this rate is calculated on the basis of the consumer price index. The CPI condenses many prices to a level, comparing this level over time gives the rate. Without index no comparable rate, without rate no indication of the level in the sense of the section.

The survey of individual prices alone is not sufficient; first the concentration in the index and the time comparison make prices an inflation rate. The rate reflects this order.

The statement is true.

The prices of certain goods and services are recorded each month and compared with the previous month or year. The comparison shows how much prices have risen. The text of the teaching refers to both horizons. Anyone who has only one reference date without comparison has prices, but no inflation rate.

The previous month shows the short movement, the previous year the usual annual rate, both sitting on the same monthly survey.

The statement is true.

Cart is the content of the measurement. Not all the goods of the economy, but the goods and services that are considered form the basket. The section describes this selection as the content of the basket. Bread, apartment, energy, leisure: later the basket is concreted, here the idea of the selection counts first.

Without fixed content, there would be no index.

The statement is true.

A single product does not produce a consumer price index. The basket includes many items, around 800 in the later set of the book, and the rate measures the development of this bundle, not the price of a single commodity. Inflation is the rise in the general level. The narrowing to a single product contradicts survey, basket and comparison.

An expensive apple is not yet an inflation rate.

The statement is false.

The price surveyed is compared to the previous month or year. "Never with the previous year" marks one of the two directions mentioned. The annual rate, which is often meant to be used in everyday language, is precisely dependent on this comparison of the previous year. The absolute is wrong.

Month to month shows short-term movement, year to year the inflation rate in the usual sense of the section. Both comparisons belong to the measurement. Anyone who denies the comparison of the previous year leaves the calculation of the level on the basis of the CPI incomplete.

The statement is false.

title: Shopping cart and HICPs
context: Evaluate the following statements to the shopping cart and the Harmonized Index of Consumer Prices:
statements: The shopping cart contains around 800 different products and services that require an average household to live.
The shopping cart includes food, accommodation and energy as well as cultural and leisure activities.
Products and services in the shopping cart are adapted every five years to the consumption habits of the population.
The Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices is the basis for the comparable measurement of inflation in Europe and for the measurement of monetary stability within the euro area.
The shopping cart is recomposed daily and never adapted to changed consumption habits.
tactical_explanations:
The text of the teaching refers to this magnitude and the purpose: what an average household needs to live is the basket. It is a representative bundle, not the shopping sheet of a single person and not the whole of all goods ever traded.

Around 800 makes the width visible without the test having to require the exact counting of each year. The statement follows the theory.

The statement is true.

Life means more than the daily food bag. Living and energy are in the basket, as are culture and leisure. The section specifically counts these groups alongside the food. Whoever narrows the basket on food underestimates rent and electricity and misses the breadth of the lifestyle. The above mentioned areas belong to the content of the CPI.

The statement is true.

Consumerism changes, the basket follows by far. Every five years, products and services are adapted to the consumption habits of the population. Smartphones, streaming, other diets: What the average buys is supposed to reflect, but not every day new. Five years is the mentioned rhythm. Without adaptation, the index would measure an outdated life.

The statement is true.

Europe needs comparability. HICPs are the basis for the comparable measurement of inflation in Europe and for the evaluation of monetary stability within the euro area. National CPIs alone are not enough because baskets and procedures otherwise run apart. The Harmonised Index makes countries and the zone readable.

Monetary stability in monetary union depends on this common measure.

The statement is true.

New every day and never adapted contradicts both: the five-year rhythm of adjustment and stability of the basket between adjustments. The presentation does not know the daily reconstruction or freezing without adaptation. Micro basket and mini basket are other indices for shorter shopping rhythms, not the daily exchange of the entire CPI basket.

The double claim is wrong.

Adjustment every five years requires that the basket is kept in between and then brought to the habits. Daily recomposition would destroy comparability, complete non-adaptation would make the average household obsolete. The text of the teaching chooses the middle way. The sentence does not hit him.

The statement is false.

title: CPI for collateral
context: Evaluate the following statements on the use of the consumer price index outside statistics:
statements: The consumer price index is used not only to calculate the level of inflation, but also to secure the value of monetary amounts, such as rents and maintenance payments.
If the index has increased at a certain point in time compared to a contractually defined index, the payment, for example, is adjusted.
In wage negotiations, the consumer price index is used as a basis for the extent to which wage increases are made.
The consumer price index may be used exclusively in statistics, according to the text of the teaching, and never in contracts.
According to the text of the teaching, maintenance payments cannot be tied to an index and can be guaranteed value.
tactical_explanations:
Statistics and contracts use the same index. The CPI measures the level of inflation and secures money amounts, such as rents and maintenance payments, against the loss of purchasing power. If prices rise, the nominal amount should be deducted to ensure that the real performance remains closer to the agreed level.

The section explicitly mentions this value-assurance in addition to the calculation of the inflation level. The index leaves the statistical office and is in contracts.

The statement is true.

Index clause means: comparison with a fixed level. If the index is later higher, the payment is adjusted, in the example the rent. The representation describes exactly this mechanism. Without the comparison to the contractual reference index there would be no automatic adjustment. The rent follows the index because the real housing value would otherwise disappear with inflation.

The rate meets the value of the rental example.

The statement is true.

Wages and salaries negotiate on the same scale. The CPI provides the basis for the extent of the increase. This is linked to purchasing power and the wage-price spiral: Employees want to see the price level increase in nominal wages. The teaching text puts this use in addition to rent and maintenance.

Negotiations remain negotiations, but the index number is the basis for the extent mentioned.

The statement is true.

Only statistics and never contracts contradict the examples of rent, maintenance and wage negotiations. The section just emphasizes that the CPI is not only the basis for calculating inflation. The absolute "exclusively" and "never-definitely" marks the value of the guarantee. The index is public and contract-worthy, according to the text of the teaching.

The claim contradicts purpose and finding.

title: Price stability at two percent

Higher than this measure means: too high an increase in the general price level, and economic operators notice it clearly. This is precisely what makes a higher rate unsuitable for price stability. The claim that a significantly higher rate is just as ideal is a step away from the gap that the ECB's foundation draws. Too high an increase in the general price level is precisely the reason to stop taking as a goal. The sentence is wrong.

The statement is false.

title: Why not zero percent

If you read 2 percent as a detour to 0 percent, you miss the point of the paragraph.

The presentation states that this is a presumption of expectations, not of nature, but of the decisive mechanism. Expected price decreases change the purchasing behaviour before prices actually fall. The price declines are expected to change the price trend.

Falling prices, rising monetary value: This is deflation in the parenthesis of the text. The value of money increases because the same sum buys more goods as prices fall. The sentence meets the definition.
